stories.title: Atiq Ahmed's family shattered in three years:He was killed, one son shot dead in encounter, another died in crash; two sons in jail, wife absconding
stories.summary: On April 13, 2023, Atiq Ahmed's son, Asad Ahmed, was killed in a police encounter. Two days later, Atiq Ahmed and his brother Ashraf were shot dead by three boys. Now, about two and a half years later, Atiq's youngest son, Aban, has died in a road accident. Atiq's two sons are in jail. His wife, Shaista Parveen, and Ashraf's wife, Zainab, are listed as wanted and are absconding in police records. Only one son is out, and now he will perform his brother's last rites. At one time, Atiq Ahmed's children held significant sway. They had special vehicles, and wherever they went, more than 20 people accompanied them for security. Gradually, their economic empire collapsed, and then the entire family scattered. Aban set out to meet Ali, died in an accident Atiq Ahmed's ancestral home was in Chakia, Prayagraj. It is about 4 kilometres away from Prayagraj Junction. After the Umesh Pal murder case, the house in Chakia was demolished. Now, only ruins remain there in Atiq's name. Atiq's fourth son, Ahjam, and fifth son, Aban, lived at their aunt Parveen Qureshi's house in Hatwa village, about 2 kilometres away from Chakia. On the morning of August 6, Aban was going with four other companions to meet his brother Ali Ahmed, who is imprisoned in Jhansi jail. The accident happened in Jhansi itself, and he died. Three years ago from today, everyone used to live in Chakia. They used to go to school from there. Atiq had admitted all his children to St. Joseph's, the city's top school. A Pajero car was bought for them to go to school. At school, the eldest son, Umar Ahmed, had the softest nature. He was also interested in studies, saying that he wanted to become an IAS, so he had to study. But when he completed his studies, following in his father's footsteps, he got involved in extortion and recovery work. He is currently imprisoned in Lucknow jail in this case. Aban was not interested in studies, but in cricket Aban, who died in a road accident, was average in studies but excelled in sports. Aban was a good cricket player. He was often seen playing cricket with the boys nearby. Because of this, his mother, Shaista Parveen, had beaten him many times. Even during their studies at St. Joseph's School, when these children misbehaved, instead of calling Principal Atiq Ahmed, they would call Shaista Parveen. Once, Shaista Parveen reached the school and scolded her children severely. The fourth and fifth sons were most afraid of Shaista Parveen. Wherever the five sons went, 20 people would be in their security. By 2022, three of Atiq's sons had completed their schooling. The eldest son, Umar, went to Uttarakhand to study law. The second and third sons got involved in politics and their father's businesses. The remaining two children continued their studies. Whenever there was an event at the house of one of Atiq's close associates in areas like Chakia, Kareli, Dhoomanganj, all five children would go together. But they didn't sit together in one car; there would be 4 separate cars. About 20 people would accompany them, 5-7 of whom would be armed. Atiq himself had instructed that none of his sons should face any trouble. The fourth son, Ali, followed in his father's footsteps. That's why people called him 'Chhote Sansad Ji' (Junior MP). He spoke openly in election rallies. Asad, on the other hand, had an arrogant temperament. He often stayed with his uncle Ashraf and engaged in fights. Shaista Parveen didn't like all this, but Atiq often remained silent on these matters. His silent consent created a craze in Asad to become a don, and that became the reason for the destruction of the entire family. Umesh Pal was murdered and then the countdown began. February 24, 2023, this day became the biggest reason for the end of Atiq Ahmed's family. Umesh Pal was the main witness in the murder case of MLA Raju Pal, which happened in 2005. He was supposed to testify, but Atiq's family did not approve of this. Even after several threats, when he didn't back down, a plan was made to murder him. Atiq Ahmed's son, Asad, was also involved in this plan and he opened fire indiscriminately outside Umesh Pal's house on February 24. In this firing, Umesh Pal along with his two bodyguards also died. CCTV footage of the incident surfaced. Asad was seen firing a gun. Police initiated swift action. On February 27, a shooter named Arbaaz was killed in an encounter. From March 1 to 3, the houses of Atiq and his associates were demolished. About a month and a half after the incident, on April 13, UP STF received input that Asad Ahmed and Ghulam were in Jhansi. When the STF started the encirclement, both opened fire. Both died in retaliatory firing. For the first time, Atiq Ahmed was seen crying On April 13, Atiq Ahmed was in the Prayagraj court with his brother Ashraf. Both had handcuffs on their hands. As soon as he learned about his son's encounter, he broke down in tears. The media tried to talk to him, but he said nothing. On April 15, the police took Atiq Ahmed and Ashraf to Kasari-Masari, from where some weapons were recovered. After this, at around 10:30 PM, both were brought to Colvin Hospital for a medical examination. At the same time, three boys, Lavlesh Tiwari, Sunny Singh, and Arun Maurya, opened rapid fire on Atiq and Ashraf with a Zigana pistol. 20 seconds later, both the strongman brothers, who once ruled Prayagraj, lay dead face down on the ground. Considering the seriousness of the incident, the police deployed security forces in every corner of the city. The entire situation remained under control. Shaista Parveen did not attend her husband's funeral even after her son's When Asad's funeral took place on April 15, it was hoped that Shaista Parveen would definitely come to see her son one last time, but she did not. Then, when Atiq and his brother Ashraf were buried in Kasari-Masari cemetery on April 16, there was talk that Shaista had come. However, this was just a rumour. She did not attend her husband's funeral either. Police have named Shaista as an accused in the Umesh Pal murder case, and there is a reward of 50 thousand rupees on her. Shaista loved her youngest son Aban the most. But the situation seen over the last two and a half years suggests that she will not even attend her son's funeral. At Aban's funeral, only his brother Ahjam will be present among blood relatives. The rest will be some of his relatives. Elder son Umar is imprisoned in Lucknow and the younger Ali in Jhansi jail. Neither of them has been taken to the scene of any death before. Police consider this a security matter.

stories.title: Liquor bound for Bihar seized with fake QR codes:1,370 bottles recovered in Lucknow; smuggler arrested
stories.summary: A joint team of the Excise Department and police has uncovered an illegal liquor business in the PGI area of Lucknow. Raiding a house in Sector-10 of Vrindavan Yojana, 1,370 bottles of suspicious English liquor were recovered. In the preliminary investigation, the QR codes, brand labels, and caps on the bottles were found to be fake. Police have arrested one accused from the spot, while a search is on for the network involved in supplying the liquor and preparing fake labels. Acting on a tip-off from an informant, the team detained Anil Verma, a resident of Azadnagar, Krishnanagar. During interrogation, he revealed that the liquor was supplied through Vimal Yadav, a resident of Azamgarh. The accused also confessed that by affixing fake QR codes, brand labels, and caps, the liquor was passed off as genuine and sent to Bihar to earn higher profits. During the raid, 612 bottles of 8 PM Premium Black Superior Whisky (180 ml) and 758 bottles of After Dark Blue Rare Grain Whisky (180 ml), totalling 1,370 bottles (approximately 246.60 bulk litres), were recovered. No data was found upon scanning the QR code with the Excise Department's mobile app. Subsequently, the investigation revealed that the QR codes, brand labels, and caps on the bottles were forged, confirming the liquor to be counterfeit. The police and the Excise Department are now engaged in investigating the entire network associated with this illegal business.

stories.title: CNG leak triggers panic in Varanasi:Major mishap averted 1 km before airport
stories.summary: A vehicle carrying CNG cylinders suddenly started to leak gas on the Babatpur four-lane road in Varanasi's Badagaon police station area on Thursday morning. The incident occurred about 1 km from the Varanasi Airport, spreading panic in the area. The driver, showing presence of mind, immediately parked the vehicle on the roadside and informed the CNG company and the fire brigade. The fire brigade and the company's technical team, who arrived at the scene, stopped the gas leak by replacing the faulty valve. No casualties were reported during this incident. Gas leak started at 12:40 AM The vehicle, loaded with CNG cylinders, was on its way for supply. On Thursday, around 12:40 AM, gas suddenly started leaking from a cylinder valve. Fire brigade took charge As soon as the information was received, the Pindra Fire Station team reached the spot. As a precautionary measure, people present nearby were moved to a safe distance. Firefighters also sprayed water to prevent any untoward incident. Gas leak stopped as soon as the valve was changed After some time, the technical team of the CNG company also reached the spot. Investigation revealed that the gas leak was due to a faulty valve in the cylinder. Employees replaced the faulty valve and nozzle, after which the gas leak completely stopped. Such incidents have happened before Local residents said that similar gas leak incidents have occurred three to four times on this route in the last six months. Each time, a technical fault in the valve or nozzle has been identified. Fire department officials stated that the situation was brought under control in time. There are no reports of any casualties or damage in this incident.

stories.title: Gonda sees Brij Bhushan show of strength:200-vehicle convoy, ‘Sher Aaya’ slogans echo; MLA son waves mace
stories.summary: Former BJP MP and ex-Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh reached Ayodhya on Thursday for the first time after being acquitted in the sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers. He put up a massive show of strength as thousands of supporters welcomed him before he left for Gonda to lead a rally named 'Satyamev Jayate'. His flight landed at Maharishi Valmiki International Airport around 11 am. More than 2,000 supporters welcomed him with drums, flower garlands and slogans of 'Sher aaya... Sher aaya' (The lion has arrived). Brij Bhushan boarded an open Hunter vehicle after leaving the airport. His convoy initially had more than 1,000 vehicles and continued to grow as it travelled towards Gonda. Offers prayers at Hanumangarhi, son celebrates verdict by waving mace The convoy first reached Hanumangarhi Temple in Ayodhya. Since the temple was observing its bhog and aarti rituals, Brij Bhushan offered prayers from outside instead of entering the shrine. He then met saints and sought their blessings. Only around 20-22 vehicles entered the temple premises, while the remaining convoy halted near Lata Mangeshkar Chowk before joining the procession again. Outside the temple, Brij Bhushan's elder son and Gonda Sadar MLA Prateek Bhushan Singh celebrated the court verdict by waving a mace from the sunroof of the vehicle. "Our leader has finally returned home. People always believed we would win. From the first day itself, everyone knew truth would prevail. It took time, but this victory feels special," Prateek said. Supporters continued showering Brij Bhushan with rose petals as slogans echoed across the temple complex. See 3 pictures of Brijbhushan's show of strength - Convoy doubles in size on way to Gonda After offering prayers, Brij Bhushan's convoy left Ayodhya for Nandini Nagar in Gonda, where the 'Satyamev Jayate' rally was scheduled. As the procession crossed into Gonda district through Katra Shivdayalganj in Nawabganj, the convoy grew from more than 1,000 vehicles to nearly 2,000, according to organisers. More than 500 Sanskrit students from Ayodhya carrying flower petals also reached Nandini Nagar to welcome Brij Bhushan. Around 200 Batuks had been invited to participate in the programme. Priests welcome him at Nandini Gaumata Temple At Nandini Gaumata Temple in Nandini Nagar, priests welcomed Brij Bhushan with flower garlands. He performed a parikrama of the temple along with priests before proceeding to the Satyamev Jayate stage. He also sought blessings from saints who had travelled from Ayodhya. His family organised an Akhand Ramayan recital at the temple. A havan was performed after the recital concluded. Brij Bhushan later addressed supporters at the rally venue. Organisers arranged food for nearly two lakh people attending the event. Around 40 quintals of laddoos were also distributed among supporters. Acquitted in sexual harassment case on August 3 On August 3, Delhi's Rouse Avenue Court acquitted Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in the sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers. Reacting to the verdict, Brij Bhushan said, "I had said earlier that if even one allegation against me was proved, I would hang myself. Hoihi soi jo Ram rachi rakha." However, wrestlers Vinesh Phogat and Bajrang Punia said they had not lost hope and would challenge the verdict before the High Court. Wrestlers say they will challenge verdict Vinesh Phogat said it had taken tremendous courage to get an FIR registered against a powerful leader of the ruling party. "He used his influence to pressure several girls into withdrawing their names, but many women wrestlers stood firm and fought the case in court. We are disappointed that the court did not hold him guilty. Our lawyers have been instructed to challenge the verdict. The fight will continue," she said. Bajrang Punia questioned the verdict and alleged that Brij Bhushan had all the power on his side. "Today's verdict makes it clear that he had all the power. Witnesses were influenced. We do not understand on what basis he has been acquitted," he said. Veteran wrestling coach Mahavir Phogat, however, said the court's decision must be respected. "Every wrestler fought their battle, but the final decision had to be taken by the court. There is no authority above the court in this country," he said. Sexual harassment case dates back to January 2023 The controversy first surfaced in January 2023 when Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik and several other wrestlers staged a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, demanding action against Brij Bhushan, who was then the president of the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI). The wrestlers alleged that six women wrestlers, including a minor, had accused him of sexual harassment. Despite the allegations, no FIR was initially registered. Following the Supreme Court's intervention, Delhi Police registered FIRs in April 2023. The minor wrestler later withdrew her complaint. 127 hearings held over 1,133 days After arguments from both sides concluded on July 2, 2026, the court reserved its verdict. The trial lasted 1,133 days, during which the court conducted 127 hearings and recorded statements of 32 witnesses. Brij Bhushan had been out on regular bail since July 20, 2023. On May 10, 2024, the court framed charges against him based on the Delhi Police chargesheet, after which the trial formally began. Timeline of the wrestlers' protest First protest: January 2023 On January 18, 2023, Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik, Bajrang Punia and several other wrestlers began a sit-in at Jantar Mantar, accusing Brij Bhushan of sexual harassment. On January 20, they submitted a formal complaint to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), which constituted an inquiry committee headed by Mary Kom. Following a meeting with Sports Minister Anurag Thakur on January 21, the government assured the wrestlers that an investigation would be conducted. The first phase of the protest ended, while the Sports Ministry suspended WFI's activities. Second protest: April to June 2023 The wrestlers returned to Jantar Mantar on April 23, 2023, alleging that the inquiry report had not been made public and no action had been taken. On April 24, they approached the Supreme Court seeking registration of an FIR. Following the Supreme Court's intervention, Delhi Police registered two FIRs against Brij Bhushan on April 28. On May 28, the wrestlers attempted to march towards the newly inaugurated Parliament building. Delhi Police stopped them through barricading, detained the protesters and cleared the protest site at Jantar Mantar. Two days later, on May 30, several wrestlers reached Haridwar intending to immerse their medals in the Ganga in protest. However, farmer leader Naresh Tikait persuaded them to postpone the decision. On June 7, after nearly six hours of discussions with Sports Minister Anurag Thakur, the wrestlers announced that they were suspending their protest. Supporters hail acquittal as 'victory of truth' Throughout the roadshow from Ayodhya to Gonda, supporters celebrated Brij Bhushan's acquittal by showering him with flowers and raising slogans. Many supporters described the verdict as a victory of truth and gathered in large numbers along the route to welcome him. The roadshow was organised under the banner of 'Satyamev Jayate', with organisers projecting it as a public thanksgiving after the court verdict. See pictures of preparations to welcome Brijbhushan in Gonda Massive arrangements made in Gonda Extensive preparations were made for Brij Bhushan's arrival in Gonda. Apart from the Akhand Ramayan recital and havan at Nandini Gaumata Temple, organisers made arrangements to serve food to nearly two lakh people attending the event. Around 40 quintals of laddoos were also distributed among supporters. More than 500 Sanskrit students from Ayodhya welcomed him with flower petals, while around 200 Batuks were invited to participate in the programme. Convoy grows as supporters join en route The convoy accompanying Brij Bhushan kept growing as it travelled from Ayodhya towards Gonda. It started with more than 1,000 vehicles after he left Ayodhya airport and swelled to nearly 2,000 vehicles by the time it crossed into Gonda district through Katra Shivdayalganj in Nawabganj. Supporters lined the route at several places to greet him with garlands and flower showers. Case remained in spotlight for over three years The sexual harassment case remained one of the country's biggest sports controversies for more than three years. The allegations first surfaced in January 2023, leading to nationwide protests by top wrestlers, intervention by the Supreme Court, multiple FIRs, and a lengthy criminal trial. The court heard the matter over 127 hearings spread across 1,133 days before acquitting Brij Bhushan on August 3, 2026. The verdict has now triggered contrasting reactions, with Brij Bhushan and his supporters celebrating the acquittal, while Vinesh Phogat and Bajrang Punia have announced that they will challenge the judgment before the High Court.

stories.title: Atiq Ahmed's youngest son dies in UP road accident:Was on way to meet jailed elder brother in Jhansi jail when vehicle hit divider
stories.summary: Atiq Ahmed's youngest son, Aban Ahmed (21), died in a road accident this morning (6 Aug) while travelling from Prayagraj to Jhansi to meet his elder brother Ali, who is lodged in Jhansi Jail. Four of his friends were travelling with him in a Creta SUV. Crash leaves two dead, three injured The accident occurred around 10.30 am in the Poonch police station area, nearly 70 km before Jhansi. The speeding SUV rammed into a road divider with such force that its front portion was completely mangled. All five occupants were trapped inside the vehicle. Police and passersby broke open the doors to rescue the victims. Aban, who was seated in the front passenger seat, and the driver, Sonu, died at the scene. The three injured occupants, Umar Ahmed, Mohammad Zaid and Aslam, were shifted to the district hospital for treatment. Conflicting accounts on cause of accident Two versions have emerged regarding the cause of the crash. One of the injured occupants told police that the vehicle lost control after hitting bricks lying on the highway. However police said, “The SUV was travelling at high speed and the driver lost control while trying to avoid an animal that suddenly came onto the road.” Atiq Ahmed's family Atiq Ahmed had five sons, with Aban being the youngest. His son Asad was killed in a police encounter in Jhansi in 2023. Of his surviving sons, Umar is lodged in Lucknow Jail, Ali is imprisoned in Jhansi Jail, while Ahzam, who is older than Aban, is currently pursuing graduation. Family remains under legal scrutiny The family has remained in the spotlight since the murder of lawyer Umesh Pal in February 2023. During the investigation, Atiq Ahmed and his brother Ashraf were brought to Prayagraj for a court hearing from separate jails and were shot dead in police custody on April 15, 2023. Atiq's wife, Shaista Parveen, remains absconding, with a reward of ₹1 lakh announced for information leading to her arrest. See photos from the accident scene Car's front portion mangled in the crash, see photos Aban suffered fatal head injuries in high-speed crash Police said, “Atiq Ahmed's youngest son, Aban Ahmed, left Prayagraj early morning for Jhansi, nearly 400 km away, to meet his brother lodged in jail. He was seated in the front passenger seat, while Zaid was driving the SUV.” SUV crashes into divider at high speed According to Jhansi Police sources, “The highway was wet due to light rain and the vehicle was reportedly travelling at nearly 100 kmph. The driver allegedly lost control, and the SUV slammed into the divider at full speed, completely crushing its front portion.” Severe impact proved fatal The collision left Aban with critical head injuries and multiple fractures to his arms and legs. He died on the spot. Police broke open the vehicle's doors to rescue all five occupants trapped inside the wreckage. Body sent for post-mortem Aban's body has been kept at the post-mortem house of Jhansi Medical College. After the post-mortem examination, the body will be handed over to his family. He is expected to be buried in Prayagraj on Friday near the grave of his father, Atiq Ahmed. Eyewitness says SUV was speeding before crash An eyewitness named Deepak Yadav claimed, “The SUV was travelling at a very high speed before crashing into the divider, with debris from the impact scattered across the highway.” He stated, “I was on my way to the farm when I saw the accident. The driver first swerved left to avoid a calf crossing the highway. Moments later, he allegedly turned the vehicle sharply again to avoid a motorcyclist, after which the SUV crashed into the divider.” Car parts scattered across 40 feet Deepak said, “The vehicle was travelling at over 120 kmph. The impact was so severe that pieces of the SUV were scattered across nearly 40 feet of the highway.” Locals rescued victims before police arrived Deepak said, “I was the first to reach the spot after hearing the crash. When the car doors could not be opened, I called the police and fetched an iron rod from a nearby house to force the doors open.” He said, “Aban was pulled out first and had blood in his mouth. When asked his name, he identified himself as Aban. The remaining occupants, including Sonu, were then rescued from the vehicle.” Police reached within 10 minutes According to the eyewitness, police arrived at the scene within about 10 minutes of being informed and shifted all the injured occupants to the hospital for treatment.

stories.title: Bus knocks down man in Gorakhpur:Dies after hand gets crushed under tyre; driver flees
stories.summary: A young man died in Gorakhpur on Thursday morning around 5:30 AM after being hit by a speeding roadways bus. After the accident, the driver fled the scene with the bus. The youth has not yet been identified. The police have sent the body for post-mortem and are working to identify him. The accident occurred at Shastri Chowk. In the accident, the bus wheel ran over the youth's hand, severely damaging it and his mobile phone. Police are scanning CCTV footage from nearby to identify the bus and the driver. Youth was walking along the roadside According to information, the youth was walking along the roadside near Shastri Chowk. During this, a speeding roadways bus from Gorakhpur depot hit him. As soon as he was hit, the youth fell on the road. The bus wheel ran over his hand, damaging his hand and the mobile phone he had with him. He died on the spot. After the accident, the bus driver fled the scene with the vehicle. Passersby informed the police about the incident. The Kotwali police reached the spot, took possession of the body, and sent it for post-mortem. Police Scrutinising CCTV Footage The deceased has not yet been identified. Police are trying to identify him. Additionally, footage from CCTV cameras installed at Shastri Chowk and nearby areas is being scrutinised to identify the bus involved in the accident. Traffic Affected for Some Time After the accident, traffic at Shastri Chowk was affected for some time. Residents demanded regular deployment of traffic police at the spot and control over-speeding vehicles. Police stated that a case would be registered upon receiving a complaint, and further action would be taken.

stories.title: Mayawati gets emotional at sole BSP MLA's funeral:Says Umashankar Singh never betrayed her, promises to groom his son in politics
stories.summary: BSP MLA Umashankar Singh from Ballia's Rasra Assembly seat passed away on Wednesday evening. His body reached Lucknow on Thursday morning at 9 am. BSP supremo Mayawati paid her last respects to the MLA's mortal remains. Appearing emotional, Mayawati offered flowers and paid tributes to Umashankar. Mayawati considered MLA Umashankar as her younger brother. Last year on 9 August, on Raksha Bandhan, she had tied a rakhi to him. Mayawati spoke to Umashankar's Yukesh. She said, “Don't lose courage. The BSP family is with you. We have to move forward.” The MLA's last rites will be performed on Thursday in Rasra at his ancestral village. Umashankar Singh breathed his last at Fortis Hospital in Delhi. 55-year-old Umashankar had been battling brain cancer for a long time. He had also undergone treatment in America, but the cancer had reached the fourth stage. Umashankar was a three- time MLA from the Rasra seat. In Umashankar's family, there is wife Pushpa Singh, daughter Yamini, and son Prince Yukesh. The MLA had performed Yamini's wedding in 2019 and Yukesh's in 2024. Minister of State Independent Charge Dinesh Pratap Singh's niece Kanika Singh is Yukesh's wife. BSP chief Mayawati had also attended this wedding. Pushpa Singh is the Managing Director of her husband's company 'C.S. Infraconstruction Limited' and Yukesh is the Chief Executive Officer (CEO). After Umashankar's demise, Prince Yukesh is being considered the heir to his political legacy. However, Yukesh has never been seen in active politics. Last connected to the Assembly online on February 24 The BSP MLA had last joined the Assembly session online on February 24, 2025, due to health reasons. During the proceedings, Assembly Speaker Satish Mahana not only permitted Umashankar Singh to join virtually and speak, but also wished him a speedy recovery on behalf of the entire House. The BSP MLA had expressed gratitude by thanking the Assembly Speaker. Joined BSP in 2011, has been continuously an MLA since then Umashankar Singh's father Ghurhu Singh had retired from the Indian Army. Umashankar completed his education in Ballia and became active in politics from his student life itself. He started his political journey by winning the student union election at Satish Chandra College in Ballia. Before entering politics, he used to work as a contractor. After winning the district panchayat election, he stepped into active politics. In 2012, he became an MLA from Rasra for the first time. In that election, BSP's seats had reduced from 206 to 80, but Umashankar Singh defeated SP's Sanatan Pandey by about 52,000 votes, securing more than 84,000 votes. After that, he continued to register victories in 2017 and 2022 as well. In the 2022 assembly elections, BSP got only one seat, and that seat was won by Umashankar Singh. Three consecutive victories proved his strong political hold in the region. Was a major face of BSP in Purvanchal Umashankar Singh came into the limelight in 2012 by organising a mass marriage of 251 girls and in 2016 by organising a mass marriage of 351 Hindu-Muslim couples. He was considered a major face of BSP in Purvanchal. He had a distinct identity in the region due to development works and public service. In February 2026, when he was undergoing cancer treatment, the Income Tax Department had also raided several of his locations. Was declared disqualified in 2017 On January 14, 2017, the then Governor Ram Naik had disqualified him. He was accused of violating the Representation of the People Act. The case was related to taking government contracts in his own name. The allegations were found to be true in the Lokayukta investigation. His membership was cancelled after the Election Commission's recommendation following the High Court's directive. This was the first case in the state where a legislator's membership was terminated with retrospective effect. Later, Umashankar Singh challenged this decision in the Supreme Court, where the verdict came in his favour. Had assets worth ₹54 crores, debt of ₹13 crores According to the 2022 election affidavit, Umashankar Singh's total assets were approximately ₹54.05 crore. This included movable assets worth ₹18.05 crore rupees and immovable assets worth ₹35.99 crore. He also had a debt of approximately ₹13 crore. Umashankar Singh was active in the business world along with politics. His company named 'Chhatra Shakti Constructions' was engaged in road construction work. It had completed several road projects. His company also worked in the mining sector. Apart from construction and mining, he was also associated with education and hotel business.

stories.title: Attachment notice served at Rajpal Yadav's Shahjahanpur house:Property to be auctioned if ₹16 crore loan isn't repaid in 34 days
stories.summary: Bollywood actor Rajpal Yadav's troubles are increasing. The Central Bank of India has pasted an attachment notice of ₹16.61 crore on his ancestral house in Shahjahanpur. The bank has warned that if the loan is not repaid within 34 days, the property will be auctioned. The auction date has been set for 9 September. Rajpal Yadav had taken a loan of Rs 16.61 crore from the Mumbai branch of Central Bank in the names of his wife Radha Yadav and mother Godavari. Twenty-seven days ago, the Delhi High Court had sentenced Rajpal Yadav to three months in jail in a cheque bounce case. However, he is currently out of jail. His elder brother Shripal Yadav said: “This is an old matter. Talks are underway with the bank regarding loan repayment. The matter will be resolved soon. Currently, there is no situation like property auction.” Notice was also posted 2 years ago Central Bank manager Anuj Verma said, “A notice has been put up on the building located in Kundra, the ancestral village of Shahjahanpur. The bank had also pasted a notice in this matter about two years ago. At that time, an agreement was reached between Rajpal Yadav and the bank regarding loan repayment.” Jailed 27 days ago in a check bounce case

stories.title: Constable says he strangled 10-year old after she screamed:Cop left home with a knife in Gorakhpur, had served as BJP MLA’s gunner
stories.summary: The constable accused of raping and murdering a 10-year-old girl in Gorakhpur had allegedly left the police line carrying a knife and had already planned to target a girl that day, according to information he later gave police during questioning. Investigators say he admitted to harbouring deep hatred towards women and girls and claimed he took pleasure in seeing them suffer. Police said the accused allegedly raped the girl at a crematorium before strangling her to death. He then allegedly disfigured her face with a knife, tied her hands behind her back using the string from her lower garment and threw her body from Chiutaha Bridge. The details emerged during the remand of constable Abhishek Yadav, who had previously served as a gunman for a BJP MLA in Gorakhpur. 6:45 hours of interrogation on police remand From Gorakhpur District Hospital, on the night of July 28, the constable had abducted, raped, and murdered a 10-year-old girl. On August 4 (Tuesday), constable Abhishek Yadav, who was in jail, was taken on 10-hour custody remand. Around 6 AM, the police, amidst tight security, brought the constable out of the district jail. First, he was interrogated for about 6:45 hours. Constable said - The girl screamed, so I strangled her to death Constable Abhishek Yadav told the police that when the girl screamed, I was afraid that people from the neighborhood might come. For this reason, I strangled her to death. Then, to hide her identity and destroy evidence, I mutilated the body and threw it into the Rohini river. Scene Recreation Started from District Hospital After this, the constable was taken to the crime scene for scene recreation. The police took him to all the places he had visited on the night of the incident. The police first took the constable to the district hospital, from where he had taken the girl on a bike. After this, the team reached the cremation ground and Chiutaha bridge via the same route. The police also took him to the spot where the girl's body was found about 500 meters away and interrogated him. Based on the constable's identification, the police also recovered the knife used in the murder from the bushes near the crime scene. The police have sent the knife for forensic examination. The information obtained during the remand will be matched with CCTV footage, mobile location, forensic reports, and witness statements. Government Quarter Also Sealed During the remand, the police also took the constable to his government quarter located in the police line. After inspecting the room, it was sealed. Some items and other evidence have been collected from there, which will be included in the investigation. Constable's Wife and Family Disowned Him Constable Abhishek Yadav's family includes his wife, a 13-year-old daughter, and a 7-year-old son. For about a year, his wife has been living with the children at her parents' house. The constable's parents and relatives are also ashamed of his actions. Since this incident, the family and relatives have distanced themselves from him. So far, no one has gone to jail to meet the constable. He has been kept in a high-security barrack in jail under CCTV camera surveillance. Girl's Body Found After 36 Hours July 28: The girl was abducted, raped, and murdered. July 29: An FIR was registered at Kotwali police station. July 30: About 36 hours later, the body was found under the Chiutaha bridge. August 5: Police filed a charge sheet in court. Police officers say that the case will be pursued at a fast-track level with strong advocacy, so that the accused can be punished soon. The girl wanted to become a doctor The 10-year-old girl wanted to become a doctor. She studied in the 5th grade at a government school in the Betiahata area. On July 28, the day of the incident, the girl went to school in the morning as usual. She didn't know it was her last morning. She returned home from school. She took off her dress and hung it on the veranda. She put on a lower and t-shirt and started playing. In the evening, her elder sister was admitted to the district hospital due to chest pain. Her father and aunt were with the admitted child. Meanwhile, at home, the 10-year-old girl cooked food. Then, at night, she took her 7-year-old younger sister to the district hospital to deliver food. The father said - the girl had gone out to get water at the hospital. Just then, the constable lured her onto his bike on the pretext of dropping her home. After that, the girl was gone forever. Mother named her son after the girl The girl's last rites were performed at Rajghat at 6 PM on July 30. After this, the girl's mother gave birth to a son the same night. The mother named the son, born after 5 daughters, after her deceased daughter. Relatives said that the girl always demanded a brother from her mother. When the brother arrived, the constable had already snatched the laughing and playing girl from her family. The constable has been a gunman for a BJP MLA In Gorakhpur, the 10-year-old girl, victim of the brutality of constable Abhishek Yadav (35), is no longer in this world. Dainik Bhaskar's team reached her home on Friday (July 31). Here, her younger sisters, aged 5 and 7, were playing with her school bag.

stories.title: Rain lashes 10 UP cities, alert in all 75 districts:40 Farrukhabad schools flooded, DM reaches by boat; crocodile spotted in Lakhimpur
stories.summary: Monsoon rains continue across Uttar Pradesh, with showers reported in 10 cities, including Lucknow and Saharanpur, since Thursday morning. Schools up to Class 8 have been closed in Prayagraj due to heavy rain, while overcast conditions prevail in more than 35 cities. The weather department has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts, including a heavy rainfall warning for 39 districts. Meanwhile, rivers remain in spate following continuous rainfall. In Farrukhabad, the Ganga is nearing the danger mark, with floodwaters entering 33 villages and 40 government schools. Water is flowing over highways. District Magistrate Ankur Lather reached affected villages by boat to assess the flood situation and interact with residents. In Ballia, three more houses were washed away by the Saryu River, taking the total number of houses lost in the past week to 27. In Lakhimpur, a crocodile was seen roaming on a road, while a venomous Russell’s viper entered a house. The forest department rescued the snake and released it into the forest. In Varanasi, the swollen Ganga has inundated 40 to 50 small temples, while the Ratneshwar Mahadev Temple is more than half submerged. Rain was recorded in 72 districts over the past 24 hours, with Banda receiving the highest rainfall at 69.3 mm. Uttar Pradesh has recorded 25% below-normal rainfall since June 1. Rain-related incidents over the past 48 hours have claimed nine lives, including six killed in a house collapse in Pratapgarh, two who drowned in a pit in Mirzapur, and one youth killed in a lightning strike. Weather scientist Atul Kumar Singh from Lucknow said: "The monsoon system has now become active over Uttar Pradesh. It is passing through Delhi, Lucknow and Patna, leading to the formation of multiple cyclonic circulations. Monsoon winds have reached the Gangetic plains, and their impact will bring widespread heavy rainfall across the state over the next four to five days." Updates from cities: Gorakhpur: Sunny spells after overnight rain Heavy rain lashed Gorakhpur late on Wednesday night. Thursday morning remained pleasant with intermittent sunshine, cloudy skies and cool winds, bringing relief from heat and humidity. Weather scientist Kailash Pandey said moderate rainfall is likely until evening. He added that weather conditions are expected to return to normal from Friday, with only intermittent light showers and no possibility of heavy rainfall. Meerut: Intermittent rain since late night Meerut has been witnessing intermittent rainfall since late Wednesday night, making the weather pleasant. The weather department said similar conditions are expected to continue over the next 48 hours, with the maximum temperature likely to remain around 28°C on Thursday. Agra: Heavy rain likely today Cloudy skies have prevailed in Agra since morning. The weather department has issued a heavy rainfall alert for the day and said similar conditions are likely to continue until August 11. On Wednesday, the city recorded a maximum temperature of 31°C and a minimum of 27.1°C. Kanpur: Cloudy weather, temperature at 27°C Dense clouds covered the sky in Kanpur on Thursday morning following overnight rain, bringing cooler conditions. The weather department has issued a heavy rainfall alert for the next 48 hours. The morning temperature was around 27°C. Prayagraj: Schools shut up to Class 8 All schools from Classes 1 to 8 in Prayagraj have been closed due to heavy rainfall. The Basic Education Officer appealed to parents to keep children indoors and avoid unnecessary travel. Teachers and school staff have also been advised to exercise caution. Farrukhabad DM visits flood-hit villages District Magistrate Ankur Lather visited flood-affected villages by boat and reviewed the situation with residents. Ballia: Three more houses swept away Three more houses were washed away by the Saryu River in Ballia, taking the total number of houses lost in the past week to 27. Varanasi: Ganga inundates temples The Ganga is in spate in Varanasi, with floodwaters entering 40 to 50 small temples. The Ratneshwar Mahadev Temple is now more than half submerged. Rain was recorded in 72 districts over the past 24 hours, with Banda receiving the highest rainfall of 69.3 mm. The state remains 25% below normal rainfall since June 1. Farrukhabad: Floodwater enters 33 villages Floodwater has entered 33 villages and 40 government schools in Farrukhabad as the Ganga nears the danger mark. Water is flowing over highways, with boats now being used on submerged roads. Lucknow: Rain since night, 51 mm in three days Continuous rainfall has been recorded in Lucknow since late Wednesday night. Light showers continued early Thursday under cloudy skies. The weather department has issued an orange alert for heavy rainfall. The city received 7.5 mm of rain on Wednesday, 14% above normal, taking the total rainfall over the past three days to around 51 mm. Saharanpur: Rain continues since late night Light rain has continued in Saharanpur since late Wednesday night. The weather department said the maximum temperature is expected to reach 28°C and the minimum 25°C. Weather fluctuations are likely to continue until August 12. Rivers above danger mark in 18 districts The impact of continuous rainfall in the hills is now visible across Uttar Pradesh. Rivers are flowing above the danger mark in 18 districts, prompting the administration to issue advisories asking people to stay away from riverbanks. The affected districts are Ayodhya, Azamgarh, Bahraich, Ballia, Balrampur, Barabanki, Basti, Deoria, Farrukhabad, Gonda, Gorakhpur, Kasganj, Maharajganj, Mau, Sant Kabir Nagar, Shravasti, Siddharthnagar and Sitapur. Authorities have stepped up monitoring in these districts and urged residents to remain alert. Below-normal monsoon likely this year India Meteorological Department Director General Dr M. Mohapatra said La Niña-like conditions in the Pacific Ocean are fading and signs of El Niño are emerging, which could result in below-normal rainfall this year. He added that reduced snow cover across the Northern Hemisphere during January-March may also affect the southwest monsoon. Monsoon arrival over the past decade A graphical comparison of monsoon onset in Uttar Pradesh over the last 10 years was also released.

stories.title: 6 family members die as century-old house collapses:Parents, son, daughter-in-law, 2 children killed in rain-triggered tragedy
stories.summary: Continuous rain caused a 100-year-old house to collapse in Uttar Pradesh's Pratapgarh late on Wednesday night, killing six members of a family. The victims included the parents, their son, elder daughter-in-law and her two children. Only one son survived the tragedy. The weather was hot and humid on Wednesday night, so all seven family members were sleeping in an air-conditioned room. At around 2 am, the roof suddenly caved in, leaving them no time to react or even cry out for help. All were buried under several feet of debris. One son, who was sleeping near the edge of the room, managed to crawl out of the rubble. Hearing the loud crash, neighbours rushed to the spot and alerted the police and fire department. A two-hour rescue operation was carried out before all seven family members were pulled from the debris and taken to hospital, where doctors declared six of them dead. The incident took place in Mahuli locality under Nagar Kotwali police station limits. According to police, those killed were homeowner Pramod Srivastava (60), his wife Rita (55), younger son Nitin (25), elder daughter-in-law Madhuri (23), and Madhuri's two sons Madhav (2) and Advik (10 months). Pramod's elder son Aman (28), the lone survivor, is undergoing treatment at the district hospital. 'When my eyes opened, everyone was buried under the debris, I screamed loudly' Pramod Srivastava was the elder of two brothers. His younger brother, Pawan, lives separately and runs a tea stall in the Pratapgarh court complex. Pramod earned a living by driving a rickshaw, while his wife was a homemaker. The two brothers had recently sold their ancestral land for around Rs 75 lakh. Pramod's 1,300 sq ft ancestral house had two rooms, a kitchen, toilet and bathroom, with a boundary wall around it. Three years ago, walls for the first floor had been built, but financial constraints prevented the family from laying the roof slab. They were preparing to complete the construction. Younger son Nitin was unmarried. The following family members died in the accident- Victims in the tragedy 'When I opened my eyes, everyone was buried under the rubble' Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, survivor Aman Srivastava said the family had dinner and gone to bed around 10.30 pm. He, his wife, two sons, parents and younger brother were all sleeping in the same room. "Between 1.30 am and 2 am, I heard a loud noise. When I opened my eyes, the room had turned into a pile of rubble. My body was buried under mud. I somehow managed to crawl out and saw my entire family trapped beneath the debris." "I tried to rescue everyone by myself, but the rubble was too heavy. I couldn't do anything. I screamed for help, calling villagers and relatives. People rushed to the spot, after which the police and fire department began the rescue operation. Police broke a window using iron rods to enter the house and pulled out my family members one by one." Rescue operation More than 30 police personnel reached the spot soon after the incident. As it was dark, rescue work began under torchlight. Police broke open a window with iron rods to gain entry into the collapsed house. The rescue operation lasted nearly two hours, with police and emergency teams pulling the trapped family members out of the debris one by one. The story is being updated.

stories.title: India’s costliest expressway sinks at 84 locations:Gadkari called it ‘like America’, BJP MP’s brother built the project
stories.summary: Just 18 days after Union Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari said Uttar Pradesh's national highways would be "like those in America" during the inauguration of the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway, the project has come under scrutiny. The 63-km expressway has reportedly developed subsidence at 84 locations, raising questions over the quality of construction. Following the damage, NHAI declared the project's contractor, PNC Infratech Limited, a non-performer. Three company officials were removed and barred from future work for the next two years. An IIT Kharagpur team will now investigate the reasons behind the damage. Dainik Bhaskar visited the site to assess the ground situation. First, know how bad the situation became in 18 days Patchwork has been done at 39 places on the road going to Kanpur on the Expressway. This means that repairs were done here after the road caved in. On the Lucknow lane, repairs have been done at 45 places. That is, repairs had to be done at a total of 84 places on the entire Expressway. The lane going from Lucknow to Unnao had to be closed again at Israel Kheda. Repairs were ongoing here within a 200-meter radius. A pothole reappeared here in the rain that occurred 2 days ago. In the Bani area, about 30 km from Lucknow, a road was rebuilt in an area of about 100 meters. Further 400 meters ahead, a small section of the road was also re-prepared by laying asphalt and gravel. Here, on the other lane (from Kanpur towards Lucknow), labourers were repairing a section of the road. They informed that on July 30, a truck loaded with gravel had sunk. When the wheel was pulled out, the entire truck overturned. NHAI dug up the road in an area of about 1000 square feet here. A pit of about 2 feet was dug and it was rebuilt. About 12 hours later, a crack of 1 to 2 inches reappeared at the same spot. The road had also sunk in a large section. Worker said - 2 inches gravel, 2 inches asphalt, wasting money The truck that overturned belonged to Golu Kumar of Hamirpur. When we arrived, workers were shifting gravel to another vehicle. They said - these people have been building the road in front of us since yesterday by laying 2 inches of gravel and 2 inches of asphalt. Public money is being wasted in this. Our truck got stuck on such a road. Due to the overturning, our owner suffered a loss of ₹1.5 lakh. Moving forward from here, the road was rebuilt at 18 points on a stretch of about 15 km. Near the 45 km board, the upper part of the road, covering an area of about 1000 square feet, was dug up again. It was constructed by laying asphalt. The construction workers, on condition of anonymity, admitted that this road is not that strong. Shoulders designed to prevent erosion on the expressway have sunk Near the 68 km board, the 'shoulder' built alongside the road had collapsed. This reduces erosion on the main road caused by rainwater. The drain built here to remove rainwater had also broken. The expressway ends at Azadnagar in Unnao. From one side, we paid a toll of 290 rupees. Regarding the collapse of the expressway road, Lucknow's Senior Engineer Shailendra Singh says, "It seems that irregularities were committed while laying the soil and building the foundation. Usually, soil is laid in a 50-centimetre layer, which compacts to 40 centimetres after rolling, but here it seems that 1 to 2 meters of soil was dumped all at once in places. It was not properly levelled." Understanding the reason from experts, we headed towards Lucknow. After 5 km from Azadnagar, a bubble (unusual bump) was felt in the car. Getting out of the car, it was found that NHAI had built the road here only 3 to 4 days ago. But the situation has deteriorated again. In a 10 km journey, 8 such points were found where the road was in the same condition. Near the 64 km board, the road had height on both sides. There was a pit of about 1 foot in the middle. We came to know that the road was built at this place a few days ago. Moving 1 km further from there, an additional bump was felt. 1-foot pit, thick crack in a 10-meter area At the 60.1 km point, a 1-foot pit has formed in an area of about 10 meters. There is a 2 to 3-inch crack in the middle of the road. Standing on it, a slight tremor was felt under the feet, as if standing on marshy soil. As soon as a truck passes over it, the road sinks. It seemed that if rainwater accumulates here, the situation could become dangerous. Driving difficult at 100 kmph While returning from Kanpur to Lucknow, we were driving in the third lane at a speed of 50-60 km/h. Here, we found 15 such points where we felt an extra bounce. NHAI has set the maximum speed limit on this expressway at 100 km/h. However, driving at 100 km/h on this lane, the bounce was felt so much that the vehicle was becoming uncontrollable. Abhishek Gaur, an engineer from a private company in Lucknow who has worked on many large projects, says- 'Every day the expressway is sinking somewhere, which means negligence was exercised in its construction. Now, to fix it, the existing layer of stone-soil mixture and coarse stone will have to be removed and rebuilt.' The company that built the expressway belongs to the brother of a BJP MP The expressway was built by PNC Infratech company. The owner of the company is Pradeep Jain, brother of BJP Rajya Sabha MP Naveen Jain. The contract for the expressway was awarded on February 23, 2022. In October 2024, the company was banned from participating in new tenders. Additionally, two subsidiary companies, PNC Khajuraho Highways and PNC Bundelkhand Highways, were also banned. This was in connection with a case registered with the CBI. The company's officials and employees were accused of attempting to bribe NHAI officials and provide undue benefits. However, the ban was lifted just one year later. 75 crore spent to build 1 km of expressway road A total of 4700 crore rupees have been spent to build the 63 km long expressway. This means approximately 75 crore rupees were spent per kilometre. Among all the expressways built in UP so far, this is the most expensive. The Ganga Expressway, about 10 times longer than this, was inaugurated on December 18, 2021. About 36,230 crore rupees were spent to build the 594 km expressway. This means that about 61 crore rupees were spent to prepare one kilometre. Its toll is also expensive. The toll for a one-way journey on the highway was 95 rupees. On the expressway, the one-way toll is 275 rupees, while the two-way toll is 415 rupees.

stories.title: VIDEO | Husband performs last rites for living wife:Posts WhatsApp status calling her 'Late'; wife alleges domestic abuse
stories.summary: In Firozabad, a man performed the 'pinddaan' (a Hindu ritual for the deceased) of his living wife. He also posted the video on his WhatsApp status. In the video, he is seen bathing at the ghat after performing the pinddaan on the banks of the Yamuna. He had also written 'late' with his wife's picture. When the woman saw her pinddaan video, she was stunned. On Sunday afternoon around 2 PM, she reached Linepar police station. She accused her husband and in-laws of harassment. She filed a complaint against all of them with the police. 3 pictures of the pinddaan Finally, the ritual of performing 'Pind Daan' for the living wife was completed by lighting a lamp on the banks of Yamuna. Now know the whole matter Married in 2014, accused of dowry harassment Deepa Swarnkar, a resident of Nagla Vishnu, filed a complaint with the police on Sunday. She stated that she was married to Jitendra Prakash in 2014. Since the marriage, her husband, mother-in-law, sister-in-law, and brother-in-law have been mentally and physically harassing her, demanding dowry. Deepa says that on July 30, 2026, her in-laws assaulted her. Feeling her life was in danger, she hid in the room. She somehow saved her life. She also has an audio recording of her husband threatening to kill her. Posted a video of Pinddaan on WhatsApp status According to the complaint, on August 2, her husband performed her Pind Daan while she was still alive. He posted a video of this on his WhatsApp status. When she protested, her husband said that she was dead to him and would no longer stay with her. Deepa stated - she has two small children. The entire family is mentally disturbed by this whole incident. She has demanded that the police register an FIR against all the accused, including her husband, take legal action, and ensure the family's safety. Inspector Ramit Kumar Arya said- The woman's husband is an alcoholic. There was a quarrel between the husband and wife. In anger, he performed his wife's 'pind daan' (a Hindu ritual for the deceased). The husband is currently absconding. He is being searched for. Action will be taken.

stories.title: Man kisses burqa-clad woman outside her home:Woman returned from shopping; says, 'He grabbed me from behind, I was left shaken'
stories.summary: A burqa-clad woman was allegedly kissed by a molester outside her house in Moradabad before he fled. A 22-second video of the July 28 incident later surfaced. After examining footage from 25 CCTV cameras, police arrested the accused on Saturday and sent him to jail on Sunday at 2 pm. The case falls under the Katghar police station area. The 22-year-old woman said she remains frightened and traumatised. She said, If something like this can happen at my own doorstep, where will women be safe? I was just entering my house and never imagined such an incident could happen in my own neighbourhood. She praised the police for their swift action in arresting the accused and demanded the strictest possible punishment to ensure he does not commit such a crime again. See 4 pictures Read the full news sequentially Grabbed girl from behind and kissed her It was around 4 PM on the evening of 28 July (Tuesday). There was silence in Karula Gali No.-3, located on Sambhal Road. A girl living here had gone to do some shopping at the weekly market held on the roadside on Tuesday. After shopping, the girl returned home. The girl was wearing a burqa. A young man started following her from the market. He followed the girl all the way to her house. Meanwhile, the girl reached her house and knocked on the gate so that someone inside could open it. At the same time, the young man who was following her grabbed the girl from behind. He kissed the girl. As soon as the girl screamed, the young man quickly ran away. Mother filed FIR at police station, accused arrested After the incident, the girl went inside the house and told her family everything. After this, the family members checked the CCTV cameras installed in the neighborhood. The young man's face was clearly visible. On 29 July, the girl, along with her mother, went to the police station with the CCTV footage and filed a complaint. Police scanned footage from about 25 CCTV cameras to identify the accused. The search for the accused young man began with the help of photos and videos. On the night of 1 August, the police apprehended the young man. He has been identified as Mukesh (28), a resident of Milak Basera Khas village in Kundarki. Police presented Mukesh in court on Sunday and then sent him to jail. Victim recounts ordeal After the accused, Mukesh, was sent to jail, the victim said she was returning home around 4 pm on Tuesday when he approached from behind as she knocked on her door, grabbed her and kissed her. She raised an alarm, prompting him to flee. Although the street was deserted, the incident was captured on nearby CCTV. She expressed satisfaction with the police action and demanded the harshest punishment for the accused. Mother demands strict action The victim's mother said they were asleep when their daughter knocked on the door. They only learnt about the incident later after watching the CCTV footage. She said women should feel safe at their own doorsteps and welcomed the accused's arrest, demanding strict punishment. SP City Ranvijay Singh said the incident occurred on July 28 while the woman was talking on the phone outside her house. The accused approached, committed an obscene act, and fled. Police registered a case, identified him through CCTV footage, arrested him, and sent him to jail.

stories.title: Schoolgirl hangs herself following police interrogation:Father in Saudi Arabia blames officers after two youths leak explicit video in Ballia
stories.summary: Distressed by the viral circulation of an explicit video, a 15-year-old girl ended her life by hanging in Uttar Pradesh’s Ballia district. The incident occurred shortly after a police sub-inspector visited her home at 1:30 pm on Saturday to conduct questioning, during which he filmed the premises and put questions to the teenager. Exactly ten minutes after the officer departed at 2:00 pm, the girl was found hanging. Family members discovered her and rushed her to a local hospital, where she succumbed to her injuries at around 5:00 pm later that evening. Following the incident, the victim's father released a video statement from Saudi Arabia levelling serious allegations against the local police force. "My wife had lodged a named FIR two days prior regarding the creation of explicit videos and subsequent blackmail. The police detained two suspects, but released one of them after taking a bribe," the father alleged. He added that officers were conducting a biased investigation and failed to invoke the POCSO (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences) Act despite the victim being a minor. "Instead of taking action against the accused, police repeatedly came to our house to interrogate my daughter and record video footage. Harassed and distressed by these actions, my daughter took her own life. Had the police taken timely and fair action, she might still be alive today," he stated. The tragic incident took place approximately 35 kilometres from the district headquarters. The 15-year-old victim, a Class 7 pupil, lived with her mother in a village under the jurisdiction of Maniyar police station. Her father works in Saudi Arabia, while her elder brother—who had recently returned to the village—is employed in a private firm in Hyderabad. On 31 July, the girl's mother filed a formal complaint at the local police station against two villagers, identified as Zahid and Ismail. According to the complaint, Zahid had groomed the teenager and drawn her into a relationship. During their phone conversations, he surreptitiously recorded an explicit video of her. Following this, the primary suspect and three of his accomplices began blackmailing the victim. They subjected the girl to continuous pressure to meet with them and forced her to accept a marriage proposal. When she refused, they threatened to circulate the explicit footage on social media. Upon her final refusal to meet the suspect, the explicit video was transmitted to several of his acquaintances and uploaded across social media platforms. Distressing details have emerged from the victim’s cousin, who revealed that police had initially apprehended two suspects but released one after allegedly taking a bribe. "Sub-Inspector Ismail Shaikh arrived at our house on Saturday afternoon to conduct an enquiry. He inspected the premises and questioned my sister. Roughly 10 to 15 minutes after his departure, she hanged herself," the cousin stated. Describing the desperate attempt to save her, he added: "We immediately rushed her to the local Community Health Centre, from where she was referred to the district hospital. As her condition deteriorated, doctors advised moving her to Mau Medical College. Tragically, she passed away on the way to the hospital at around 5:00 pm." The victim's brother further accused the investigating officers of intimidation and incompetence: "For the past two days, the police were doing nothing under the guise of an investigation except harassing our family. They kept coming to our home and recording videos for no valid reason. Instead of interrogating the accused, they were grilling us."

stories.title: Road rage in Haridwar:Pilgrim assaulted and car smashed with sticks; video shows caught attacker begging with folded hands
stories.summary: A Kanwariya from Haryana, returning with Kanwar from Haridwar, was severely beaten on the way. In Manglaur, Haridwar, a Kanwar was broken due to a collision with his vehicle. Local youths immediately surrounded the vehicle and started vandalising it. All the windows of the vehicle were shattered with sticks and rods. After this, a youth jumped repeatedly on the car's roof, denting it. When the victim protested, he was dragged out of the vehicle. A video of this incident has also surfaced, in which some Kanwariyas are seen hitting an S-Presso (Maruti Suzuki) with sticks. The rear door of the car was also bent. After the incident, chaos continued on National Highway-58 till late at night. Upon receiving information, the police reached the spot. Considering the seriousness of the matter, the police registered a case and arrested the local youth accused of vandalism, Raja alias Rajesh. Read the full case in detail Main accused arrested, search for others ongoing Considering the seriousness of the matter, the police started an investigation. Police investigation revealed that local youth Raja alias Rajesh (resident of Kamelpur, Roorkee) is the main accused in the vandalism and commotion. Police have arrested Raja, while efforts are underway to identify and arrest two-three other unknown Kanwariyas and youths involved in the incident.

stories.title: Gen Z trapped PM Modi In reel culture, claims Akhilesh:SP leader redefines BJP as party of the corrupt, tyrannical, and sinful
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday said, “The BJP calls itself the world's largest party, but they trapped the Prime Minister himself in the process of making reels. Then Gen-Z made a reel of the Prime Minister. Now when I see Instagram, it makes me very sad.” Akhilesh was referring to PM Modi's recent Instagram content and reels made for the youth. In the last 10 days, PM Modi has made five videos on Instagram, in which he is seen presenting his views before youngsters and students. During the press conference in Lucknow, Akhilesh said, “BJP means 'Corrupt, Oppressive, and Sinful'. This party can never be loyal to anyone. If there is any biggest crisis in UP today, it is BJP. Until this government is removed, the state's crises and the public's problems will not be resolved.” The SP chief also honoured two artists who came as Hanuman and Ram during the press conference by giving them ₹51,000 each. The artist who became Hanuman had danced during BJP President Nitin Nabin's roadshow in Lucknow on 4 July. There was a lot of controversy in the matter. Lawyers, including opposition parties, had objected and demanded an FIR. Key points from Akhilesh's press conference- 1. Destroyed the education system, eliminated employment opportunities Akhilesh Yadav said, “Earlier, there used to be theft in fertiliser sacks. Now, the entire sack is being stolen. They talked about doubling farmers' income but nothing happened. The potato farmer is ruined. There is no legal guarantee for MSP. The education system has collapsed. Employment opportunities have also been destroyed. If there are no jobs, there will be no reservation.” 2. Corruption happened on the expressway, offerings were stolen The SP chief said if E-20 increases mileage, companies should advertise it. There has been large-scale corruption on the expressway. Public funds have been stolen. Regarding Jauhar University, the intention and motive have not been right from day one. They don't want people to study. They couldn't build this university. They want to hammer it down. These issues will be raised in the assembly. 3. 26,000 schools closed in 10 years, reservation posts were stolen Akhilesh Yadav said 26,000 schools were closed in 10 years during BJP's rule. As many as 26,386 schools were closed in the name of merger. The highest number of primary schools were closed in Lakhimpur. Papers of more than 20 examinations have been leaked. More than 12,000 reservation posts for backward classes and Dalits have been stolen. Ever since we started providing data, the government website has been shut down. Those who claim to make India a 'Vishwaguru' (world leader), the reality is that 7,000 schools do not have electricity. Two-thousand schools do not have functional toilets for girls. Five-hundred schools do not have water arrangements. Twenty-three-thousand schools do not have computers.

stories.summary: SSI Dharamveer Shahi of Ashiana police station, accused of sexually exploiting a B.Ed student in Lucknow by promising marriage, has been suspended. The young woman alleges that the sub-inspector called her to the police station and said, “Your rape case is old. If you have relations with me once, the medical report will come out correct.” The victim alleges that the sub-inspector called her to his room at the police station and had physical relations with her. After that, he sexually exploited her multiple times by promising to strengthen her case and marry her. The matter pertains to Ashiana police station. The victim had filed a case against Abhishek Singh, a resident of Basti, accusing him of having physical relations by promising marriage. SSI Dharamveer Shahi was investigating this case. It is alleged that on February 21, he called the victim to Ashiana police station. After that, they met several times. When the student pressured him for marriage, on the night of July 30, the accused assaulted her and snatched her mobile phone. After this, the young woman complained to the Police Commissioner and DCP Central. After investigation, an FIR was registered against the accused, SSI Dharamveer Shahi, and he was suspended. First, read what the victim said... In a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, the victim stated that she had completed her B.Ed. During her studies, she met Abhishek Singh, a resident of Shankhpur, Basti. Abhishek made physical relations with her on the pretext of marriage and later backed out of the marriage. After this, the woman filed a case against Abhishek in Basti. The case was transferred to Ashiana Police Station in Lucknow under zero FIR. The victim stated that during the investigation, when the crime scene was found to be in the PGI police station area, the case was transferred there. It is alleged that despite this, SSI Dharamveer Shahi, the investigating officer posted at Ashiana Police Station, concealed this information and called her for questioning on February 21. He said that he would conduct the entire investigation of the case. After this, he started calling her continuously in the name of investigation. The victim alleges that during the conversation, he also started making obscene remarks. Established a relationship by claiming the medical report was old The victim alleged that Dharmveer Shahi said, “Your case has become quite old. To connect it with the current incident, you will have to have physical relations again. When she protested, the sub-inspector assured her of marriage.” He said that if she had a relationship with him, he would support her for life, give her the status of a wife, and marry her. The victim alleges that under the pretext of marriage, she was sexually exploited from March until now. Secret revealed during trip to Banaras The victim stated that about a month and a half ago, she went to Banaras with the sub-inspector. There she found out that the sub-inspector was already married. Knowing this, she became upset. When she talked about marriage, the sub-inspector started procrastinating. The victim alleges that when she pressured him for marriage, the sub-inspector assaulted her with kicks, punches, and slaps. He hit her head against the wall and said, “I have kept you only for fun. You are equal to my shoe.” Allegation of Assault Again on the Night of 30 July The victim alleges that on the night of 30 July, around 11 PM, when she went to Apollo Hospital to get medicine for her mother, Dharamveer Shahi called her to Ashiana Police Station. There, along with his two associates, he assaulted her again. It is alleged that an attempt was made to knock her unconscious by hitting her head with a heavy object. Her hands were twisted and an attempt was made to break them, causing swelling in her hands. Additionally, her mobile phone was snatched while threatening to kill her and run her over with a vehicle. Allegation of snatching mobile to destroy evidence The victim alleges that Dharamveer Shahi snatched the mobile phone to erase the chats, photos, videos, and other evidence present in it. According to the complaint, the accused threatened that if she complained to the authorities, he would defame her everywhere. He also said, "I will get you and your family killed. I have connections with senior police officers, so the police won't be able to harm me." The victim states that since these threats, she and her family are scared. Now know in which case the student had filed a complaint About a year ago, the student became friends with Abhishek Singh, a resident of Basti. It is alleged that he repeatedly had physical relations in Lucknow by promising marriage and later refused to marry. In this case, an FIR was registered at Chhawani police station in Basti in February 2026. Through a Zero FIR, the case reached Ashiana police station, from where it was transferred as the incident site fell under the PGI police station area. It is alleged that during the investigation of this case, the student met the then investigating officer, SSI Dharmveer Shahi. The victim says that the sub-inspector lured her under the pretext of investigation and later sexually exploited her. After he refused to marry her and assaulted her, the student complained to the DCP Central, based on which a case was registered against the accused SSI and he was suspended. DCP Central said - FIR registered, accused sub-inspector suspended DCP Central Vikrant Veer said: A case has been registered. The accused SSI has been suspended. The investigation of the case has been handed over to ACP Cantt. Further action will be taken based on whatever evidence comes to light during the investigation.

stories.title: Drove car in reverse, evaded police for 7 km:Theft suspect escaped after stopping on Agra Expressway; only female friend found
stories.summary: A car theft accused dodged the police in cinematic style on the Agra-Lucknow Expressway. The police, who had been searching for him for a long time, tried to stop the accused's car at the Fatehabad toll, but the accused drove the car in reverse (in back gear) for 500 meters on the wrong side. After that, he turned the car around and sped off. He evaded the police for about 7 km. Then he abandoned the car and fled towards the fields with his accomplice. The police found the accused's female friend in the car parked on the expressway. After questioning, the police released her. Several luxury cars were stolen The incident occurred on Friday afternoon around three o'clock. A month ago, several luxury cars parked outside bungalows in Jaipur House (Lohamandi police station area) and Kamla Nagar police station area were stolen. A special team was deployed for the investigation. Police had received information that a vehicle theft accused from Hardoi was heading towards Lucknow via Mathura in a stolen car. Based on this information, the police were alerted at the Rahankalan toll on the Inner Ring Road. The car passed the Rahankalan toll. Police surrounded the vehicle at Fatehabad Toll Plaza The vehicle theft accused proceeded towards Fatehabad in his car. Dauki police were deployed at Fatehabad Toll Plaza. Toll staff lowered the barriers, causing a jam. The car-borne ringleader was with a companion and his female friend. Car punctured by police bullet, accused kept driving Seeing the police, the accused put the car in reverse gear. He drove the car in the wrong direction for about 500 meters. After this, he brought the car into another lane and drove it towards Agra for 7 km. Police fired and punctured the car, but he kept driving it. At Ramada Cut, after stopping the car, the accused got out and fled with his companion. Police found the accused's female friend in the car. She was brought to the police station and interrogated. The accused is a resident of Hardoi DCP City Syed Ali Abbas stated that police had received clues in car theft cases from Jaipur House and Kamla Nagar. Following this, a special team of police was engaged in the investigation. On Friday, information was received from an informant that an accused named Abhishek Vajpayee from Hardoi was passing through Mathura along with his female friend and companion. Following this, a cordon was laid, but he managed to escape. A team has been deployed for his arrest.
