stories.title: 'I will have relations with your wife':Sting operation exposes UP Maulanas; defend triple talaq; perform halala themselves
stories.summary: “Your divorced wife will marry me first, then halala will take place. It is my decision whether I keep her for one night or longer. You cannot ask me to divorce her.” These are the words of Maulana Rehmatullah from Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh, who was secretly recorded allegedly promoting halala. Although the triple talaq law has been in force for seven years, a sting operation claims that some maulanas in Uttar Pradesh are still exploiting Muslim women under the cover of religious practices. Under the traditional practice, if a husband divorces his wife by pronouncing talaq three times, they cannot remarry unless the woman first marries another man. The second husband must consummate the marriage and later divorce her of his own free will. Only then can she legally remarry her first husband. This process is known as halala. According to the sting operation, some couples avoid involving relatives in this process. Instead, certain maulanas allegedly offer to perform halala themselves. They are accused of staying with divorced women in hotels and charging money for accommodation and other expenses. During the investigation, Dainik Bhaskar's team approached two maulanas, who allegedly agreed to carry out halala themselves in the name of religion. In Gorakhpur, we contacted Maulana Rahmatullah. The Maulana runs a tailor shop. We told Rahmatullah - we have had a triple talaq. Iddat, meaning 3 months, is about to be completed. Now we want to live together again. What is the way? Halala is necessary and just as husband and wife live, it is necessary to live that way Rahmatullah : The Quran is considered divine. Halala is in it. The woman should stay away from her husband for 3 menses (menstrual periods). Then she should marry a person who is responsible. It should never be kept in mind that he (the new husband) should divorce her; this will not be according to the Quran. This is the will of the new husband. It is necessary to live in the same way that a husband and wife live together. Reporter : Then with whom should Halala be performed? Rahmatullah: If it's a brother or a close relative, they get halala done with him. This happens because he gives a divorce, but sometimes the man (who performed halala) doesn't divorce her at all. There was a 70-year-old man in Meerut. He divorced his wife. There was an acquaintance with whom he arranged a nikah (marriage) under halala. Later, he changed his mind. He said, "Where is your wife? Now she is my wife." The woman also said that she would stay there. The woman was 40-45 years old. Reporter: We don't want to get halala done with anyone from the family. Rahmatullah: Okay, your wife will be married to me. After that, halala. Now it's my will whether I keep your wife for one night or for how long. Whatever expenses are incurred in this, you will have to pay. Reporter: What will be the expense? Rahmatullah: Oh brother, whatever the Maulana's expense will be. You will have to pay for everything. We will inform the gentleman (pointing towards our source). Not much, consider it within 20 to 25 thousand. Reporter: Will I have to bring my wife here? Rahmatullah: Bring her after Muharram, then the marriage will happen. Then I will explain some things to your wife. For example, when you were husband and wife before, you didn't tell anyone each other's secrets. Similarly, you shouldn't tell anyone what I say. Reporter: Will it be physical too? Rahmatullah: This thought should not be in your mind. Tell me, when a Nikah happens, suppose your wife gets her periods on the first night, then you won't do it, then you'll do it on the second night. You will do it after 4 days, won't you? A relationship has to be built. I was just watching on YouTube. A Maulana says that the husband-wife relationship has to be maintained. You have to forget that she is my wife. Reporter: Meaning we have separated, now she has been married anew. Rahmatullah: We get ready for Nikah because of me, the relationship becomes better. Our family is of Pirs (spiritual guides). My maternal grandparents' home is in Maharajganj. There is Khutha Bazaar there. The Pir Sahib there is our biological great-grandfather. That's why we perform prayers and make amulets. Reporter: What time should I come in the morning? Rahmatullah: Come by 11-12 AM. Then leave your wife with me for 4-5 hours. What happens is that to build a relationship, we need to talk a little. I will have to explain things to her. It's not like coming and pouncing like a dog. We can book a hotel. From here, we left saying that we would bring the wife after a few days. Now we were looking for a Maulana whose stature among Muslims was even greater. Our search ended with Mufti Meraj Ahmed Qadri. The source told us that Meraj Ahmed is a Mufti in the Madina Mosque of Gorakhpur. Hundreds of people offer prayers behind him daily. We approached him and discussed Halala. 'It is in the Hadith that physical relations must be established at least once' Meraj Ahmed: In the case of divorce, Halala is the only way. It would have been better if you had not given 3 divorces. If you had given 1 or 2 divorces, you could have called her back and remarried. Since you have given three divorces, she is out of your hands. Now, if you want to have loving conversations with her, it is not permissible. Reporter: What is the way out of this? Meraj Ahmed: The way is that if you want to live with your wife and children, Islam states that the wife should have a second marriage (Nikah). If there's someone from your family, marry her to him, or marry her to someone I tell you about. She just has to spend 1 or 2 nights with him. They just have to consummate the marriage, even if it's just once. That too, because you have given a divorce. If she has completed her Iddat (waiting period), then when the second marriage (Nikah) happens, she will again enter Iddat (after the second divorce). After that, she will be 'fresh' (eligible). Then you can marry her. The only way for this is Halala. There is no other permissible way. If you go to court, they will just finalize the divorce. Iddat means a waiting period. After divorce, one has to wait for about three months. Before that, a remarriage cannot happen. Reporter: Do they have to have the same kind of relations as a husband and wife? Meraj Ahmed: Look, you will have to spend one night with him. What he does, only he knows. But, in Hadith, it is stated that a relationship (physical intimacy) must be established once. You are doing this for Allah's principle. Reporter: In our view, there is no one who is loyal, who would do something at our behest. We don't want to do it at home. Meraj Ahmed: There is a way. If you don't find anyone, let us know. We will talk to such a person who is responsible. But, the condition is that after the Nikah, you will have to take a room in a hotel for 2-3 days. It's possible that the work might be done in one day. It's possible it might take more days. After that, the Mahr (dower) money will also have to be given. And some 'Nazre Inayat' (favors/gifts), whatever they wish, that will have to be given. Whatever expenses arise, you will have to bear them. After one or two nights, they will give divorce. After 4 months pass, then you can perform Nikah (marry again). Reporter: What will be the cost involved in this? Meraj Ahmed: Look, the Mahr (dower) will not be less than 11 thousand. We'll check the rate of Dirham (silver coin). Assume it will be between 11 thousand to 15 thousand. After that, arrangements for food and drink will have to be made. A gift (nazrana) of 10 to 15 thousand will have to be given. If you don't give it, it's possible that it might come to his mind and he won't leave your wife.

stories.title: BJP survey predicts loss of 52–67 seats in UP:Recommends dropping 35% of MLAs to counter anti-incumbency
stories.summary: Before the UP Assembly elections, the BJP has received a major setback from an internal survey conducted by the party. The report indicates that if elections were held in the current situation, the BJP might have to struggle for a majority. There could be a direct loss of 52 to 67 seats for BJP. The BJP is getting 190 to 205 seats. 202 seats are needed for a majority. In 2022, the BJP received 255 seats. In by-elections, 2 more seats were added to the BJP's account. Currently, the BJP has a total of 257 MLAs. The survey agency has also given suggestions to avoid this loss. For this, the party will have to deny tickets to 35% of its current MLAs. There is maximum discontent regarding MLAs in the Purvanchal region. BJP conducted a survey through the Nation With Namo agency before the assembly elections. This is a registered organization. It conducts political surveys for BJP. I n this, experts and researchers included in the team reached all assembly constituencies from March to the second week of July and took predetermined samples. Some questions were asked to people- 2 types of discontent were seen in the survey In the survey report, people's discontent has been divided into 2 types. The first category includes discontent with the government, i.e., central and state government policies. The second category includes anger towards MLAs. During the survey, the policies and incidents related to the government on which the public expressed dissatisfaction are as follows- Displeasure with MLAs emerged due to these reasons- Team gave 2 types of suggestions in the survey report Suggestion 1- Tickets of 30 to 35% MLAs should be cut The survey revealed resentment against 30% to 35% of BJP MLAs. People clearly told the team that came to conduct the survey that if old faces are given another chance in the Assembly elections like the Lok Sabha, we will look for other options. The survey suggests that to reverse these results, the BJP will have to deny tickets to 30 to 35% of its current 257 MLAs. This will reduce people's anger towards the ruling party's MLAs. The BJP can cross the majority mark. Currently, the party is strong on 190 to 205 seats. However, based on the right selection of candidates, balancing caste equations, and issues that emerge just before the elections, there could be a fluctuation of 10% in this estimate. Faces were changed in 2022 as well Before the 2022 assembly elections, the BJP had commissioned surveys from 2 agencies. Based on that report, the BJP had denied tickets to more than 120 MLAs. New candidates were fielded on 165 out of 403 seats. Despite this, the BJP's seats decreased from 312 in 2017 to 255. This resulted in a loss of 57 seats for the BJP. Suggestion 2- Advantage in fighting elections on issues like nationalism The survey team believes that if the election remains focused on issues like religion, nationalism, and law and order, the BJP will benefit. However, if the SP succeeds in making caste equations and PDA (Backward, Dalit, Minority) politics a major issue, like in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP could suffer losses. Resentment against Yadavs has decreased among the new generation A member of the survey team stated that Yadavs have been considered traditional voters of the SP. During SP rule, Yadavs' matters were often heard quickly in many cases. This led to resentment against them among non-Yadav people. However, this resentment has decreased over the past 5 years. Especially Gen-Z (the new generation) does not consider the Yadav versus non-Yadav concept to be correct. Yogi's team is also conducting a separate survey The BJP organization's survey has been completed. However, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath is conducting a separate election survey. A private agency is going village to village collecting feedback from people about the government, MLAs, and the Chief Minister's image. This situation has arisen after the disqualification of MLAs, by-elections, and deaths following the 2022 elections

stories.title: 'Today is a dark day in history':Allahabad HC judge says attempt was made to influence him; rescuses himself from ₹900 cr codeine case
stories.summary: 'An attempt was made to reach the judge for bail. Such attempts are a direct attack on the independence and impartiality of the judiciary. These cannot be accepted under any circumstances. This is a black day in the history of the judiciary.' This comment was made by Allahabad High Court Judge Krishna Pahal on Thursday in the codeine cough syrup case. He sent 80 petitions, including the bail application of accused Bhola Prasad, to the Chief Justice and recused himself from all cases. Judge Krishna Pahal said at the start of the hearing - After the judgment was reserved, the accused attempted to reach the presiding judge personally. Calling it an assault on judicial dignity, he said such tendencies cannot be accepted in the court premises under any circumstances. Bhola Prasad is the father of Shubham Jaiswal, the kingpin of the codeine cough syrup gang. Shubham is absconding. He has already been declared a fugitive. The next hearing will now be on 7th August. Judge said- If ignored, trust will be shaken Actually, about 80 accused in the codeine cough syrup case have filed bail petitions in the High Court. For their hearing together, the court had fixed Thursday, July 30 at 10 AM. Along with the lawyers of the accused, Additional Advocate General Anoop Trivedi and AGA First Paritosh Kumar Malviya were also present on behalf of the state government. As soon as the hearing began, the court said that the order could have been reserved after the hearing was completed, but later attempts were made by the accused to reach and contact the presiding judge. The court said that if such conduct is ignored, it will weaken the roots of judicial independence and the common people's faith in the justice system will be shaken. Judge said - Prestige of the judiciary cannot be put under the cloud of doubt Judge Krishna Pahal said, ‘If in such circumstances the decision had come in favor of the party whose arguments appeared strong, then despite the legal strength of the judgment, this doubt could have arisen that the decision was the result of some external influence or improper attempt rather than judicial discretion.’ The reputation of the judiciary earned over years cannot be put under the shadow of such doubt. The court said - Justice is not only sufficient to be done, but it should also be clearly and unequivocally seen that justice has been done impartially. Attempting to make personal contact with a judge in a pending case is against the ethics of advocate conduct and the constitutional values of an independent judiciary. The High Court, calling it an assault on judicial dignity, said that such a tendency cannot be accepted in the court premises under any circumstances. The court warned lawyers and accused, saying - Judicial independence is not a special privilege, but a constitutional right granted to every citizen. Any attempt to weaken it should be strongly condemned. High Court has already refused to cancel the case In the codeine cough syrup case, the accused first filed petitions to have the case cancelled, but these petitions were rejected by three different division benches of the High Court and one division bench of the Lucknow bench. The court said that there is sufficient basis for investigation in the matter. After this, the accused filed applications for anticipatory bail. Even on these anticipatory bail petitions, no relief was granted to any petitioner by the High Court, and arrests continued. Following this, petitions were filed for regular bail. In these too, the regular bail petitions of four accused have been rejected by different benches of the High Court. Case was registered on 15 November, 2025 In the case registered at Kotwali police station on 15 November, about 40 people, including Shubham Jaiswal and his father Bhola Jaiswal, were named. As the investigation progressed during the inquiry, many names came to light. Many of them have already been arrested. Now know what are the charges against Shubham A case has been registered at Kotwali against 28 drug traders of Kashi, including interstate gang leader Shubham Jaiswal and his father Bhola Jaiswal. The allegation is that 89 lakh bottles of banned cough syrup worth ₹100 crores were bought and sold. In the name of 93 medical stores in Kashi alone, 84 lakh bottles of banned cough syrup were bought and sold. Most of the medical stores in whose names the business was shown were not found at the location. Later, the fraud of this illegal business network spread across Bengal and Bangladesh was exposed. The investigation revealed that cough syrup was sold to 9 closed firms. These include Messrs Srishti Pharma, GT Enterprises, Shivam Pharma, Harsh Pharma, DSA Pharma, Mahakal Medical Store, Nishant Pharma, VPM Medical Agency and Shri Balaji Medical. According to the Commissioner, fake firms were created only for the purchase and sale of codeine-containing syrup. Cases are also registered against Shubham Jaiswal in other districts including Sonbhadra, Jaunpur, Varanasi, Ghaziabad, and Chandauli.

stories.title: 'Babua will remain a child all his life':Yogi takes jibe at Akhilesh; says 'Evening gatherings were routine, change requires hitting the ground'
stories.summary: On National Handloom Day, CM Yogi Adityanath said that those who held power in the state before 2017 had no vision for development. When people in power are not interested in work, the state's deterioration is inevitable. Due to this irresponsibility, the state remained engulfed in months of curfews and riots. Innocent children died from diseases like encephalitis and dengue. Without naming the SP chief, Yogi took a jibe, saying: Some people get associated with a word in life that they can never shake off. Some people remain children throughout their lives. Babua was also like that. He would wake up at 12 noon, get ready by 2 pm, go to the gym at 5 pm, and by 7 pm the gathering would be in full swing. Then how could he think about the state's development? Read the key points from CM Yogi's speech Vote bank politics worsened the situation before 2017 The Chief Minister said that before the BJP government was formed in the country in 2014 and in UP in 2017, work for the development of artisans could have been done, but it requires thinking and vision. He listed three shortcomings of the SP government- 1- Deterioration of education: Earlier, basic schools were in bad condition. There was neither arrangement for drinking water nor toilets. Today, schools are providing bags, uniforms, and modern facilities. PM Modi's 'Nipun Bharat Abhiyan' is being implemented on the ground. 2. Security and Infrastructure: Before 2017, the state had neither electricity, nor roads, nor law and order. Daughters and traders were not safe. When markets remain deserted, it affects every artisan, woman, and youth. 3. Plunder and Insecurity: Previous governments had no interest in development works; there was just a race for plunder within the dynasty, and they themselves posed a threat to women's safety. Handloom and Handicrafts received a new identity CM Yogi stated that the handloom and powerloom industry is UP's great heritage. About 30 lakh people's livelihoods are connected to it, of which 70% are women workers. Last year, the government provided electricity facilities worth ₹109 crores to 40 thousand artisans. Before 2017, Bhadohi's carpet cluster had become almost inactive. Today, exports worth crores of rupees are happening from there to world markets. Prime Minister Narendra Modi himself took the initiative and had Bhadohi carpets laid in the country's new Parliament building. When we appreciate the sweat of our artisans and encourage them, the country's money will remain in the country and prosperity will reach directly to the homes of craftspeople. 'Chief Minister and Ministers have to descend into the field' CM Yogi said in the end that the transformation of the state is possible when the Chief Minister himself takes out time to visit every district and ministers go to ground zero. In our government, every scheme is reaching directly to the public without any discrimination and vote bank politics.

stories.title: Car gutted in Lucknow, youth burnt alive:Only skeleton left by the time fire brigade arrived; one hand found stuck in seat
stories.summary: A young man was burnt to death in a Maruti Zen car that caught fire around 11:30 PM on Thursday night in Lucknow. He could not get out of the car after it caught fire. By the time the fire brigade brought the fire under control, only his skeleton remained inside the car. The accident occurred near Saraiya Mod in the Bakshi Ka Talab (BKT) area. According to the police, the cause of the car fire is not yet clear. It is also not known whether the car caught fire while moving or if it was stationary at the time. The body has been sent for post-mortem. Young man's body found burnt on the driving seat ACP Vikas Pandey said that at around 11:30 PM, information was received about a car catching fire on the highway. When the police and fire brigade reached the spot, the car was completely engulfed in flames. After extinguishing the fire, when the car door was opened, a completely burnt body of a person was found on the driving seat. Only a skeleton remained on the seat. The forensic team was called upon receiving the information, and they collected evidence from the scene. In the initial investigation, the body could not be identified. Police identified based on car number Based on the car's number, the police traced its owner. Investigation revealed that the car was registered in the name of Almash, son of Hamidul, a resident of Khurramnagar. Upon contacting the family, it was confirmed that the body found inside the car was that of 32-year-old Almash. The ACP stated that the family is being interrogated. The cause of the car fire has not yet been clarified. The matter is being investigated keeping all aspects in mind. Another body found inside a car in Ashiana Meanwhile, the body of a person was recovered from an abandoned Swift Dzire car at Salenagar intersection in Ashiana police station area around 11:57 PM on Thursday night. According to local residents, the car had been parked on the roadside for the past three days. When a strong foul smell emanated from it on Thursday night, people informed the police. Upon receiving the information, Ashiana police reached the spot, took possession of the car, and started an investigation. During the search, the body was found inside the car. According to the police, the car's registration number is UP 33 BB 8989. The body was identified as Gyanendra Singh, son of Uday Bhan Singh, a resident of Niralanagar, Raebareli.

stories.title: VIDEO | 2 groups of schoolgirls clash outside Gorakhpur school:Argument escalates to physical altercation, hair-pulling
stories.summary: On Wednesday evening, after school hours, a fierce fight broke out between two groups of girl students at the gate of an inter college located in Chargaon, Shahpur area of Gorakhpur. First, there was an argument, which quickly escalated into a physical altercation. Someone viralized a video of this street fight on social media. It is being reported that on Wednesday evening around 4 PM, after school hours, the girl students came out of the school. During this, an argument started between two students over some issue. According to eyewitnesses, as the dispute escalated, students from one side started verbally abusing and physically assaulting the other student. During the incident, a crowd of passersby and other students gathered outside the school gate. Attempts were made to intervene, but both sides continued to clash with each other. Principal said - Investigation underway The school principal stated that as soon as information about the incident was received, the matter was taken seriously. On Thursday, the students involved in the dispute did not come to school. The entire matter is being investigated. Action will be taken as per rules if found guilty. The police say that no complaint has been received from either side so far. An investigation is also being conducted based on the video. The school administration has appealed to students and parents to maintain discipline.

stories.title: Auto-rickshaw driver's body found in Varuna river:Son says, 'Cop had been following him for three days'; police probe underway
stories.summary: A commotion erupted after the body of an auto driver was found in the Varuna River near Varuna Bridge in the Cantt police station area of Varanasi. The Kachahri outpost in-charge had reached the spot with police force upon receiving information about an abandoned auto standing on Varuna Bridge. A bottle of acid was found inside the auto. Following this, when police started searching, a body was found floating in the Varuna River. The police then informed the family members using the auto's number, retrieved the body, and sent it to the mortuary. The deceased's son, who reached the spot, alleged that his father had said that some policeman had been following him for three days. Meanwhile, police have started investigating the case. The causes of the incident are being ascertained through CCTV footage. Police arrived upon receiving information about an abandoned auto People had informed the Cantt police station that an abandoned auto bearing number UP 65 ET 8037 was standing on Varuna Bridge, with a bottle of acid kept in the front. The Kachahri outpost in-charge immediately reached the spot and gathered information about the auto, which was found to be registered in the name of Rajendra Prasad Gupta. On this, the chowki in-charge called, and they informed that their auto is driven by Gyanchand Sonkar. His number was taken and his family members were called. Boy who reached the spot made allegations After receiving information, Gyanchand Sonkar's son Ashish Sonkar reached the spot. Police got the auto identified. After that, when searched, a body was found floating in the Varuna. His son Ashish identified it as Gyanchand. Ashish said that during Sawan, everyone had gone to Ayodhya but father had not gone. For the past three days, he was saying that some policeman was following him. And today his body has been found. Police engaged in investigation Cantt Thana in-charge Raj Kishore Pandey said - The body has been taken out of the water and sent to the mortuary. The post-mortem of the body will be conducted today. Further action will be taken based on the statement of the family members. Meanwhile, police are checking CCTV footage.

stories.title: Abaan Ahmed suffered ruptured liver and lungs, broken ribs:Died from 23 injuries, post-mortem reveals; brother broke down upon seeing body
stories.summary: 23 injuries were found on the body of Abaan (21), son of mafia Atiq Ahmed, in Jhansi. The post-mortem report revealed that his liver, lungs, and spleen ruptured due to a high-impact collision. His ribs were also broken. He died due to excessive internal bleeding. Meanwhile, Sonu, Abaan's companion who was sitting behind Aban's seat in the car, died due to a fractured skull. Fractures were found in both his arms. Both were post-mortemed by a panel of 3 doctors at Jhansi Medical College on Thursday night at 11:30 PM. Aban's elder brother, Ahjam, reached inside the post-mortem house. Seeing the body of his brother Aban, he burst into tears. Relatives consoled him. After this, he asked the police for the post-mortem report. Officials said they would provide the report later. After the post-mortem, Ahjam, along with relatives, placed both bodies in the same ambulance. They departed for Prayagraj with the bodies at 12 AM. Both will be cremated today. On Thursday, Abaan was going to meet his elder brother Ali Ahmed, who is imprisoned in Abaan Jhansi Jail. Four friends were with him in the Creta car. His car collided with the divider in the Poonch area, 70 km before Jhansi on the Jhansi-Kanpur Highway. Aban and Sonu died in the accident. His 3 friends Umar Ahmed, Mohammad Zaid and Farooq Ahjam were injured. Dr. Rajneesh, who conducted the post-mortem, said- Both died due to injuries sustained in the accident. First, Aban's body was post-mortemed. After this, Sonu's body was post-mortemed. Both were post-mortemed along with Dr. Pankaj Mustaria and Dr. Zia Zafar. See 2 pictures of the accident- So much internal bleeding occurred in Abaan's body that it came out of his mouth. Aban was sitting in the front seat of the car. His friend Zaid was driving the car. Sonu was sitting behind Abaan. The car, travelling at a speed of about 120 km/h, hit the divider on the side where Abaan was sitting. This is why Aban sustained the most injuries in the accident. Shortly after the collision, Abaan and Sonu died on the spot. Eyewitness Deepak Yadav, who was the first to arrive after the accident, said - I heard the noise and was the first to reach. I tried to open the car door, but it wouldn't open. After that, I brought a crowbar (iron rod) from a house and broke the door. Deepak said - After opening the door, I first pulled out a young man. His mouth was full of blood. He said - My name is Aban, save me. After this, he became unconscious. Aban had left Prayagraj for Jhansi at 5 AM on Thursday. The Creta car hit the divider in the Poonch police station area. The impact was so strong that the car was thrown about 7 feet into the air. Its pieces were scattered about 40 feet across the highway. The left side of the car was severely damaged. Brother said - Let the brothers be brought for burial Upon receiving news of Abaan's death in the accident, his elder brother Ahjam reached Jhansi from Prayagraj. First, he reached the accident site and gathered information from the police. After this, he went directly to Jhansi Medical College. Here, he met all three injured. Ahjam said - Let the brothers be brought for burial. After Ahjam arrived, the police completed the inquest for both bodies and conducted post-mortems. Ahjam has also given a written complaint to the police, based on which the police may register a case. Sonu's brother-in-law, who arrived in Jhansi from Satna to collect Sonu's body, said - Sonu used to work with trailers. He had come home from Dubai some time ago. Here too, he was working with trailers. But currently, due to the Kanwariyas, work has stopped. He was a friend of car driver Zaid and other companions. That's why he was coming to Jhansi. Cigarettes, shoes and two books found in the car According to Jhansi police, the forensic team found cigarette packets, shoes, and two books in the car. These include 'The Idiot' and 'The Stationery Shop of Tehran'. According to the police, it is possible that Aban was carrying these items for his brother Ali. Abaan was sitting in the front seat of the car, while his companion Zaid was driving. Zaid is the son-in-law of Atiq's maternal cousin sister. He had received this car as a wedding gift. Now only 3 of Atiq's 5 sons remain Atiq Ahmed had 5 sons. Abaan was the youngest. One son, Asad, was killed in a police encounter in Jhansi in 2023. Now there are three sons. Among them, the elder son, Umar, is imprisoned in Lucknow Jail, and the second, Ali, is in Jhansi Jail. While Ahzam, older than Abaan, is currently pursuing his graduation. He has reached Jhansi. Seeing the body, he said, "Let the brothers be brought to the soil (buried)." Lawyer Umesh Pal was murdered in Prayagraj in February 2023. In this case, Atiq, imprisoned in Gujarat Jail, and his brother Ashraf, from Bareilly Jail, were brought to Prayagraj for a court appearance. There, on April 15, 2023, Atiq and Ashraf were murdered in police custody. Atiq's wife, Shaista, is currently absconding. Abaan's mother Shaista, carrying a reward of 50 thousand, is absconding Atiq's wife Shaista Parveen has been absconding since 2023. There is a reward of 50 thousand on her. There are 6 cases. Shaista did not attend the funerals of both her son Asad, after his encounter, and her husband Atiq, after his murder. Ashraf's wife Zainab is also absconding. Questions are being raised about whether Shaista will attend Aban's funeral. Murder took place in police custody Lawyer Umesh Pal was murdered in Prayagraj in February 2023. In this case, Atiq, who was imprisoned in a Gujarat jail, and his brother Ashraf, from Bareilly jail, were brought to Prayagraj for a hearing. There, on April 15, 2023, Atiq and Ashraf were murdered in police custody. Atiq's wife Shaista is currently absconding.

stories.title: Rain lashes Lucknow, highway flooded in Farrukhabad:River swallows 50 acres in Lakhimpur; rainfall 150% above normal in 24 hours
stories.summary: The spell of monsoon rain continues across Uttar Pradesh. Lucknow received rain early on Friday, while around 40 cities, including Agra and Jaunpur, remained cloudy. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts today, with a heavy rainfall warning for 18 districts. According to the IMD, the state has received 19.3 mm of rainfall, which is 150% above the normal 7.8 mm. Heavy rain on Thursday evening inundated homes and schools in Bijnor. Waterlogging was reported on a national highway in Farrukhabad and in several residential areas. In Rae Bareli, a road caved in after the rain, leaving a three-foot-deep crater. Rivers are also in spate due to continuous rainfall. In Lakhimpur Kheri, the Sharda River has eroded around 50 acres of land so far. In Ballia, 27 houses have been washed away by the Saryu River. In Farrukhabad, the Ganga has risen close to the danger mark, with floodwater entering 33 villages and 40 government schools. The Ganga is also flowing above normal levels in Varanasi. Floodwater has entered 40–50 small temples, while the Ratneshwar Mahadev Temple is more than half submerged. A crocodile was spotted roaming on flooded roads in Lakhimpur Kheri. Forest department officials also rescued a Russell's viper that had entered a house and released it into the forest. Meanwhile, more than 20 cities, including Lucknow, Saharanpur and Meerut, received rainfall on Thursday morning. Due to continuous rain and rain-related incidents over the past three days, schools up to Class 8 have been closed. Rain-related accidents have also continued. In Barabanki, a dilapidated wall collapsed on five children on their way to a madrasa. All five were trapped under the debris. A 7-year-old boy and his 14-year-old sister died, while the other three children were rescued by villagers and taken to hospital. In Pratapgarh, a 100-year-old house collapsed amid continuous rain, killing 13 members of the same family. See pictures of floods and rain... Lucknow weather scientist Atul Kumar Singh said- The monsoon system has now become active over UP. It is passing through Delhi, Lucknow and Patna. Due to this, several cyclones have become active. Monsoon winds have reached the plains of the Ganges. Due to its effect, there will be heavy rainfall across the state for the next 4 to 5 days.

stories.title: Senior officials spared, juniors punished over Kanpur Expressway mess:Responsible officers cleared files blindly, without inspecting the site
stories.summary: The dilapidated condition of the country's most expensive Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway has ruined the image of the Union Ministry of Road Transport. The department and NHAI (National Highways Authority of India) are facing disrepute all around. NHAI had to blacklist the construction company of a BJP leader's brother. In a hurry, the Authority tried to show by taking action against some officers that it would not spare those responsible. But the truth is that there are others responsible on whom no action has been taken. Because when the expressway was being built for a long time, what were the officers sitting above doing? Did they check the quality or allow morang and asphalt to be laid based on estimates? Are those responsible for the shoddy construction being protected? In this report by Dainik Bhaskar, we will tell who else is responsible for this. First, let's tell which 3 officers NHAI held responsible and took action against them- Major culprits of the irregularity, against whom no action was taken Responsibility - NHAI's Regional Officer Gautam is based in Lucknow. His job is to monitor NHAI projects in UP and conduct quality checks through periodic site visits. Negligence - Initially, the first defect came to light on July 26. Then he tried to suppress the matter. He said there was a problem with bitumen (coal tar) in a small area. After the matter got out of hand, action was taken against the Project Manager and the Director. Dainik Bhaskar tried to contact Vishal Gautam. The call was answered, but immediately disconnected. When called again, the phone was not picked up. Responsibility - After Saurabh Chaurasia, Sharad became the Project Director of the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway and remained in this position for about 1 year. He was responsible for managing important technical arrangements during construction. Negligence - During his tenure, instead of inspecting the quality by visiting the site, he blindly trusted files and reports. Due to less visits to ground zero, he kept approving every file with 'OK', overlooking construction deficiencies. Dainik Bhaskar tried to contact him, but it was not possible. Responsibility - He is the head of PNC Infratech, the company building the expressway. The company is named after 3 brothers - Pradeep, Naveen, and Chakresh. Naveen Jain is a Rajya Sabha MP from BJP. Negligence - Secured a two-phase tender by bidding a total of ?2926 crore, but paid no attention to site monitoring and quality control during construction. No concrete information could be found about them either. Could not be contacted despite efforts. Now know about two cases of irregularities, in which the company owner was held responsible- What was the responsibility of the officials against whom action was taken? Responsibility- He was the highest-ranking officer for construction work in the field. It was his responsibility to get every layer of soil and gravel inspected and send the report upwards. Negligence- Ignored quality and committed irregularities in the field. Action- On July 30, NHAI removed him from the project and banned him for 2 years. Responsibility- He remained Project Director from the start of construction until 2024. The maximum construction happened during his tenure. Negligence- Instead of inspecting on-site, he blindly trusted PNC's reports. The foundation of irregularities was laid during his time. Action- NHAI has issued a charge sheet, framing the charges. Responsibility- Posted in the position for the last 1 year. The work was completed and inaugurated during his tenure. Negligence- 95% of the Greenfield area work was completed a year ago. Still, they gave an 'all okay' report without checking the quality. Action- Removed from NHAI and attached to PWD. 3 Crores Spent to Repair Sunken Expressway According to NHAI, 3 crores have been spent so far on the repair of the 63 km long expressway. This cost will be borne by PNC Infratech. The company has also been fined 2% of the performance security. The negligence of Theme Engineering Services Private Limited, which monitors the quality of construction, has come to light. Therefore, this company will be excluded from future projects. NHAI itself is getting the quality checked After the embarrassment, NHAI will now get the expressway inspected with a laser profilometer. This technique uses a laser beam to measure the texture, roughness, and height of an object's surface. It creates an accurate 3D map of the surface without touching it, which will precisely reveal the irregularities. How is a non-performer company building the Bahraich Expressway? stories.title: Atiq Ahmed's son writhed in car for 2 minutes:'My name is Abaan, save me'; eyewitness recounts final moments
stories.summary: "My name is Abaan... save me." Only this much could come out of his mouth. People pulled him out of the car, but within two minutes of struggling, his breathing stopped. These were the last words of mafia Atiq Ahmed's youngest son Aban Ahmed (21). Abaan was going to meet his brother Ali, who was imprisoned in Jhansi jail. He had also bought two romantic novels for his brother. When Ali received the news of the accident in jail, he started crying. Abaan was very dear to him. Perhaps this was the reason why Abaan had met Ali 49 times in 10 months. Dainik Bhaskar's team spoke with eyewitnesses, the injured, and police. Read the complete story of the last moments of the accident... First, let's understand how the accident happened? Abaan Ahmed left for Jhansi, 400 kilometers away from Prayagraj, around 5 AM on Thursday with his 2 friends and 2 relatives. But an accident occurred 70 kilometers before reaching there. Near Khilli village in Poonch, while trying to save a calf that suddenly appeared on the highway, the Creta car went out of control. It crashed into a concrete wall built on the roadside. At that time, the car was traveling at a speed of about 120. The collision was so severe that the car flew about 7 feet in the air and its pieces scattered up to 40 feet on the highway. In the accident, Abaan and his friend Sonu died on the spot, while three people were injured. Broke car doors with rods and pulled people out Eyewitness Sakesh said, ''I was working at my shop. Suddenly there was a loud explosion. It felt like something had burst. Several people present around the shop ran to the spot. Saw that there was a severe car collision. Immediately called 112 and got an ambulance. Until the ambulance and police arrived, we ourselves got engaged in rescuing the injured and trapped people. The car doors were jammed. Before the police arrived, we broke the doors with iron rods and pulled out the injured. Later, the police and ambulance took them to the hospital.'' Accident while trying to save a calf, car crashed into wall Eyewitness Deepak Yadav said - I was going from home to the field. Then I saw that a calf was crossing the highway. To save it, the car driver turned the vehicle to the left. Meanwhile, a biker came, and to save him, the car driver turned the car even more to the left. The very next moment, the car crashed into a wall built on the roadside. Some people came running. The injured were pulled out of the car. One injured person's mouth was filled with blood. When we asked his name, he said, "My name is Abaan. Save me." After this, he didn't say anything. His breathing stopped. 10 minutes after calling, the police arrived at the spot. The police took all the injured to the hospital in an ambulance. One part of the car was damaged; Aban-Sonu were sitting on this side According to the police, 5 people were sitting in the car. Mohammad Zaid (35) was driving the vehicle, and Abaan Ahmad (21) was sitting next to him. Sonu (24) was on the seat behind Abaan. Next to Sonu were Umar Ahmad (18) and Farooq Ahjam (28). The car was running close to the middle divider. The car crashed into a concrete wall built on the roadside towards the village. The front part was completely shattered. All airbags deployed. The left side of the car was more damaged. Abaan was sitting in the front on this side, and Sonu was sitting in the back. Both sitting on the left side died on the spot. Aban suffered serious head injuries. His hands and legs were broken. Aban-Sonu kept writhing in pain for 2 to 5 mins Eyewitness Ramakant said - Abaan and Sonu kept struggling for about two to five minutes, then their breathing stopped. Ambulance driver Pravesh said - All the injured were brought to CHC Moth. From there, I brought one injured person, Umar, to Jhansi Medical College. He had a fracture in his hand. The condition of all three injured was normal; they were talking. Village head Brijesh Kumar said - The car hit the divider due to loss of balance. The car's speed was high. After the accident, about 50 villagers and I reached the spot. Injured Mohammad Umar said - Car hit the divider Mohammad Umar, injured in the accident, said - The car was at high speed. Suddenly, after losing control, it crashed into the divider. The collision was so severe that Abaan and his friend Sonu died on the spot. Umar was not informed about brother Abaan's death Lucknow Jail's Jailer Ritwik Priyadarshi said - Atiq's elder son Umar has not been informed about Abaan's death. Information is given only as per the protocol prescribed in the jail. Family members have contacted lawyers of Prayagraj District Court to allow Atiq Ahmed's two sons imprisoned in jail to participate in Abaan's funeral. The lawyers replied that a parole application will have to be filed in the High Court. Two books and cigarette pack found in the car The Creta car (UP70 FW2432) belongs to Zaid; it was received as a wedding gift. Zaid is the son-in-law of Atiq's khaleri, that is, his maternal cousin sister. Two books were found in the car - 'The Stationery Shop of Tehran' and 'The Idiot'. Besides this, a cigarette pack was also found. Was going to meet Ali in jail with friends and relatives See pictures related to the accident- Brother left with the body late at night after post-mortem Abaan's body was kept in the post-mortem house of Jhansi Medical College. After the post-mortem, the body was handed over to brother Ahjam. Abaan will be buried next to Atiq's grave in Prayagraj on Friday.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan says, 'Priyanka was misled into turning against him':'It was only a good touch-bad touch allegation'; vows to return to Parliament
stories.summary: Former BJP MP from Uttar Pradesh Brij Bhushan Singh staged a show of strength on Thursday and spoke to Dainik Bhaskar about the women wrestlers' sexual harassment allegations, the alleged conspiracy, and politics. He said, "They turned a matter of good touch and bad touch into a movement. Posters appeared in Canada and the US. Some people were working behind the scenes. Bhupinder Singh Hooda and Deepender Singh Hooda misled Priyanka Gandhi, who then joined the movement." Referring to his political future, he added, "Everything is fine now. The Parliament I was once not allowed to enter, I will return to that very Parliament." Read the full interview... After a long legal battle, court acquitted you; what would you say? Brij Bhushan: This entire matter was about 'good touch-bad touch'. I garlanded some players and gave medals to others, and I touched or hugged them after they won a wrestling match. Later, it was said that they were uncomfortable during that time. But this was turned into such a big movement, as if something very serious had happened. There were poster wars and candle marches against me even in Canada and America. Priyanka Gandhi, farmer leaders, and even Khalistanis sitting in Canada got involved in this. It was given a caste and regional color. You are continuously talking about conspiracy; according to you, who were the people behind it? Brij Bhushan: In this conspiracy, some faces were visible in front, and some were behind the curtain. If I have to name them, the most prominent role was played by Bhupinder Singh Hooda and Deepender Singh Hooda. They also misled senior Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi and connected her to this movement. Apart from this, many big lawyers, big capitalists, and a large part of the opposition were involved in it. Politics and wrestling- was there an attempt to snatch both in this conspiracy? Brijbhushan: You can say that, but an even more serious attempt was to destroy my character. Character assassination of any person is the biggest sin. The athletes who made the allegations were on the world and Olympic level, so the wrong message went out to the entire world. But after the court's decision, the truth is now in front of everyone. Will you now make an active comeback in both politics and wrestling? Brijbhushan. Where did I go? Neither from politics nor from society. I had said earlier that I will definitely return one day to the Parliament where attempts were made to stop me from entering. I am fully confident that my return to Parliament is certain. What do you think is the reason for the way people came out in your support in Ayodhya? Brijbhushan: This is not support of one day. This is the result of my nearly 50 years of penance. Since the age of 17-18, I have been working among people for public issues. The crowd that was seen on the roads today is the result of that long social and political relationship. Saints on your platform raised the issue of misuse of laws related to women; what would you say? Brij Bhushan: Laws are extremely necessary for the safety and security of women and daughters, but if they are being misused, then there should be serious discussion on it. Saints have raised this issue; if public support is built in society, then further discussion will happen. For now, there is no plan for any movement. What is your view on opposition parties and movements happening in the country? Brij Bhushan: The job of the opposition is to raise public issues. But an old party like Congress has not conducted any major movement under its own banner in the last 10 years. They only mislead people by joining others' movements, whether it's the farmers' movement, the wrestlers' issue, or recent movements.

stories.summary: A con artist named Victor Lustig famously 'sold' the Eiffel Tower for scrap in 1925. He convinced scrap metal dealers the monument was being dismantled due to high maintenance costs. Lustig used forged documents and official appearances to execute his elaborate deception. After his initial success, he attempted the same scam again in Paris. His criminal career eventually ended with his arrest and imprisonment in the United States.

stories.title: 'They don’t need a certificate from you': Priyanka hits back at RSS chief Bhagwat’s Gen Z outreach
Any post against PM Modi to be deleted in three hours: Arvind Kejriwal on new social media law
6,000-km-long ant super colony stretching from Portugal to Italy
Govt bars firms filing fake drug data from seeking fresh approvals
A well in Gujarat's Morbi has been shaking continuously with rippling water with experts having no clue why
stories.summary: In Morbi district of Gujarat, a well has been causing an unusual spectacle with its strange water oscillations since early August. Hundreds of inquisitive locals have flocked to Pranjivan Sadariya's fields to witness this rare occurrence. While local officials have dismissed seismic activity as a potential cause, initial investigations point towards groundwater recharge and trapped air as contributing factors.

stories.title: 14-year-old Millie Pradawong uses AI and CRISPR to make microalgae produce more biofuel
stories.summary: Fourteen-year-old Millie Pradawong has developed an AI-powered computational tool that predicts how CRISPR gene editing could improve microalgae for biofuel production. Her project, MACRO, aims to increase oil production without reducing algae growth. A finalist in the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge, Millie hopes her work will support future research in clean energy and biotechnology.

stories.title: BJP MLAs storm well, disrupt Jharkhand assembly over exam irregularities
Meet Arya Satheesh: High school student invents plant-based plastic that removes microplastics
Argentina property bill protest: Police fire tear gas, water cannons at protesters
India, China agree to use diplomatic, military channels to avoid LAC misunderstandings: MEA
Vijay vs Udhayanidhi: CM rejects DMK's all-party meet demand on Mekedatu and Cauvery dispute
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay rejected an all-party meeting on the Mekedatu Dam. He asserted his government would not compromise on Cauvery water rights. The opposition leader demanded the meeting, citing concerns over water release. Vijay stated the state's position was already conveyed to the Prime Minister. He urged the opposition not to politicize the serious water dispute.

stories.title: Scientists release 42 snakes to bring a giant US species back
stories.summary: In Spring 2026, conservationists released 42 eastern indigo snakes into their historical habitats in Florida and Alabama. After a year of specialized care, these reptiles have adapted well, with monitoring indicating successful survival and breeding in the wild. This significant reintroduction effort seeks to restore self-sustaining populations of this unique snake species to their native regions.

stories.title: The 1900 mystery of three lighthouse keepers who vanished
stories.summary: In 1900, three seasoned lighthouse keepers mysteriously disappeared from Eilean Mor. When a supply vessel arrived, they found the lighthouse abandoned with signs indicating a hurried exit. Investigations uncovered no indications of violence or outside interference. The prevailing theory suggests a rogue wave may have taken the men by surprise. This enigmatic maritime case continues to baffle experts over a century later.

stories.title: In 1974, a German fisherman released thousands of baby catfish into a river; 50 years later they are threatening native wildlife
stories.summary: In 1974, German biologist Roland Lorkowsky introduced the Wels catfish to Spain's Ebro River, where they've since become a top predator, threatening native wildlife. Their large size and aggressive feeding present significant hurdles for conservationists trying to maintain balance. Worsening climate change conditions could facilitate their further invasion into European waters, leading experts to deem eradication efforts nearly impossible.

stories.title: 11-year-old boy took Abbot's kneecap in 1956; 70 yrs later, his widow returns it to the museum
stories.summary: A medieval abbot's kneecap and a floor tile have been returned to Glastonbury Abbey more than 70 years after they were taken by an 11-year-old schoolboy during an archaeological dig. The artefacts were kept in Australia for decades before the boy's widow brought them back following his death in 2025.

stories.title: Trump angry over leak of US weapons shortage as Iran talks enter crucial phase: Report
stories.summary: President Trump expresses frustration over media claims regarding the depletion of US weapons stockpiles, fearing the leaks may undermine America's leverage in negotiations with Iran. While he admits some reports accurately reflect a tighter supply of advanced munitions, he aims to pursue severe penalties for those behind the information leaks. Vice President Vance characterizes negotiating with Iran as exceptionally challenging, referring to their people as radical.

stories.title: China's Taklamakan Desert is now capturing more carbon than it emits
stories.summary: China's shelterbelt initiative has made remarkable strides, turning arid desert borders into thriving carbon sinks. Through strategic vegetation choices, this project now captures more carbon dioxide than it expels. This achievement is anchored in mountain meltwater, vital for its irrigation systems. The initiative showcases the powerful impact of ecological restoration given optimal environmental conditions, though future water supply will be critical for sustaining these achievements.

stories.title: 'Power Banks' for satellites? Bengaluru Company builds tech to keep ageing spacecraft alive
Thailand school shooting: Student opens fire; 7 dead
Jharkhand student protest Day 14: Hunger strike continues as BJP, Rahul Gandhi back students
Trump’s Gaza Board moves ahead with first project - military base for Moroccan troops
Italy, France, Germany battle extreme heat as Europe faces record temperatures
Rahul Gandhi flags Ken-Betwa tribal displacement; Centre forwards complaints to MP govt
Government: Global headwinds pressurising finances
Iran President met a 'voice in the dark', isn't sure it was Mojtaba Khamenei: Report
Australian citizenship for 2 Iranian women soccer players who sought asylum
Patient dies in China biotech company’s gene editing trial
Clarify Dhaka policy: Bangladesh to India after Hasina’s presser
‘Need to elect JD’: Trump ‘backs’ VP as president nominee in ‘meet with donors’
Tell Trump to desist or we hit you hard: Iran warns Gulf countries
Senate panel holds Fauci in contempt for not answering Covid questions
Alternative-fuel passenger vehicles fast catching up with petrol ones
stories.summary: In a significant shift, alternative-fuel passenger vehicles have captured forty percent of the retail market, nearly matching petrol-powered models, which hold a slender one percent lead. July marked the highest sales figures for automobiles ever recorded. Additionally, electric two-wheelers are experiencing unprecedented market penetration, highlighting changing consumer preferences towards cost-effective options.

stories.title: Survey: 81% of study-abroad aspirants plan to return home
stories.summary: Nearly all Indian students heading overseas for education plan to come back home after their studies. What's striking is that about 90% are pioneering this journey as the first in their families to study abroad. This trend highlights a shift towards self-driven decisions among students. Business and management fields are particularly appealing, with many utilizing Google searches and agents to find their perfect educational fit.

stories.title: Temporary disability cert no bar for PwBD quota MBBS seat: NMC
stories.summary: Candidates holding temporary disability certificates can now pursue MBBS admissions, reflecting significant changes in the National Medical Commission's policies. The revised guidelines indicate that admission requests from persons with disabilities will be subject to assessment by medical boards. It is noteworthy that the presence of progressive or non-progressive disabilities will not inherently prevent admission, with a thorough evaluation of functional competency taking place.

stories.title: Settling with a few cases won't stop CBI probe: Supreme Court warns realtors
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will continue CBI investigations into defaulting realtors. Builders cannot escape probes by settling with only a few homebuyers. Many bank officials are found to have colluded with these builders. CBI has completed probes in eighteen of fifty registered cases. Banks must grant prosecution sanctions for accused officials within two weeks.

stories.title: Rahul reaches out to Gen Z, backs student stir in Jharkhand
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi took to Instagram to voice his support for student protests, labeling the education system as deeply flawed and in need of urgent reform. His remarks were made following a meeting with NEET protesters who detailed their encounters with police brutality. The students bravely shared stories of discrimination they faced while advocating for their rights.

stories.title: Prosecutors Outline Grim Allegations: Filings detail alleged planned killing; body reportedly hidden for months
stories.summary: Prosecutors have outlined new allegations in the murder case against singer d4vd, claiming a heated argument with 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez preceded her death in April 2025. Court filings allege the singer killed and later dismembered the teenager before concealing her remains in his Tesla. d4vd has pleaded not guilty to all charges, and his legal team maintains he neither killed Celeste nor caused her death.

stories.title: Need to seal alliance deal with SP soon for UP polls, MPs tell Congress leadership
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Congress MPs are actively pushing for a partnership with the Samajwadi Party, considering it vital to mount a formidable challenge to the BJP in the upcoming elections. With a strong consensus among the MPs for quick action, party leaders are currently assessing viable constituencies and gathering data to facilitate negotiations, striving to strengthen their united front against the BJP's dominance in the state.

stories.title: BJP to Congress: Let House function, Amit Shah will come
stories.summary: The BJP has called out Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge for allegedly spreading misinformation. They assert that Home Minister Shah is present at Parliament House, but is unable to participate due to ongoing protests. Continued disruptions by the opposition hinder legislative work, yet Shah is ready to address their concerns directly. The BJP confirmed Shah is in his office daily, awaiting the resumption of parliamentary activities.

stories.title: Rijiju raises point of order, Kharge hits back at minister
stories.summary: The Rajya Sabha approved the Appropriation Bill, 2026, authorizing fund withdrawals for excess expenditure. Opposition members repeatedly demanded Home Minister Amit Shah's presence in the House. Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju was asked to convey their sentiments to Shah. Leader of the Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge sought the Home Minister's statement on student police action. The opposition also requested the Prime Minister's apology for the alleged police excesses.

stories.title: Land-grab case: Supeme Court grants interim bail to Abhishek's PA
stories.summary: In a significant move, the Supreme Court has granted interim bail for one week to Sumit Roy, who serves as the personal assistant to TMC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee. Roy is implicated in the Salboni land-grabbing case, which followed the arrest of former TMC MLA Sujoy Hazra. Notably, the court has stayed Roy's arrest until it reconvenes for the next hearing.

stories.title: UPI charges: Lok Sabha passes bill for government to make changes
stories.summary: The Lok Sabha has taken a vital step by passing a Bill aimed at simplifying tax rules to enhance investment attractiveness. The new legislation abolishes a limitation on specific electronic payment options, allowing banks and providers to charge merchants on transactions. Additionally, the government is empowered to revise the zero-MDR scheme for UPI and RuPay. This initiative is poised to drive advancements in the financial sector’s infrastructure and innovative capabilities.

stories.title: Amid cyber threats, IT ministry asked to expedite hirings
stories.summary: The finance ministry has sanctioned more posts for CERT-In, yet the hiring remains underway. With rising cyber threats dominating discussions, a parliamentary committee is pressing for expedited recruitment. The IndiaAI Mission's fellowship program initially struggled to attract candidates. In response, MeitY is implementing outreach sessions and promotional campaigns to encourage more applicants. Additionally, final touches are being made to recruitment guidelines for several scientific roles ahead of future job s.

stories.title: 15 Indian seafarers killed in West Asia and Black Sea conflicts: Regulator
stories.summary: Geopolitical conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea have endangered Indian seafarers. Fifteen Indian seafarers have died and two remain missing in recent months. Drone and missile attacks have become rampant in the Black Sea region. Piracy off Somalia and Houthi threats have also resurfaced significantly. India's maritime regulator is enhancing safety measures and tracking seafarers' well-being.

stories.title: Rahul ignored plan to end my fast, says Sonam Wangchuk
stories.summary: Sonam Wangchuk voiced disappointment with political leaders after his hunger strike concluded. His wife Gitanjali sought Rahul Gandhi's involvement but received no positive response. Union ministers also reportedly broke a promise regarding the release of photos. Wangchuk felt leaders showed a narrow approach and arrived late to his protest. He praised the apolitical CJP organization for its fair and just advocacy.

stories.title: 3 rebel TMC MPs to meet Prime Minister today
stories.summary: A trio of dissenting Trinamool MPs is set to engage with Prime Minister Narendra Modi following their earlier discussions with Union Minister Amit Shah related to pressing concerns. Notably, these lawmakers have distanced themselves from two NDA meetings. Additionally, other NCPI representatives and Shiv Sena MPs are expected to join them for a breakfast meeting with the Prime Minister on Friday morning.

stories.title: Supreme Court happy with progress in talks in Sunjay Kapur case
stories.summary: In an effort to resolve a high-profile family dispute, members are actively engaging in mediation under the supervision of ex-CJI DY Chandrachud, following a Supreme Court directive. So far, six sessions have taken place, where the parties have agreed to continue discussions. They are pursuing a comprehensive settlement related to trust claims, with mediation scheduled to run until November 2.

stories.title: 5.7 lakh people fined Rs 5.1 cr in 2025-26 for smoking in public
stories.summary: In India, over 570,000 individuals were fined for smoking in public spaces, accumulating penalties exceeding Rs 51 million under the COTPA legislation. Karnataka led the charge, issuing the most fines. Interestingly, several states recorded no violations or fines throughout the year. Enforcement primarily lies with state governments, highlighting the varying levels of adherence to the public smoking ban.

stories.title: Weeding out dead wood aim of compulsory retirement, says Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court clarified that compulsory retirement is not a punishment for diminished performance, but rather a necessary step to uphold the standards of efficiency and discipline required. The court dismissed a plea from a CISF officer who disputed his removal after his performance had notably dropped from 'Good' to 'Average'. It emphasized the importance of consistent high performance among personnel in disciplined forces.

stories.title: South Africa recalls envoy for attending Zuma meet with businessman Gupta
stories.summary: South Africa's diplomatic relations may be on shaky ground as the country has recalled its ambassador to India. This step follows the emergence of images depicting a meeting between ex-president Jacob Zuma and Ajay Gupta, a businessman facing serious corruption accusations. The Gupta brothers, known for their controversial ties during Zuma's term, along with Zuma himself, have staunchly rejected all charges against them, raising questions about accountability.

stories.title: Can't exclude SC/ST creamy layer from quotas: Government to Supreme Court
stories.summary: The government is against extending the creamy layer to SC and ST reservation benefits, emphasizing that the challenges these communities face are rooted in more than economic issues. Reservation serves to right historical wrongs and ensure equitable access. The Supreme Court has permitted states to categorize castes within SC groups, but only Parliament holds the power to amend the lists of SC and ST populations eligible for these allocations.

stories.title: Netanyahu calls PM Modi, discusses bilateral ties, West Asia situation
stories.summary: In a significant phone discussion, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu evaluated the progress made in their strategic partnership and bilateral engagements. They also addressed current developments in West Asia, amidst Israel's increasing international scrutiny due to its military actions. This exchange highlights their continued efforts to bolster cooperation and deepen ties between India and Israel.

stories.title: Foreign funding up despite tightening of FCRA rules
stories.summary: Despite the tightening of regulations, foreign contributions to NGOs have surged. Recently, however, there has been a notable decline in the number of registered NGOs, now totaling merely 14,500 compared to several lakh in the past. The government emphasizes that the amendments focus on specific foreign-funded channels, aiming to enhance oversight without hindering the broader civil society framework.

stories.title: Opposition opposes FCRA bill, says minorities being targeted
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi briefed opposition parties on discussions regarding the delimitation bill. The opposition maintains its stand on women's reservation within the current Lok Sabha strength. Discussions also covered the FCRA bill, with concerns raised about its impact on minorities. Some members noted potential government removal of retrospective effect clauses. Parliamentary functioning remains contingent on government statements regarding protests and donations.

stories.title: Amit Shah assured proposed FCRA changes will not be retrospective, says Mizoram CM
stories.summary: Chief minister Lalduhoma from Mizoram held a pivotal meeting with Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday, where Shah confirmed that amendments to the FCRA will not have a retroactive effect. Church representatives were also part of the discussion, emphasizing the need for suggestions to safeguard the FCRA. A vital debate on the proposed bill is set for August 12, promising to clarify future legislative actions.

stories.title: Supreme Court dismisses plea challenging Delhi HC relief to Hinduja brothers in Bofors case
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has officially closed the chapter on the Bofors payoff case by dismissing an appeal that challenged the Delhi High Court's 2005 ruling, which had previously annulled criminal proceedings against the Hinduja brothers. Advocate Ajay K Agrawal filed the appeal, but the court decided against allowing more time for arguments, finalizing the legal dispute once and for all.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Mignon McLaughlin: 'The proud man can learn humility, but he will be proud of it' and why some things never change
Quote by Michel Foucault: 'Maybe the target nowadays is not to discover what we are but...'
stories.summary: Michel Foucault posited that identity is sculpted by societal labels rather than an inherent human essence. He asserted that true freedom lies in critically examining and discarding these imposed identities. Today, power operates subtly through institutions dictating people's identities. Furthermore, technology and algorithms play a role in shaping digital personas, echoing Foucault's warnings. Choosing to resist these labels empowers individuals to transcend predefined identities.

stories.title: Quote of the day by JD Vance on 'Limousine socialists': 'They're not promising you industry, they're not promising you good jobs, what they are promising you is...'
Quote by Martha Nussbaum: 'Knowledge is no guarantee of good behavior, but ignorance is...'
stories.summary: Martha Nussbaum emphasizes that possessing technical skills isn't synonymous with ethical conduct. She points out that ignorance, whether intentional or overlooked, can lead to detrimental choices. Today's educational systems may churn out proficient employees but often lack the essential elements of critical thinking and empathy. The humanities, she argues, play a crucial role in fostering understanding and reducing harm by encouraging a variety of viewpoints.

stories.title: Hawaii congressional candidate Kirill Basin allegedly threatened beachgoers in Maui
stories.summary: At Keawakapu Beach, Democratic congressional hopeful Kirill Basin encountered serious legal issues after reportedly threatening individuals with a knife and a gun. A bystander, trained in martial arts, bravely intervened and rendered Basin unconscious during the altercation. Now charged with terroristic threatening, Basin faces a one million dollar bail, further complicated by a troubling history of previous arrests for assault and property damage.

stories.title: Iltija booked for ‘assaulting’ cop; PDP says she was manhandled
stories.summary: An FIR has been filed by J&K Police against Iltija Mufti, accusing her of assaulting an officer amid protests. Charges against her involve public servant assault and rioting, while her mother, Mehbooba Mufti, is also named for failing to adhere to protest regulations. The PDP refutes these claims, asserting police brutality led to Iltija's injuries and criticizing the questioning of an individual in medical care.

stories.title: 'USCIS makes mistakes': Immigration expert breaks down new H-1B, Green Card rule, calls its another step in dismantling legal immigration
Landmine blast injures Army duo in Poonch’s Mendhar, 2 rusty shells destroyed in Mankote sector
stories.summary: In the Mendhar sector, two personnel from the Army Bomb Disposal Squad sustained injuries while trying to defuse a dangerous landmine. A nearby team later located and safely destroyed rusty mortar shells in the Mankote sector. The initial discovery of the landmine was made by an Army patrol, which promptly notified the bomb disposal unit.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Michael Fassbender: "I've always been more inclined to go out to work than…"
Andy Burnham 'personally intervenes' as UK reviews early release of grooming gang offenders
'12 years in the US, leaving with empty hands': Indian woman says her H-1B was revoked because employer didn't run payroll
'He deserves to be remembered': British man who wrongly spent 11 years in jail raises funds to restore murder victim’s grave
Chicago homeowner sues US govt over alleged warrantless immigration raid that damaged property
stories.summary: A Chicago homeowner has sued the US government, alleging Customs and Border Protection officers entered his property without a warrant during an immigration operation in 2025. The lawsuit claims officers damaged his home, ignored requests to leave and violated his constitutional rights. The Department of Homeland Security says its officers acted within legal authority.

stories.title: Saudi Prince's $450 million superyacht hides a secret cabin deep inside the hull, designed to...
stories.summary: The superyacht Serene, owned by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud, features a unique hidden sea cabin. Strategically positioned for stability, this Balinese-inspired retreat offers serenity during turbulent waters. Additionally, the yacht showcases an extraordinary custom snow room, perfect for cooling off from the intense Middle Eastern heat, merging ingenious engineering with unrivaled luxury for ultimate comfort at sea.

stories.title: 'Islamification of the country has to stop': McKinney council meeting extends for 5 hours over debate on mosque project, plan gets nod after massive fight
Europe’s forests losing biomass fast; carbon sink weakened by drought, beetles
Canada deported 3,323 Indians in first half of 2026: Report
UK officials issued a legal warning after protected seahorses were disturbed; divers should...
stories.summary: UK marine authorities are sounding an alarm for water users and film crews alike, as the rise in coastal tourism increases the chances of encountering protected seahorses. Disturbing these delicate creatures without the necessary permits can lead to legal repercussions. It’s advised to maintain a respectful distance and refrain from touching seahorses, while reporting any sightings contributes significantly to conservation efforts for these vulnerable populations.

stories.title: Study discovers that primates take care of animals outside their own family
Indian-origin landlord sued in Pennsylvania for harassing tenant: Only wore khaki pants, showed photo of naked man and woman
Vance over Rubio for 2028? What Trump reportedly told donors at private meeting
'Grievance of Gen Z genuine': RSS chief defends protest as way of 'reaching consensus' in democracy
stories.summary: Calling "protest is a way of dialogue", RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat said: "I won’t say that Gen Z should not protest, but in a democracy there are ways of going about it". He said that Gen Z and Gen Alpha want "logical answers" to the questions raised by them. The RSS chief also said that the "education is not a commercial business". Earlier, Bhagwat urged parents to lead by example.

stories.title: In 2023, a veterinarian left a $150,000 job; three years later, relief work pays twice as much
stories.summary: Oregon veterinarian Ron Titterington made a bold move, leaving his lucrative executive position for flexible relief shifts. Surprisingly, he now earns double his previous salary while achieving a healthier work-life balance. This shift highlights the increasing trend of seasoned veterinarians prioritizing well-being over traditional burnout, as the high demand for relief vets significantly enriches their earnings. Titterington plans to pursue this gratifying path rather than opting for full retirement.

stories.title: US judge clears way for Trump admin to end deportation protections for 350,000 Haitians
How Cambridge's youngest black professor 'conned' Great Britain
stories.summary: How did Jason Arday’s extraordinary claims travel from interview to interview without serious scrutiny? His rise and fall tells a larger story about Cambridge, imperial guilt, institutional theatre and the modern Britain that wanted to believe.

stories.title: TikTok Star Enters Hospice: Family say Sydney Towle is in end-of-life care; fans recall Miami runway
stories.summary: TikTok creator Sydney Towle, 26, has entered hospice care after a three-year battle with the rare bile duct cancer cholangiocarcinoma. Her family shared the emotional update, thanking supporters for their love and prayers. Diagnosed at 23, Towle inspired more than 1.1 million followers by documenting her journey with honesty, hope, and resilience. Despite her worsening condition, she remained optimistic, reminding fans that miracles can happen and encouraging others to never lose hope.

stories.title: Who is Sadhana Gollapudi? Row over Indian woman's dancing video as she's baselessly accused of visa fraud; US attorney says she's a naturalized citizen
stories.summary: An Indian-American woman's online life took a dark turn when she was falsely accused of visa fraud. A hate account shared Sadhana Gollapudi's dancing video and claimed that she had been on a student visa since 2014. A US attorney stepped in, clarifying her status as a naturalized citizen. The entire episode triggered a massive row and Gollapudi too issued a statement.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Keanu Reeves: ‘Grief changes shape, but it never ends,’ and why healing is not the same as forgetting
stories.summary: Keanu Reeves opens up about the profound impact of grief after experiencing notable losses in his life. He shares that mourning evolves rather than fades, as individuals adapt to living with the void left behind. This insightful viewpoint encourages a softer way to cherish those we've lost, suggesting that love's essence remains in our ongoing memories and daily reflections.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Ex-Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal convicted in rape case; Atiq Ahmed's son killed in road accident
'We are not enemies': Rijiju meets Rahul to break Parliament logjam over Delimitation, FCRA
In 1986, Australia eradicated rabbits from an island stripped bare by 150 years of grazing
stories.summary: Phillip Island has undergone a remarkable environmental turnaround following an extensive pest eradication initiative. The island is witnessing a resurgence of native flora and is nurturing thriving colonies of migratory seabirds. Each year, it becomes a safe haven for thousands of seabirds to breed. Ongoing restoration efforts aim to safeguard native wildlife and reinforce vulnerable soil ecosystems, making it a crucial sanctuary for reptiles that have vanished from other regions.

stories.title: Top 7 US employers pay H-1B workers 50% more than national median: Report
IIT-G develops low-cost device to detect toxic metals, bacteria in water
