Govt backs 20 indigenous AI models, clears 58 centres of excellence
stories.summary: Among the models already launched are Sarvam AI’s 30-billion and 105-billion parameter models and Indus, Gnani.AI’s speech-to-speech model, BharatGen’s multilingual models and Avataar AI’s video-generation model. The IndiaAI Mission, approved in March 2024 with an outlay of Rs 10,371.92 crore over five years, is aimed at creating domestic capabilities in computing, foundation models, applications, research and responsible AI.

stories.title: 'Can't be run in India as per US law': Govt, Meta discussions continue on algorithms and compliance
stories.summary: Meta's international team is in ongoing talks with Indian government representatives today, aiming to align with local laws and tackle content moderation challenges. Officials are requesting insights into algorithms and preventive measures against harmful content. They are also discussing WhatsApp policies and strategies to combat CSAM. A meeting between IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Meta's global team is expected later today.

stories.title: Canadian woman who slapped teen wearing pro-Trump clothing faces deportation
How Detroit's abandoned lots became one of America's largest urban farms
stories.summary: In Detroit, an inspiring urban agriculture movement has taken root, converting neglected land into vibrant community gardens and farms. With over two thousand installations, this initiative not only bolsters food security but also ignites a sense of pride among local residents. City officials are now working to formalize the movement, enhancing access to essential land and water resources while universities and organizations lend their support in the land acquisition journey.

stories.title: Why New York turned 5,000 discarded toilets into oyster reefs beneath Jamaica Bay
stories.summary: New York City repurposed nearly five thousand old toilets into artificial reef structures. These porcelain fixtures now provide a base for juvenile oyster growth in Jamaica Bay. Oyster reefs are vital for filtering pollutants and improving water quality in New York Harbour. Decades of pollution and overfishing had previously destroyed these important natural systems. This initiative supports broader coastal resilience and habitat restoration efforts across the region.

stories.title: On the frontlines: How Indian sailors are paying the price in Middle East war
stories.summary: India's maritime workers are confronting unprecedented challenges as wartime conflicts reconfigure shipping routes into perilous zones. The recent loss of life among Indian sailors in attacks on commercial vessels has raised alarm. With many enduring extended time away from home and facing harsh conditions at sea, their families live in constant worry about their safety. The call for better protection and governmental assistance for these seafarers is intensifying.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Michael Jackson: "You never know how long you have with someone, so don't forget to say…"
Chicago study links more urban tree cover to fewer deaths
stories.summary: A new study by Northwestern University has found that neighbourhoods in Chicago that lost more tree canopy over 11 years also recorded higher mortality rates, particularly in hotter areas. The researchers say protecting mature trees, along with planting new ones, could help reduce heat-related health risks and improve public health in cities.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Emma Watson: ‘Don't let anyone tell you what you can and can't do,’ and why limits are often imposed before they are real
stories.summary: Emma Watson's post-Harry Potter journey is a testament to breaking barriers and redefining success. Opting for higher education and championing gender equality over conventional Hollywood roles, she embodies the spirit of the saying, 'Don't let anyone tell you what you can and can't do.' Watson's story motivates others to carve out their own paths and pursue their goals with unwavering conviction.

stories.title: Rivalry out in open: Japan labels China 'greatest strategic challenge'
From Rs 36 crore to Rs 180 crore: PM Modi's foreign travel bill jumps 5x since 2021
Meet ‘Granny H’, the mystery knitter leaving toys for children
stories.summary: A ninety-year-old woman named June Rose Hood secretly left knitted toys for village children. These mysterious gifts appeared for two years, sparking much speculation among residents. Hood, known as Granny H, found knitting therapeutic and a way to manage anxiety. Her grandson helped hide the handmade toys, which brought smiles to many faces. The community later celebrated Hood's kindness and her significant contribution to their village.

stories.title: US dumped 2 million tyres in the 1970s to help marine life; cleanup continues
stories.summary: Millions of old vehicle tyres were placed offshore near Broward County for artificial reefs. Shifting currents and storms scattered these tyres, damaging existing coral reefs. Government agencies are now undertaking a massive, multi-year cleanup operation. Specialist divers and equipment are required for this extensive recovery effort. This project highlights the long-term consequences of environmental initiatives.

stories.title: ABVP to continue 'democratic protests' against exam, recruitment irregularities
Heart attack survivor reunites with nurses who saved him mid-flight after week-long search
Why were Naruto and Safine handed suspended sentences over Jean Pormanove? Here’s what we know
stories.summary: Owen Cenazandotti and Safine Hamadi, two French streamers, received suspended sentences for their actions during streamed content. The court has prohibited them from uploading any online material for six months. Their content, aired from 2023 to 2025, showcased disturbing violence against people. Despite calls for stricter consequences, their sentences remain on hold unless they breach conditions set by the court.

stories.title: As Japan battles a 'cruelly hot' summer, lions and people are falling victim to the heatwave at a record pace
stories.summary: Amidst deadly heat waves, Japan faces a growing crisis marked by significant hospitalizations and loss of life. These soaring temperatures are thwarting recovery initiatives in earthquake-impacted areas. In a heartbreaking occurrence, three lions at a Tokyo zoo succumbed to the heat. In response, officials have issued a heatstroke warning for vast regions of western and southern Japan, introducing the term 'kokushobi' to highlight these dangerously hot days.

stories.title: US buried 56 million gallons of highly radioactive waste during Cold War, now experts will use it to make 4.2 metric tons of glass daily
stories.summary: During the Cold War, the Hanford Site was vital to the U.S. nuclear program, generating plutonium but also creating a daunting legacy of hazardous radioactive waste—millions of gallons of it. Vitrification is at the heart of the solution, as it transforms this hazardous material into glass for safer long-term storage. The Vit Plant has started processing actual nuclear waste and aims for consistent glass production.

stories.title: People can walk across this river in Indonesia without touching the water; the reality is alarming
‘Will be a pressure group’: CJP announces nationwide 'Kya Bolti Public' campaign from September
stories.summary: The Cockroach Janata Party is stepping in as a public pressure group, primarily targeting pressing issues such as unemployment and education reform across the country. Set to launch their 'Kya Bolti Public' campaign in September, they aim to engage the youth in dialogue for transparency and accountability. Moreover, the CJP is determined to tackle escalating education costs and improve the reliability of media.

stories.title: 'Hemant Soren unfit to hold office': Jharkhand students on hunger strike demand CM's resignation
stories.summary: Gearing up for assembly "gherao" on August 10 in the backdrop of the ineffective redressal, a protester said: "We remain steadfast until the government accepts our demands. We now demand the chief minister's resignation, as he is unfit for the office he holds. It has been so long since he returned from Bengaluru, yet he has taken no cognisance of the situation."

stories.title: Who is Jason Arday? Cambridge professor resigns amid plagiarism allegations
White phosphorus scare: US military denies chemical leak at South Korea military base
stories.summary: In a precautionary measure, South Korean officials advised residents to evacuate Osan Air Base following reports of a potential white phosphorus leak. The US military promptly investigated and concluded that there was no trace of the hazardous material. Subsequent analysis identified the residue as harmless corrosion from environmental factors. The evacuation notice was rescinded after successful decontamination efforts, with no injuries reported at the site.

stories.title: Scientists reveal how green roofs cut rooftop temperatures by 40°F
stories.summary: Green roofs offer a solution to urban heat by absorbing sunlight and releasing water. Vegetation shades surfaces and evapotranspiration naturally cools surrounding areas. These living roofs also manage rainwater and provide habitats for urban wildlife. Extensive and intensive systems cater to different building needs and budgets. Cities worldwide are adopting green roofs to combat rising temperatures and improve environments.

stories.title: "I just got violated": Twitch streamer Austin McBroom reacts after woman grabs him on livestream
stories.summary: Twitch streamer Austin McBroom reacted with shock after a woman appeared to grab him during a livestream. He stated he felt violated, questioning the laughter of onlookers at the moment. This incident has prompted widespread discussion about the importance of consent and unwanted touching. Some viewers question if the livestream event was genuinely unplanned or staged for attention.

stories.title: 'Convey sentiments': Rajya Sabha Chairman tells Kiren Rijiju after opposition demands Amit Shah's presence
stories.summary: Parliament proceedings faced disruptions as opposition parties demanded Union home minister Amit Shah's statement. Rajya Sabha Chairman asked Kiren Rijiju to convey the opposition's sentiments to the home minister. Mallikarjun Kharge reiterated the demand for a statement and discussion on the police action. Rijiju said Kharge had not cited any rule while making the request.

stories.title: Total solar eclipse 2026: Why this tiny Spanish village will go dark twice this August
stories.summary: Avellanosa de Muño will host Spain's first total solar eclipse since 1912. Daylight will briefly disappear as the Moon covers the Sun near sunset. This event offers a unique viewing experience unlike a midday eclipse. Later that night, the Perseid meteor shower will also be visible. The village's rural setting provides ideal conditions for astronomical observation.

stories.title: 15000-year-old bones and teeth reveal what humans ate before agriculture
'What if patients die? Can you bring them back to life?': Bombay HC orders resident doctors to call off strike
'We are with students': Kharge's 1st reaction on Jharkhand student protests
Tarun Tejpal sentenced to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment in 2013 rape case; gets two weeks to surrender
Chubby marmots join subscription service after sanctuary faces money trouble
stories.summary: In a creative twist, a biologist from Colorado turned to popular subscription service to secure funding for crucial marmot research. He shares engaging and family-oriented videos featuring yellow-bellied marmots, motivated by recent federal budget cuts affecting his long-standing project. Operating for over sixty years, this initiative not only raises awareness about marmot populations but has also begun to generate essential financial support for ongoing scientific investigations.

stories.title: 'Budget to praise CM Vijay, not address drought': MK Stalin, Udhayanidhi say TVK has failed farmers
stories.summary: DMK leaders criticized the Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget for ignoring farmers' concerns. They alleged the budget praised Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay instead of offering relief. The opposition claimed existing schemes were merely renamed without substantive measures. Delta farmers suffering crop losses received no significant support from the budget. DMK plans to raise farmers' issues and water disputes in the assembly.

stories.title: Los Angeles singer taught her rescue horse to play the guitar and harp
stories.summary: In a fascinating blend of music and animal companionship, a California singer-songwriter is working on a groundbreaking album alongside her rescue horse, Yupia. Using his nose and teeth, Yupia has mastered playing the guitar and harp, creating a partnership that has captivated millions online. The album promises a heartwarming fusion of Yupia's unique sounds and Khramov's vocal artistry, showcasing the profound trust and bond formed between humans and animals.

stories.title: 'Why by December? She should come now': Tarique Rahman's aide challenges Hasina
Why scientists released billions of sterile moths across American cotton fields to defeat one of agriculture's most destructive pests
Scientists turn factory exhaust carbon dioxide into useful chemicals, study reveals
stories.summary: A team of scientists has pioneered an advanced system that converts carbon dioxide directly from factory emissions. This groundbreaking process sidesteps expensive gas separation and purification techniques. By utilizing specially formulated organic electrolytes, the system successfully facilitates the conversion of CO2 into carbon monoxide while minimizing unwanted reactions. This innovation presents a cost-effective solution for curbing carbon emissions from industries.

stories.title: Soaked in rain, fired by anger: JPSC-JSSC aspirants & students' Tiranga march rocks Ranchi
Part of SpaceX rocket the size of a school bus crashed into the Moon
stories.summary: Unexpectedly, a four-ton SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket stage has collided with the Moon, exhibiting the increasing issue of space debris. After spending over a year in orbit, the remnants triggered observable spectral lines indicative of sodium and lithium gases upon impact. NASA, alongside South Korea, intends to photograph the resulting crater to understand the event better. This incident underscores the urgency of addressing space junk management and its proper disposal.

stories.title: Pakistan's crackdown in PoK: How Islamabad is tightening information chokehold amid global scrutiny
Why wildlife managers are coating raven eggs with nontoxic oil to protect sage-grouse
stories.summary: A new study has found that coating common raven eggs with non-toxic mineral oil can reduce raven reproduction and improve the survival of vulnerable greater sage-grouse. Researchers reported that sage-grouse nest survival more than doubled, while their relative abundance increased by 44% in treated areas. However, they said long-term conservation also requires protecting habitat and addressing human activities that boost raven populations

stories.title: Ruled just 27 days: Liu He’s tomb held 2M coins and 120kg of gold
Former gangster-politician Atiq Ahmed's son dies in car crash in UP's Jhansi
Meet Aakash Manaswi, the Florida student whose CO2 mite blower made bees healthier, increased honey across 60 hives
stories.summary: Aakash Manaswi has pioneered a groundbreaking technique to tackle the Varroa mite crisis threatening honey bee populations. His research indicates that carbon dioxide treatment rivals traditional pesticides in efficacy. This method stands out due to its cost-effectiveness and safety for both bees and consumers, providing beekeepers with a scalable, residue-free solution that supports honey bee conservation and enhances global food security.

stories.title: Meet Marie Tharp: The woman who mapped the hidden ocean world in 1957
stories.summary: Marie Tharp's groundbreaking work in transforming ocean floor data into intricate maps unveiled previously unknown underwater landscapes and geological formations. Her findings prompted a reevaluation of established scientific theories about the Earth's surface, with subsequent earthquake data substantiating her revelations. Tharp's innovative cartography served as a pivotal cornerstone for the development of plate tectonics theory.

stories.title: Assam floods crisis deepens: 1.6 lakh people affected across 14 districts, death toll rises to 95
stories.summary: Assam's flood death toll has climbed to ninety-five, with over 1.6 lakh people affected. Six more deaths were reported on Wednesday, primarily in Sivasagar district. Authorities have established over one hundred relief camps for displaced residents seeking shelter. Floodwaters have submerged thousands of hectares of cropland and damaged public infrastructure.

stories.title: NZ councillor joins Zoom meeting from bathroom
stories.summary: In an unexpected twist during a televised council meeting, Dunedin City Councillor Jo Galer joined from her bathroom, laundry visible in the frame. The mayor playfully advised her to move the camera for better professionalism. To add to the intrigue, a shadowy figure emerged behind a frosted glass door during discussions on council budget, sparking viral attention online. This amusing scenario raises important discussions about maintaining boundaries while working remotely.

stories.title: Meet Bartlomiej Kubkowski: The first man to swim 100 miles across the Baltic Sea from Sweden to Poland
stories.summary: In a remarkable display of endurance, Bartlomiej Kubkowski swam an astonishing 160 kilometers continuously across the Baltic Sea, achieving this incredible milestone in 55 hours and 10 minutes. After four previous attempts without success, his persistence finally bore fruit, helping to raise nearly $190,000 for children battling cancer. This achievement signifies a noteworthy moment in the annals of marathon swimming history.

stories.title: Airline ordered to pay Rs 53,923 after passenger's luggage was delivered three days late
stories.summary: A consumer commission ordered an airline to pay compensation for delayed luggage. The passenger's checked baggage was delayed by three days after his flight. The airline failed to provide compensation despite repeated passenger complaints. The commission directed reimbursement for essential clothing and litigation costs. This ruling highlights airline responsibilities under the Passenger Charter.

stories.title: This 2,300-year-old Greek theatre still echoes with live performances
African Great Lakes hold 25% of Earth's freshwater as unique species face extinction
stories.summary: The African Great Lakes boast a treasure trove of freshwater and unique species, forming crucial ecosystems. However, they are under siege from human activities, with pollution and overfishing threatening both water quality and wildlife. This mounting pressure is exacerbated by rapid population growth and the looming specter of climate change, which further endangers the delicate balance of biodiversity in this region.

stories.title: California teen honors late father, raises record $1.23 million for blood cancer
'Not fluent in Tamil is an insult': Actor Dhanush pushes for mother tongue first
Scientists create world’s whitest paint that could cool buildings naturally
stories.summary: Scientists have created an exceptionally reflective white paint to cool buildings. This new coating bounces away nearly all incoming sunlight, reducing heat absorption. Laboratory tests show the paint reflects 98.1% of sunlight, outperforming standard paints. Outdoor trials demonstrated surface temperatures significantly cooler than ambient air. This innovation offers a practical way to lower cooling energy demand in warm climates.

stories.title: Bombay high court convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, overturns acquittal
Rahul Gandhi slams BJP over NEET protest crackdown, says students were forced to apologise
'No explanation given': Arvind Kejriwal claims Meta restricted his account in India
stories.summary: Arvind Kejriwal claims Meta restricted his account in India without explanation. He stated that verbal inquiries at Meta's India office yielded no reasons. Emails sent to the company received only routine acknowledgements. Kejriwal alleged Meta bowed down to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Meta has not yet publicly responded to these claims.

stories.title: Air India turbulence lasted 'four to five minutes'; some passengers still in hospital
stories.summary: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has launched an investigation into a shocking episode of severe turbulence that struck an Air India flight. On Tuesday, multiple passengers and crew were injured as the plane faced an alarming drop in altitude for several minutes. Following a safe landing, medical teams promptly attended to those affected. Vital evidence has been gathered by the regulator to facilitate a comprehensive inquiry.

stories.title: Centre deploys national team as Chandipura outbreak probe intensifies
stories.summary: A national investigation into Chandipura virus outbreaks is currently underway in Gujarat and Rajasthan, where 35 infections and 22 fatalities among young children have been reported. Researchers are analyzing the pathways of transmission and possible animal carriers. Increased surveillance for febrile illnesses and encephalitis cases is in effect, while whole-genome sequencing is being utilized to track the evolution of the virus strain currently affecting the regions.

stories.title: Jharkhand protests: Five-member student panel to hold talks with Soren govt today - key points
Pakistan crackdown in PoK draws protests on UK streets
Air India turbulence scare: After the drop, the trauma lingers
stories.summary: An Air India flight's recent bout of intense turbulence has left passengers grappling with the aftermath. Injuries sustained during the turbulence might not be felt right away and could need later assessment. Moreover, many may face psychological repercussions like anxiety or fear of flying. Experts suggest it's crucial to seek help for any ongoing distress and take gradual steps towards recovery to restore confidence in flying.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Carl Weathers: "I majored in theater at San Diego State. My one eye was on football, and my other eye was on…"
Life's changed in J&K, Ladakh since Article 370, 35(A) repeal: PM Modi
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi emphasised the significant transformation taking place in Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. The repeal of Article 370 opened a new chapter, leading to increased infrastructure and opportunities in the region. Empowerment and constitutional rights have been extended to women and marginalized communities, marking the beginning of a new era characterized by peace and progress for these Union territories.

stories.title: Cabinet secretary and home secretary get one-year extensions
Government hits out at Pakistan’s malicious propaganda against India
stories.summary: In a strong rebuttal, India rejected Pakistan's Youm-e-Istehsal, deeming it as propaganda intended to obscure its own human rights abuses and terrorism connections. The Indian government asserted that the constitutional changes in Jammu and Kashmir fall within its sovereignty, whilst the global community takes note of the human rights oppression occurring in Pakistan-administered regions. Pakistan is called upon to address ongoing bloodshed and relinquish its illegal occupation of Indian territories.

stories.title: Government orders blocking of 7,393 links involved in film pirac
stories.summary: The government has directed online intermediaries to block 7,393 links involved in film piracy. This action includes the blocking of 4,996 Telegram channels and 1,263 websites. The information and broadcasting ministry disclosed this directive to the Lok Sabha on Wednesday. This move follows amendments to the Cinematograph Act in 2023. The legal framework against online film piracy has been strengthened by the government.

stories.title: Supreme Court acquits man in jail for 22 years for wrong conviction
stories.summary: After enduring twenty-two long years of wrongful imprisonment, a man was finally acquitted by the Supreme Court. The injustice stemmed from the trial court's flawed evidence analysis, compounded by the High Court's refusal to entertain his delayed appeal. The Supreme Court emphasized how marginalized communities often find access to justice frustratingly elusive, shedding light on the pressing issues within the judicial system that disproportionately affect the underprivileged.

stories.title: Trai unveils draft service quality norms for network slicing
stories.summary: Indian telecom consumers may soon see network slicing come to life, as the telecom authority has released draft protocols for this groundbreaking technology. These anticipated regulations will enable different internet speeds tailored to various user segments, allowing telecom operators to set unique prices for services like 4G and 5G. This development follows appeals from prominent telecom service providers.

stories.title: Decide on raising retirement age of judges by Sept 2: SC to states
stories.summary: The Supreme Court urged states to decide on raising trial court judges' retirement age. This move aims to align their superannuation age with that of High Court judges. States were asked to make this decision by September 2, dismissing financial constraint arguments. The court stated that retaining experienced judges offers financial benefits to the government. High Courts were also requested to support this age enhancement initiative.

stories.title: ‘Criminal cases can’t have lifespan of turtle’: Supreme Court on activist’s trial delay
stories.summary: The Supreme Court voiced apprehension regarding the extended duration of a criminal trial involving a Popular Front of India activist, who could face more than three years behind bars. With 700 witnesses lined up for prosecution, the trial has been severely delayed. The activist is charged with fundraising and supporting alleged terrorism, prompting the court to call for a swift resolution to the drawn-out legal proceedings.

stories.title: 25 India-bound ships in Hormuz; government set to evacuate 13 soon
stories.summary: Dozens of Indian and India-bound ships are currently in high-risk maritime zones. The government has facilitated the safe return of over four thousand stranded Indian seafarers. Maritime authorities are actively monitoring distress alerts and coordinating rescue operations. Financial assistance is being provided to the families of deceased seafarers. The government remains committed to the safety of its maritime workers.

stories.title: Lok Sabha approves Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill without debate
stories.summary: The Lok Sabha recently approved the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, a significant update from an older statute. This new law modernizes the procedures for presenting digital banking records in legal settings. Despite opposition members’ protests and disruptions in the house, the government stood firm, accusing them of hindering religious initiatives and temple projects. Ultimately, the bill passed through a voice vote before the house adjourned.

stories.title: Rajya Sabha passes by voice vote bill to raise Supreme Court judge strength
stories.summary: The Rajya Sabha approved a bill to increase the Supreme Court's judge count. This legislation replaces an ordinance that raised the sanctioned strength to thirty-eight judges. The bill's passage aims to expedite case disposal and enhance judicial efficiency. It will also provide the Chief Justice greater flexibility in forming constitution benches. India anticipates its first woman Chief Justice in the near future.

stories.title: Rijiju reaches out to Rahul on delimitation bill
stories.summary: The government is pushing its delimitation legislation to increase Lok Sabha seats. This bill also proposes one-third reservation for women starting in 2029. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi rejected the government's outreach for support. The government may reintroduce the Constitution amendment bill soon. Discussions continue regarding the Foreign Contributions Regulation Amendment Bill.

stories.title: Meta apologises for ‘error in restricting PM’s video’
stories.summary: Meta's CEO Mark Zuckerberg formally apologized to the Indian government over several operational missteps, including issues with paid content amplification. The acknowledgment of these errors comes as officials expressed concerns over the potential loss of safe harbor protection for the platform. As the government reassesses its child online safety regulations, Meta committed to implementing necessary corrective actions to address these concerns.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Jackie Chan: "I never wanted to be the next Bruce Lee. I just wanted to be…"
Navigation sat NVS-03 ready for launch, 3 more satellites to follow: Space min Jitendra Singh in LS
Army chief General Dhiraj Seth visits Central Command HQ to review operational readiness
Quote of the day by Jackie Chan: 'You can't back and change your path. Your life is decided by...'
stories.summary: Jackie Chan's career highlights life's irreversible decisions and immediate choices. His demanding training instilled habits which guided his actions under pressure. Ancient philosophy and modern economics support this view of character formation. High-stakes decisions in business and aviation demonstrate their lasting impact. Accepting that every choice leaves a permanent mark is essential.

stories.title: Quote of the day inspired by Homer’s Odyssey: 'Men are so quick to blame the gods, they say...'
stories.summary: Throughout history, individuals have sought to attribute their setbacks and misguided choices to outside influences. This theme resonates in ancient tales like The Odyssey, illustrating a long-standing human inclination. In contemporary discussions, psychology's locus of control principle reflects this habit. Today, institutions and technology take center stage as convenient scapegoats for our failures. Nevertheless, embracing accountability for our actions is essential in overcoming life's hurdles.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu government vows to secure rightful share in inter-state river water
Quote of the day by Napoleon Bonaparte: "Never interrupt your enemy when he is making…"
Real-time mineral monitoring system to curb illegal mining, says Tamil Nadu government
‘Miles to go before I sleep’: Omar gets poetic, says ‘wounds of Art 370 abrogation yet to heal’
Terrorist hideout busted in Poonch, ammo seized; search ops launched in Jammu, Kathua
Researchers examined every body vertebra in 13 Australian snakes and found five distinct regions
stories.summary: Recent studies reveal that snake spines are now categorized into five unique anatomical regions. Surprising findings indicate that snakes have a notably short neck, which reflects their ancestral lineage from lizards. Additionally, this research highlights a newly discovered middle thoracic region that has adapted for movement, enhancing their abilities to burrow, swim, and climb. Interestingly, snakes have evolved their skeletons structurally rather than simply after losing their limbs.

stories.title: West American dams are on the verge of shutting down
Unelected Bihar minister Deepak Prakash nominated as MLC days after SC questions cabinet continuance
In 2023, America’s first live yellow-legged hornet, a bee-killing predator, was found in Georgia
stories.summary: This year, Georgia agriculture teams have successfully trapped more than 866 invasive hornets while destroying 44 active nests in a continuous effort to combat this threat. These pests are harmful to local pollinators and food production, prompting officials to call for immediate reporting of any suspected hornet sightings or nests. Public vigilance and targeted nest removal are vital to managing this invasive species effectively.

stories.title: BJD opposes proposed nuclear plant in Odisha, warns of mass agitation
stories.summary: Addressing a press conference, BJD senior general secretary Lekhashree Samantsinghar claimed that a nuclear power plant would pose a serious threat to the health and safety of people living in the state. She accused the BJP's "double-engine government" of ignoring public welfare in favour of corporate interests. Samantsinghar added that the consequences of those disasters were still being felt and argued that nuclear power carries significant risks to human life.

stories.title: Indian-origin man among 5 convicted in UK child sexual exploitation, human trafficking case
NHRC summons Delhi police chief after failure to answer summon over CSAM content on Instagram
Scientists coated a cicada wing with silver and created a sensor that amplified molecular signals
stories.summary: Researchers developed a sensitive optical sensor using cicada wings and silver. This natural structure boosts weak molecular signals significantly, replacing expensive manufacturing. Silver coating on cicada wings creates tiny gaps that amplify light signals. This technology could lead to portable sensors for detecting pollution and toxins. Future studies will test these sensors with real-world environmental and medical samples.

stories.title: Inside bassist Flea’s $8M Malibu home
stories.summary: The renowned bassist for the Red Hot Chili Peppers, Flea, has placed his sought-after Malibu estate back on the market, currently commanding a price of $7.99 million. This elegant four-bedroom beachfront abode was once offered for monthly rent at $75,000. Additionally, Flea encountered difficulties while trying to sell another of his Californian residences, famed for its design by Richard Neutra, underlining the allure of this exclusive coastal community.

stories.title: Indian-American Congressman Shri Thanedar loses Democratic primary in Michigan
stories.summary: Shri Thanedar lost the Michigan Democratic primary to Donavan McKinney. McKinney secured victory with support from the party's progressive wing. Thanedar acknowledged the socialist movement's influence on the election outcome. His defeat may reduce Indian-American representation in the House. Thanedar expressed gratitude for his service and plans to remain active.

stories.title: With all eyes on delimitation & FCRA, Parliament monsoon session sinks deeper into deadlock
stories.summary: Parliament has hit yet another impasse as the opposition protests continue for the thirteenth day. Despite this, the government succeeded in passing important legislation, including the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill and a bill concerning Supreme Court judges. In an effort to resolve the deadlock, minister Kiren Rijiju met with opposition figures, while Prime Minister Modi focused on discussing strategies with BJP Members of Parliament.

stories.title: Pilot, 69, lands helicopter at Cabela’s for shopping; no citation issued
UBC scientists develop a mixture that keep strawberries fresh
stories.summary: In an exciting advancement, scientists have created an edible seaweed coating that dramatically prolongs the freshness of fruits, particularly strawberries, even at room temperature—outperforming typical refrigeration. This innovative method not only safeguards vital nutrients but also possesses antibacterial features that benefit produce. By adopting this approach, we can significantly cut down on food waste and reduce environmental impact, offering a sustainable alternative to existing cold storage techniques.

stories.title: UK's most wanted fugitive arrested in Spain over multiple sexual assault probe
'My family felt so complete': Usha Vance on why she hesitated before having fourth child
Mystery hero saves Las Vegas family from house fire, vanishes before being identified
An 11-year-old autistic boy wanted to trick-or-treat in summer; neighbors opened their doors and...
stories.summary: A heartfelt Facebook post from a mother seeking birthday cheer for her autistic son ignited an incredible wave of community support. Eighty-three families joined in a unique summer trick-or-treat celebration for Soren, showering him with handcrafted gifts and candies. This touching event not only spread joy but also shed light on the importance of acceptance, dismantling stereotypes associated with autism and showcasing the strength of community bonds.

stories.title: 'No special session of Parliament': Govt on Women's Reservation and Delimitation Bills
'Don't use students for politics': BJP attacks Rahul Gandhi over Jantar Mantar protest claims
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party has rejected Rahul Gandhi's allegations of police excesses. BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra stated no bullets were fired during the protest. He accused Gandhi of spreading a false narrative and using students politically. Patra also questioned Gandhi's selective focus on certain student groups. The party maintained that ministers attend Parliament when their departments are discussed.

stories.title: Over 3,000 cases of deadly fungus Candida auris reported in US: What it is, how it spreads- explained
IMA threatens nationwide strike over Maharashtra move to register CCMP-trained Homeopaths
stories.summary: In a letter to Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Wednesday, IMA Headquarters termed the government’s August 3 Government Resolution (GR) “illegal” and urged its immediate cancellation, arguing that it undermines medical education, violates established legal principles and poses a risk to public health. The IMA further pointed out that the issue is already pending before the Bombay high court.

stories.title: Nearly 2,000 RSS volunteers assist over 40,000 flood-affected families in Assam
stories.summary: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh volunteers aided over forty thousand families in Assam's flood-hit regions. They provided rescue, food, and essential supplies to affected villagers in three districts. Medical camps were organized by the organization in collaboration with the National Medicos Organization. Volunteers also assisted with post-flood rehabilitation, including cleaning and agricultural support. These efforts focused on helping communities recover after the recent devastating floods.

stories.title: Congress vs Congress in Punjab: With 'sleeper cell' warning, party puts Channi camp on notice
stories.summary: Amid rising infighting, the Congress party has issued a stern warning to Punjab's dissenters regarding their involvement with internal 'sleeper cells.' Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, the state president, has promised that party members acting against Congress will face consequences, with no tickets granted to them. The situation intensifies as Charanjit Singh Channi's supporters openly question the leadership, complicating the party's position in the face of a multi-dimensional electoral challenge in assembly elections early next year.

stories.title: Stacy Brooks expected to dislike downtown Minneapolis, but a one-year trial changed her mind
stories.summary: Stacy Brooks, originally from northern Minnesota, discovered a newfound happiness in her urban high-rise. After a year-long experiment, she and her husband are in the process of purchasing their 19th-floor apartment. Their daily routine transformed into leisurely walks, indulging in community amenities, and savoring a variety of local dining options. The supportive community of childfree neighbors further enhanced her experience, marking a significant departure from her previous suburban life.

stories.title: Row erupts as UK Conservatives allow man jailed for antisemitic abuse to contest local election
'Orchestrated spectacles': India rejects Pakistan's 'Youm-e-Istehsal' on revocation of Article 370
'Spewing venom to stay politically relevant': Owaisi hits back with 'chair-stool' jab at Keshav Maurya over madrassa remarks
Evening news wrap: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg apologises to Centre; Rahul Gandhi meets student protesters, targets PM Modi & more
stories.summary: Meta's CEO apologized to the Indian government regarding content moderation and platform issues. Rahul Gandhi met student protesters and criticized the Prime Minister and Home Minister. An India-flagged ship was hit and sank in the Red Sea, though its crew was rescued. Parliamentary affairs minister met Rahul Gandhi to discuss breaking the ongoing Parliament deadlock. Trump's immigration crackdown has reportedly detained parents of active-duty US military personnel.

stories.title: Meet Seungah Chung, the US eighth-grader who used 200 ants to discover landmark navigation
stories.summary: A bright young student embarked on a fascinating ant navigation experiment fueled by her natural curiosity. Through her meticulous research, she uncovered that ants primarily depend on visual markers for navigation. This groundbreaking project garnered her acclaim at a well-regarded science competition, showcasing the potential of such findings to inspire the development of innovative robots and autonomous systems.

stories.title: Texas uses discarded Christmas trees to help sea turtles survive
stories.summary: Discarded Christmas trees are repurposed to build sand dunes along the Texas coast. These trees are placed on beaches to trap shifting sand and strengthen the shoreline. This process occurs before the sea turtle nesting season begins each year. The new dunes provide a protective barrier for relocated sea turtle eggs. This initiative helps ensure a safer environment for hatchlings during their development.

stories.title: 'No need to apologise': Rahul meets student protesters, slams PM Modi, Shah over police brutality
Sambhal violence 2024: Probe panel claims unrest 'pre-planned', links Samajwadi MP, MLA
stories.summary: Last year, three-member panel had met the CM and submitted its report concerning the violence that erupted near the Shahi Jama Masjid on November 24 in 2024 during an ASI-monitored survey of the mosque. The unrest resulted in four fatalities and injuries to several others. In the document, a sharp demographic shift is observed.

stories.title: Trump's immigration crackdown hits US military families; over 50 spouses, parents detained
stories.summary: Dozens of parents and spouses of US service members face detention and deportation. This marks a significant shift from prior bipartisan immigration policies for military families. Many are detained during routine immigration status adjustment appointments. The Department of Homeland Security states military service does not exempt violations of immigration laws. These detentions negatively impact military readiness and family stability.

stories.title: California will close the westbound Zampa Bridge for 53 hours to replace part of its deck
stories.summary: Important notice for travelers: Westbound access on the Al Zampa Memorial Bridge will be entirely shut down for 53 hours, commencing on Friday, August 21, and concluding on Monday, August 24, to facilitate necessary repairs. Motorists are urged to anticipate heavy delays and to follow detour signs. Please be advised that foot and bicycle traffic will also be halted during this repair window. Prepare your travel plans accordingly.

stories.title: Jharkhand recruitment protests: CM Hemant Soren says 'action soon'; CJP extends support - top developments
'They told you twice they don't want you': Andy Burnham reveals wife's reaction to PM bid
Quote of the day by Mother Teresa: "I prefer you to make mistakes in kindness than…"
Rajya Sabha passes bill to increase number of SC judges, returns it to Lok Sabha
Secret winter ocean conveyor: Study tracks chlorophyll plunges to 1,000m; deep sea stores carbon
'Apologised to minister': Meta official on PM Modi post removal; Zuckerberg sorry for deepfakes
NYPD officer Rebecca DePaula dies after DR surgery; family seeks probe
Peace talks abroad, protests at home: The many contradictions shaping Pakistan today
Beyond Donations: How CSR Is Rewriting India’s Education Story
Quote of the day by Socrates: "The secret of happiness, you see, is not found in seeking more, but in…"
Cabinet secretary TV Somanathan, home secretary Govind Mohan get one-year extensions
Hawaii’s ancient island origins explain why it has no native snakes
stories.summary: Hawaii's unique volcanic history and geographic isolation effectively kept snakes from establishing themselves on the islands. This absence allowed native wildlife to flourish without the fear of snake predators. Unfortunately, accidental snake introductions, as evidenced by Guam's experiences, can wreak havoc. To combat this risk, Hawaii enforces strict regulations and vigilant monitoring to safeguard its delicate ecosystem and ensure the island's natural heritage endures.

stories.title: Experts used 'Judas goats' to hunt down their own kind, eliminating over 140,000 invasive goats in a $10.5 million mission
stories.summary: In a remarkable ecological initiative, over 140,000 invasive goats have been eradicated from three areas of the Galapagos Islands. This operation, costing $10.5 million, aims to rejuvenate the habitat for native wildlife. Using judas goats fitted with transmitters, conservationists pinpointed the remaining invaders. Following their removal, the area's native plants are thriving once again, supported by continuous monitoring and protective measures.

stories.title: 45,000-year-old crystal tool reveals Neanderthals valued beauty too
stories.summary: A remarkable find in France reveals a 45,000-year-old Neanderthal quartz scraper that changes the narrative around these ancient beings. This tool, crafted from rare rock crystal, highlights that Neanderthals had an appreciation for aesthetics and craftsmanship, challenging the notion of them as mere primitive beings. The sophistication in its creation suggests a deeper cultural understanding and skillful manipulation of their environment, offering insights into Neanderthal life and artistry.

stories.title: After losing both grandparents, 17-year-old Hudson Waters recreated their home in a backyard shed
stories.summary: Hudson Waters created a heartfelt replica of his grandparents' home in a backyard shed. He carefully filled the space with their furniture and cherished belongings. This personal project helped him cope with profound grief after their passing. The touching tribute has since resonated with thousands of people online. His story highlights the importance of preserving familiar spaces and family history.

stories.title: After disappearing for decades, seven beavers returned to California's Tule River and began restoring the landscape
stories.summary: Beavers have returned to Tule River Tribe lands after decades of absence. A family of seven beavers was released in June 2024 to restore the watershed. Their dams will slow water flow, creating wetlands and improving drought resilience. This reintroduction also supports threatened species and reconnects the Tribe to its heritage. The project demonstrates how one species can revitalize an entire landscape.

stories.title: 'Grave security threat': CJP's Saurav Das alleges media 'breaking into' his house
stories.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party began as a satirical online response to a statement by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant but later developed into a broader youth-led campaign. The movement has focused on issues including exam security, administrative reforms and employment-related concerns. Das became one of CJP's most visible representatives due to his background in journalism and his ability to present arguments through data, documents and legal references.

stories.title: 'Consumers paying more': Congress alleges E20 has tilted benefits towards ethanol producers
'No blanket ban on reporting': SC clarifies order restricting use of audio-video clips of court proceedings
Livestream captures giant iceberg flipping in Greenland’s Ilulissat Icefjord
'Remake of Dravidian model': Ex-Tamil Nadu CM MK Stalin calls Vijay government's budget a 'waste'
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu's opposition leader M.K. Stalin criticized the TVK government's budget as a waste. He stated the budget repackaged old schemes and lacked new vision. The finance minister presented a budget aiming for a $1.5 trillion economy by 2031. Opposition parties also pointed out unfulfilled election promises and debt concerns. The budget included allocations for schools, higher education, and welfare initiatives.

stories.title: Indian expat from Kerala killed in Dubai gas cylinder blast; colleague recalls moments before explosion
Singapore is planting one million trees to cool its streets
Scientists looking for giant trees in Taiwan discovered a hidden forest filled with some of East Asia's tallest trees
stories.summary: A team of researchers has uncovered remarkable giant temperate forests nestled within the mountains of Taiwan. Utilising airborne laser scanning technology, they identified towering conifers and age-old broadleaf trees that sequester substantial carbon, acting as crucial reserves for climate stability. As an outcome of Taiwan's challenging terrain, these ancient ecosystems have remained preserved for generations, underscoring the necessity of their conservation.

stories.title: Listen to youth, read, learn, understand Parliament: PM Modi guides newly elected BJP MPs on grassroots connectivity
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday hosted a breakfast meeting for newly elected BJP Rajya Sabha MPs and those who recently joined the party, during which he guided the parliamentarians on various issues and shared effective ways to connect with the youth.

stories.title: Mexican TikTok influencer Cesar Gastelum is shot dead during a livestream in Culiacan Sinaloa
stories.summary: Cesar Gastelum, a popular TikTok comedian from Mexico, was tragically killed during a livestream in Culiacan. While entertaining his audience, gunfire erupted as two individuals on a motorcycle targeted him. The shocking footage appears to show the assailant shooting. Known for his comedic prowess and a following of nearly 600,000, Gastelum’s death highlights the risks faced by online personalities.

stories.title: Seafarers’ union urges PM Modi to deploy Navy after Indian vessel sinks
In 2006, a tiny deep-reef fish was pulled from deep water off South Australia and misidentified; nearly 20 years later, scientists recognised a new species
stories.summary: A newly identified species of deep-reef fish, collected back in 2006, has intrigued scientists after spending nearly twenty years in a museum's vault due to a mix-up. A thorough re-examination unveiled unique physical traits that highlight the significance of museum collections in preserving and unveiling hidden biodiversity. This find serves as a reminder of the untapped potential awaiting discovery within scientific archives.

stories.title: Three American coasts are losing 84% of their wetlands to rising sea levels
stories.summary: As sea levels continue to rise at an alarming rate, coastal wetlands are facing unprecedented inundation. A staggering eighty-four percent of these essential ecosystems are currently experiencing loss on a national scale. The Gulf Coast wetlands are bearing the brunt of this crisis, largely due to human impact. Still, there’s hope—many wetlands could shift inland if space allows, highlighting the importance of concerted conservation efforts to preserve these invaluable habitats.

stories.title: Kolkata opens its doors after 19 years: Where does Taslima Nasreen go next?
stories.summary: Taslima Nasreen returned to Kolkata after nineteen years of exile and received a civic felicitation. The writer expressed gratitude for the new government's assurance of security and her right to visit. Her return highlights the city's evolving political landscape and its stance on free expression. The article explores whether this visit signifies a permanent homecoming or a ceremonial occasion.

stories.title: Japan's Nagoro village lost most of its people, replaced with life-size dolls
Mass crossing leaves nearly 1,000 migrant children stranded in Spain’s Ceuta
stories.summary: Thousands of people crossed into Spain's Ceuta enclave from Morocco, creating a sudden migration crisis. Many children arrived alone and became separated from their families during the chaotic journey. Spanish authorities struggled to provide shelter and care for the overwhelmed migrant support facilities. Families searched for missing relatives on the Moroccan side of the border after the crossing.

stories.title: What happened to Sydney Towle? TikToker’s brother shares heartbreaking cancer update
stories.summary: TikTok creator Sydney Towle has entered hospice care, according to an emotional update shared by her brother, Austin Towle. The 26-year-old influencer has openly documented her battle with rare bile duct cancer for years while continuing to inspire followers with hopeful messages. Her latest health update comes after months of treatment, a clinical trial, and her determination to keep believing that better days were still possible.

stories.title: Twitch streamer SukiMellow has police called on her after Apple Pay prank on elderly couple
stories.summary: Twitch streamer SukiMellow faced significant online backlash after a prank video surfaced. The video showed her startling an elderly woman with a loud notification sound. The frightened woman repeatedly called for police assistance and asked for her phone. Another concerned woman intervened and began recording the streamer's actions. SukiMellow and her cameraman then walked away laughing from the situation.

stories.title: Lok Sabha secretariat director found hanging in Noida flat; suicide note recovered
Scientists discover a new eyeless cavefish genus hidden for decades
Polish swimmer becomes the first person to swim from Sweden to Poland across the Baltic Sea in 55 hours
Scientists placed 42 sea sponges in a polluted Spanish port
How a faulty dam gate revealed a 2,400-year-old Turkish settlement
Parliament deadlock: Rijiju meets Rahul to break logjam; Shah may speak on FCRA bill
Grade 9 student wins gold for wearable that detects IV leaks early
Jharkhand student protest: Mahto takes water after Sonam Wangchuk's appeal, to continue hunger strike
stories.summary: After four days without food or water, Jharkhand student leader Devendra Nath Mahto drank water following an appeal from climate activist Sonam Wangchuk but said his indefinite fast over alleged irregularities in state recruitment examinations would continue.

stories.title: Lithops werneri: Tiny Namibian plant survives by disguising itself as a pebble
'Tread carefully': SC calls for restraint, dialogue in dealing with student protesters
Apologise in 3 days or face action: Parliament panel to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg
'Operation Eau de Fraud': Chicago YouTuber charged after replacing luxury perfumes with modeling clay
stories.summary: A YouTuber from Chicago has been charged in connection with an intricate perfume return fraud scheme. He allegedly swapped high-end fragrances for modeling clay and resealed packaging. During a search of his apartment, authorities confiscated hundreds of perfume bottles valued at approximately $250,000. The case was initiated after a luxury retailer flagged concerning returns of modified items, underscoring the escalating issue of return fraud in the retail sector.

stories.title: Brazil's Snake Island is home to just two snake species, including one of the world's most venomous pit vipers
stories.summary: Ilha da Queimada Grande, known as Snake Island, hosts a unique evolutionary marvel. This isolated Brazilian island is home to the critically endangered golden lancehead viper. Rising sea levels trapped snake ancestors, leading to remarkable adaptations over millennia. The island's extreme snake population results from isolation and a specialized bird diet. Access is restricted to protect both the snakes and researchers studying them.

stories.title: New Whale Stomach Bacteria Found: Scientists identify 3 Helicobacter genotypes
J&K, Ladakh have entered 'a decisive new chapter': PM Modi on Article 370 anniversary
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi marked seven years since the abrogation of Articles 370 and 35A. This move ushered in a new chapter for Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. The region has seen wide-ranging transformation and expanded opportunities for its citizens. Constitutional rights have been ensured for all, empowering previously marginalized communities. The government reaffirms its commitment to the progress of these regions.

stories.title: ‘Vile, abusive’: Bombay HC orders takedown of fake posts targeting Gadkari over E20 ethanol row
California’s western monarch migration hits third-lowest count at 12,260
stories.summary: This winter's survey of the western monarch butterfly revealed over 12,000 individuals, a small rise from last year. Despite this slight increase, conservationists remain alarmed as numbers are still critically low. Ongoing challenges such as habitat loss and environmental stressors severely impact the butterfly population. Conservation initiatives are actively working on restoring habitats and engaging the community in monitoring efforts.

stories.title: 'I'm Kalaignar's grandson, M K Stalin's son': Udhayanidhi hits back after release, shares photo
After Japan's devastating 2011 tsunami, volunteers have planted more than 680,000 trees to protect the coast from future tsunamis
stories.summary: In a remarkable effort to enhance its coastal protection, Japan is planting over 680,000 native trees through the Chinju no Mori Project. This initiative, which complements existing concrete seawalls established after the 2011 tsunami, employs the innovative Miyawaki Method. By drawing inspiration from ancient guardian forests, these new dense forests will not only serve as a natural barrier against disasters but also provide numerous ecological advantages.

stories.title: The insect that carries its own bomb: How the bombardier beetle turns chemistry into a weapon
stories.summary: Bombardier beetles possess a unique defense mechanism involving explosive chemical sprays. These insects mix chemicals to create a hot, noxious spray for protection. Their specialized internal structures allow them to survive these powerful self-inflicted explosions. Bombardier beetles can fire their chemical bombs multiple times before needing to escape. These fascinating insects have evolved remarkable adaptations for survival in various ecosystems.

stories.title: 'We'll know in 48 hours': Trump warns Iran to open Hormuz or get 'hit very hard'
Scientists prove Charles Darwin's 150-year-old theory right with the help of an insect-eating plant
stories.summary: A breakthrough in plant science has validated Charles Darwin's historic conjecture surrounding carnivorous Saxifraga species. Researchers discovered that these plants ensnare small gnats with sticky hairs, emitting fragrances that lure their prey. Chemical tests confirmed that insects provide essential nutrients upon capture, as showcased by isotope labeling. This pivotal finding sheds light on the complex interactions and nutritional strategies of plant carnivory in mountainous regions.

stories.title: Leonardo DiCaprio and Jeff Bezos unveil $200 million mission to save 100 endangered species
stories.summary: A new $200 million Phoenix Species Project will support 100 critically endangered species. This initiative is a collaboration between Re:wild and the Bezos Earth Fund. The project aims to provide significant financial backing for long-term recovery programs. It will bolster existing conservation efforts and expand habitat protection initiatives. Local organizations will receive crucial funding and technical assistance for their vital work.

stories.title: Scientists clone rare Queen of Sheba Orchid, growing 1,000 plants in five years
Day 12 of Jharkhand students' protest: Hemant Soren says govt taking exam row 'very seriously'
stories.summary: In response to mounting allegations of irregularities in recruitment exams, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren reassured students of a fair resolution under the law. He emphasized that investigations into reported paper leaks are already in progress by government agencies. Meanwhile, students persist in their protests, calling for exam cancellations and significant reforms. A final decision from the government will follow the completion of these investigations.

stories.title: Govt distances itself from Hasina event but Dhaka not convinced
stories.summary: India has firmly denied any role in Sheikh Hasina's forthcoming media address, while Dhaka expresses skepticism, worried that the address may jeopardize diplomatic ties. Meanwhile, Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has received an invitation to the Brics summit from India, but he may encounter domestic backlash concerning the extradition of Hasina. To date, Bangladesh has not officially responded to the Brics invitation.

stories.title: Russian drone chases Ukrainian vegetable seller in 'safari' attack - Watch
Govt dismisses reports of fuel quality issues, says checks on
'Contamination' in fuel, says SIAM, later retracts
Crew rescued after India-flagged ship hit by projectile sinks
West Bengal to fast-track land acquisition to take trains close to Doklam
stories.summary: West Bengal government has approved land acquisition for a new railway line. The new rail link will boost tourism in the Jhaldhaka-Bindu-Todey Tangta region. Railways and the forest department will conduct a joint survey after the monsoon. This strategically important project was previously stalled due to state government non-cooperation.

stories.title: Child rights body takes up with Meta issue of CSAM ads on Instagram
stories.summary: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights has taken action against Meta, prompted by allegations regarding s associated with child exploitation materials on its platforms. Seeking accountability, the commission requested clarification from Meta about these grave concerns. After assessing the company's response, a formal investigation is now underway. This decision aligns with growing attention on child safety practices across digital platforms.

stories.title: Cyber crime reports down from 1.2L in 2024 to 16,377 now: Government
stories.summary: Supreme Court urged prompt action against cyber fraudsters, while noting a reduction in incidents. Authorities were directed to expedite decisions on a 'kill switch' for phones. Monies transferred to mule accounts will be placed on hold by banks. Victims will receive recovered amounts expeditiously after investigations conclude. New directives aim to enhance cyber crime grievance redressal mechanisms.

stories.title: WA tests optional age verification pilot, says user privacy will be protected
stories.summary: To comply with the upcoming Digital Personal Data Protection Act, WhatsApp is piloting new privacy-focused age verification methods for Indian users. This initiative is completely voluntary, allowing users to choose their participation. With the new law's emphasis on stricter regulations for children's personal data, WhatsApp is taking care to safeguard user privacy during this important verification process.

stories.title: Government to grill Meta brass on child abuse, AI content
stories.summary: In an important meeting scheduled for this week, government officials will confront Meta executives regarding pressing issues. The discussions will center around the presence of child sexual abuse material, the rise of AI-created content, and the measures in place for takedowns involving notable personalities. Compliance with local laws and the efficiency of Meta's content moderation efforts, particularly in monitoring synthetic content, are also poised to be key topics of concern.

stories.title: Government may allow fees on UPI payment above Rs 2,000
stories.summary: The government may allow a small charge on UPI payments exceeding two thousand rupees. This levy would apply to transactions made to businesses and not individuals. Official estimates suggest this change will impact only five percent of all UPI transactions. Most daily purchases like groceries and taxi fares will remain unaffected by this potential fee. Industry experts anticipate a possible ceiling on the absolute amount charged for these transactions.

stories.title: Over 30 operatives killed by 'Indian agents' since 2020: LeT commander
stories.summary: Rizwan Hanif, a commander affiliated with Lashkar-e-Taiba, has alleged that Indian agents have systematically killed more than thirty individuals in different Pakistani locations since 2020. He characterized these murders as acts of religious persecution and rejected the authority of foreign entities. This statement comes amid heightened rhetoric from Pakistan's military, and experts suggest it serves as a strategic narrative amidst rising tensions.

stories.title: Computer-based NEET? Govt tells SC decision after Nilekani report
stories.summary: The government informed the Supreme Court about considering NEET's shift to computer-based testing. This decision awaits the Nandan Nilekani task force's report on public examination systems. Measures are being taken to make the exam more secure and prevent unfair means. The National Testing Agency has already moved seven major exams to computer-based formats. NEET (UG) currently remains the only major pen-and-paper examination conducted by the NTA.

stories.title: '100% pure'? Stop misleading products' sale, FSSAI tells Dabur
stories.summary: Dabur India has been instructed by the FSSAI to halt the sale of items claiming to be '100% pure.' This decision stems from a violation of food regulations deemed misleading to consumers. The FSSAI identified unauthorized organic claims on various products. Despite Dabur's assertion that its labels meet regulatory standards, the company will eliminate '100%' references from its marketing efforts.

stories.title: Census phase 2 likely to accept half-filled forms
stories.summary: Census authorities are considering allowing partially filled online forms for self-enumeration. This change aims to ease the process for respondents and enumerators alike. Previously, blank fields prevented form submission, discouraging self-enumeration. The population enumeration exercise is scheduled nationwide for February 2027. Select snow-bound regions will conduct enumeration earlier, from September 1 to 30.

stories.title: Tie compensation to functional disability, says SC
stories.summary: Gives ₹83.3L To Road Crash Victim

stories.title: Government: 20 died in heatstrokes across 4 states
BJP uses skit as ammo, claims 'insult' to Hinduism
274 fugitives brought back from 36 nations since 2019
stories.summary: Government brought back 274 fugitives from 36 countries since 2019. Assets worth over Rs 17,874 crore were attached during this period. This contrasts with the UPA government's record of fewer extraditions annually. Legal frameworks were updated, and diplomatic efforts intensified for fugitive recovery. This approach reflects a coordinated "whole of government" strategy for justice.

stories.title: BJP attacks Cong 'double standards' on students stirs
stories.summary: The BJP has called out the Congress party for its hypocritical stance on examination irregularities. They pointed to the Congress's lack of response to student protests in both Jharkhand and Karnataka. Additionally, the BJP criticized Priyank Kharge for his defense of police action against demonstrators, claiming that the opposition is purposefully causing disruption in Parliament over these issues. The BJP argues that this selective outrage stems from political motivations.

stories.title: Rajya Sabha clears birth, death regn bill without any discussion
stories.summary: Oppn Protests Continue To Disrupt House

stories.title: Govt dismisses reports of fuel quality issues, says checks on
Day after PK's poll win, PM Modi talks to Nabin, meets Nitish
stories.summary: During a recent NDA meeting, government officials emphasized the importance of economic growth and the creation of jobs. The event also saw discussions surrounding India's evolving sports landscape. Prime Minister Modi and Amit Shah were present, and a humorous exchange between Modi and Nitin Nabin generated buzz among the MPs. Subsequently, Modi held discussions with former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar and his JDU associates.

stories.title: US Congressman warns FCRA Bill could affect India-US ties
56% of vehicles not insured, SC says challan them
stories.summary: Court Also Suggests Such Vehicles Be Denied Fuel

stories.title: Florida tests exposed endangered Caribbean corals to predatory bacteria; over half resisted spread
stories.summary: In the Caribbean, researchers are exploring the use of predatory bacteria as a means to combat coral diseases. Laboratory tests have demonstrated that these microscopic bacteria can successfully eliminate harmful Vibrio bacteria while preserving the coral's vital microbiome. This promising method provides a focused mechanism to defend corals against disease. However, additional field trials are necessary for its application in conservation efforts.

stories.title: An illinois family gave its old farmhouse for firefighters to train inside before it burned
stories.summary: A four-generation family farmhouse in Illinois was given a meaningful final purpose before being demolished. The Kestel family donated the vacant house to the New Lenox Fire Protection District, where nearly 100 firefighters trained in realistic live-fire rescue and firefighting exercises over three days. Although watching the home burn was emotional, the family said knowing it helped firefighters gain life-saving experience made its final farewell a fitting tribute to their family's legacy of community service.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Warren Buffett: 'Look for the job you would take if you didn't need a job' and timeless career advice
From launch to data, tech to Isro facility, pvt firms to get 30-100% subsidy
stories.summary: New government schemes will offer significant financial support to Indian private space companies. These initiatives aim to boost domestic launch capabilities and global competitiveness for businesses. Subsidies will cover launch services, technology transfer, and access to ISRO facilities. The programs are designed to lower entry barriers and accelerate private sector growth. This support will make satellite data and infrastructure more affordable for Indian entities.

stories.title: For every Rs 100 India spends on R&D, govt gives Rs 48, pvt Rs 45
stories.summary: The balance of research and development funding has shifted, with government and private industry now investing nearly the same amount. In recent years, private sector contributions to research have seen a notable rise. Government spending is concentrated on sectors deemed strategic and beneficial to the public. Additionally, multinational corporations are increasingly influential in shaping India's research environment, although the overall research intensity still lags behind other major economies.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Chandrika Kumaratunga: 'Power is a joke, but it gives me the authority to do what I think I need to do for the country'
US saw 2,562 woodwasp interceptions (1952–2020); wood packaging was the main pathway
stories.summary: Wooden packaging serves as the primary channel for introducing woodwasps across the globe. A thorough investigation reviewed decades of border inspection data from three different nations. Findings revealed that almost all interceptions were associated with pallets, crates, and other dunnage utilized in shipping. The evolution of trade routes has affected the source of these intercepted woodwasp species. Consequently, maintaining international regulations on wooden packaging is vital for enhancing biosecurity initiatives.

stories.title: China's tree patches restored forests, but reached only 19–30% of natural diversity in 20 years
stories.summary: A 20-year study in southwest China found that planting small patches of native trees can help restore damaged tropical forests without planting entire landscapes. The approach successfully rebuilt forest cover, but researchers found that biodiversity and mature forest conditions recovered much more slowly, showing that long-term restoration still requires sustained effort.

stories.title: Big clean energy milestone: NPCIL cumulatively generates over 1,000 bn units of N-power, avoids 860 million tons of CO2 emissions
stories.summary: India has achieved a remarkable milestone in clean energy, generating over one thousand billion units from nuclear power. This achievement helps avoid more than 860 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions. The government aims to increase nuclear power capacity to 100 GW by 2047, with an intermediate target of 22 GW by 2031-32. This expansion will involve multiple stakeholders and the introduction of new legislation.

stories.title: MPs feel left out of foundation stone laying, parliamentary panel steps in
stories.summary: A parliamentary panel has called attention to the frequent exclusion of MPs from events related to rural road schemes. To rectify this, the committee has urged the introduction of mandatory invitations for MPs to ceremonies. Additionally, it proposed uploading high-quality photos showcasing MP involvement online. A quarterly system will be implemented to monitor adherence to these protocols, ensuring that the established parliamentary etiquette is upheld for PMGSY projects.

stories.title: Egyptian doctor wrongly connects organ in a way that bowel waste is channeled back to stomach, UK cancels his licence
Terror suspects spotted, search ops launched in J&K’s Poonch
stories.summary: Following intelligence indicating potential terror suspects in Poonch, security forces have launched coordinated operations in two strategic locations. Reports have confirmed sightings near Gujjar Naar and Kherowali dhok, prompting a thorough search in the isolated Dhara Sangla village by army and police units. As of Tuesday evening, no contact with the suspects has been reported. Earlier, a significant search initiative was executed in the Thanamandi area of Rajouri district.

stories.title: Experts warn great white sharks are 'already lurking off UK beaches' and another toothy predator could follow
stories.summary: With rising ocean temperatures, great white sharks are migrating further north than ever documented. Researchers suggest that these formidable predators might already be silently exploring British waters. This phenomenon signifies a broader ecological crisis, forcing various marine species to adapt their hunting and migration patterns in response to shifting sea temperatures, highlighting the urgent need for conservation efforts.

stories.title: Scientists identified seven new diamond frog species in Madagascar after a 12-year search
stories.summary: Scientists have identified seven new diamond frog species in Madagascar. These discoveries highlight the island's extensive undocumented wildlife and hidden diversity. Modern genetic tools and traditional anatomy revealed evolutionary differences previously unseen. Many of these frogs inhabit small, isolated ranges, emphasizing conservation needs. This finding underscores Madagascar's ongoing biological mysteries and the importance of habitat protection.

stories.title: Vaishno Devi fake silver row: Court seeks detailed probe report, orders evidence preservation
stories.summary: The Jammu Chief Judicial Magistrate has taken decisive action by ordering the preservation of evidence in a troubling case of fake silver offerings amounting to Rs 550 crore. In response to a petition seeking to secure all relevant physical and electronic evidence, the court acknowledged allegations of adulteration and pilferage concerning around twenty tonnes of silver.

stories.title: NC, PDP announce protest plans; BJP to celebrate Article 370 abrogation
stories.summary: Kashmir's political landscape will witness separate protests from the NC and PDP this Wednesday, marking seven years since Article 370 was abrogated. The NC is pushing for the restoration of its statehood, whereas the PDP demands the reinstatement of Article 370. Meanwhile, BJP's celebratory events, including a Tiranga rally from Lal Chowk, suggest a contrasting narrative on the changes in Jammu and Kashmir's sentiments following the abrogation.

stories.title: After opening golf tournament, CM Omar says authorities must not allow repeat of migrant worker killings
stories.summary: Omar Abdullah, the chief minister of Jammu and Kashmir, strongly condemned the recent violence against migrant laborers, emphasizing that such acts are unacceptable and calling for heightened security measures. He also underscored the significance of golf tournaments as a means to boost tourism in the area, recalling a time when these events were a hallmark of Kashmir's serene landscape, well before militancy took root.

stories.title: CPI (ML) L whose students wing was at forefront of Gen Z protests wants voting age lowered to 16
Rooftop solar scheme crosses 50-lakh household mark
Over 170 migrants rescued after Channel boat catches fire; UK says 'all will be returned' to France
Why vultures can eat rotten meat without getting sick
US built a neighbourhood upon 22,000 tons of buried toxic waste, then children began returning home with burns
stories.summary: Originally designed to be a groundbreaking canal project, this site succumbed to a fate of pollution as industrial and municipal waste accumulated over decades. The catastrophic rainfall in 1976 triggered the release of these harmful chemicals into nearby homes, displacing numerous families. This incident catalyzed the formation of the Superfund program, dedicated to remedying toxic environmental disasters across the nation.

stories.title: Indian cargo vessel sinks after attack in Yemeni waters; all 14 crew rescued
US judge blocks New York's ban on ICE officers wearing face masks
EU eyes tougher border controls after Ceuta migrant surge triggers alarm
stories.summary: European Union ministers are demanding stricter measures against migrant smuggling networks. They also seek stronger return policies following a large influx into Ceuta. The bloc is enhancing border security and intelligence sharing with external partners. Disinformation by smugglers fueled the unprecedented migration surge into the Spanish enclave. This crisis has reignited divisions within the European Union over migration management.

stories.title: Gaza mass funeral for 112 Palestinians, including dozens of children, recovered from 2023 strike
New rules for US citizenship: Trump administration wants new educational requirement for naturalization
Child protection panel launches inquiry into Meta over alleged child sexual abuse material ads
stories.summary: The NCPCR has initiated a formal investigation following alarming claims from a BBC report which suggested that s on Meta’s platforms like Instagram were linked to the promotion of child abuse material. In response, the child rights organization has demanded clarity from Meta Platforms Inc. Furthermore, the NHRC has instructed the Delhi Police to look into these troubling assertions, as both entities scrutinize Meta's adherence to child protection regulations.
