stories.title: ‘No insurance, no fuel’: SC directs govt to prepare pilot project, flags 16.54 crore uninsured vehicles
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has initiated a pilot project that connects fuel supply to the vehicle's insurance status, aiming to enhance adherence to mandatory third-party insurance laws. Additionally, the court has extended the insurance requirement period for new vehicles, intending to ensure that accident victims receive prompt compensation. Monitoring compliance will be supported by automatic number plate recognition cameras.

stories.title: ‘Will give fitting reply at appropriate time’: Sunetra Pawar on Congress’ ‘gungi gudiya’ jibe
IShowSpeed criticizes Diamond Gym’s "fatigue maxxing" after seeing 300 burpees before workout
stories.summary: IShowSpeed, the internet sensation, recently shared his thoughts on a trending clip from Diamond Gym. He expressed concern over the gym’s rigorous practice of performing 300 burpees before workouts. Known as 'fatigue maxxing', this method aims for maximum exhaustion. Diamond Gym has gained notoriety for its extreme training styles, and Speed's critique has sparked new discussions surrounding these intense fitness trends.

stories.title: 75-country Green Card ban illegal, rules Indian-American judge Amit Mehta; DHS says Trump upholding highest standards
Study finds 84% of U.S. coastal wetlands sinking as seas rise
Toxic plants yield enzymes that could power future medicines
'Good precedent': Kangana Ranaut backs police action against Udhayanidhi Stalin for crass remark
B.C. restores 70 hectares as Cowichan marsh faces 60% loss by 2100
stories.summary: British Columbia invests $500,000 in a large-scale Cowichan Estuary restoration project. This initiative aims to strengthen watershed health and improve climate resilience for the region. The project focuses on rebuilding vital habitat for fish and wildlife populations. Indigenous stewardship is central, guiding land use and planting culturally significant species. This significant effort protects biodiversity and supports local communities dependent on the estuary.

stories.title: Farmers back ethanol in meeting with agriculture minister, say it will boost income, secure energy
Uttarakhand CM Dhami welcomes Kanwariyas in Haridwar, inaugurates health camp amid Kanwar Yatra
stories.summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Tuesday welcomed Kanwariyas arriving in Haridwar for the annual Kanwar Yatra, showering flower petals on Shiva devotees from a helicopter and washing the feet of five pilgrims as a mark of respect.

stories.title: “Extinct” snail returns—1,000 reintroduced to Norfolk Island after 30 years
stories.summary: Campbell's keeled glass snails have reached a major conservation milestone on Norfolk Island. Over one thousand critically endangered snails have now been released onto the island. This marks a significant comeback after the species was presumed lost for decades. The successful recovery program involved extensive collaboration and captive breeding efforts. Researchers will continue monitoring the snails to ensure population growth and survival.

stories.title: SC calls to 'dismantle' ‘men’s clubs’ in Bar Councils, orders co-option of 2 women members
Archaeologists uncover 600-year-old saint statue beneath Berlin's oldest district
stories.summary: Excavations in Berlin's Molkenmarkt uncovered medieval religious artefacts from the 14th and 15th centuries. These discoveries include well-preserved saint figurines and a Madonna and Child sculpture. An extraordinary cache of ceramic figures containing human bone fragments was also found. These finds offer fresh evidence of devotional practices in medieval urban life. The discoveries contribute to understanding medieval Berlin and its spiritual traditions.

stories.title: From Hype To Help: How AI Is Solving India's Real Problems
stories.summary: India is harnessing the power of artificial intelligence to address its various developmental challenges effectively. In educational settings, AI supports teachers in remote areas, while in agriculture, it assists farmers facing changing climate conditions. The healthcare system is being transformed through AI-driven diagnostics, and access to government services is increasing. Furthermore, AI contributes to strengthening climate resilience and streamlining agricultural loan assessments, prompting significant investments in the necessary infrastructure.

stories.title: Security on high alert in Jammu & Kashmir: Pakistani drone sighted in Kathua, anti-terror search intensifies in Poonch
stories.summary: A Pakistani drone was spotted over Kathua's Hiranagar sector, prompting a security search. Security forces also conducted a large anti-terror operation in Poonch district. An unexploded mortar shell was recovered from a house in Kathua. These events occur amid heightened tensions along the India-Pakistan border. India stated it will safeguard its national interests as needed.

stories.title: Meet Darshan Magdum, Indian member of US boy band, who finally gets O-1 visa and the Internet is behind it
Iran war depletes US missile stocks, raises concerns over readiness for China
Delhi SIR dates extended: BLO visits till August 17, final rolls on October 27
How the US army built the 1,500-mile Alaska Highway in just 8 months
Hidden for 2,000 years, this Egyptian tomb held 560 ushabti figurines meant to serve the dead in the afterlife
stories.summary: Excavations at Tell Quesna have revealed a remarkable funerary complex adorned with hundreds of burial artifacts. Among the treasures, archaeologists discovered 560 ushabti figurines, believed to assist the deceased in the afterlife. Additional finds included protective amulets and pottery, with imported items from Rhodes highlighting trade links with the Mediterranean. These artifacts significantly enhance our knowledge of ancient Egyptian spiritual beliefs and rituals.

stories.title: When Jeff Bezos asked his team to help after a rainforest charity saving the Amazon said it was blocked from using 'Amazon' in Google Ads
What is 'Operation Fortress'? Reform UK's military plan to stop migrants crossing English Channel
'RSS involvement in Sainik Schools increasing', says Rahul Gandhi; Parl panel chief demands evidence
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi alleged increasing RSS involvement in Sainik Schools during a committee meeting. He referred to a media report while making his claim to the panel. The committee chair asked Rahul Gandhi to provide supporting documents for his allegations. Other BJP members also questioned the basis of his statements. Gandhi has previously accused the RSS of capturing public institutions.

stories.title: ‘Why the hurry?' Punjab Assembly opposes E20 policy, alleges Centre acted under US pressure
stories.summary: Punjab's Assembly passed a resolution opposing the Centre's E20 fuel policy. Concerns were raised about potential vehicle damage from the higher ethanol blend. The state questioned the accelerated rollout and alleged external pressure influenced the decision. The Aam Aadmi Party is campaigning nationwide against the policy. They demand consumer choice and lower prices for the blended fuel.

stories.title: How John Beal transformed polluted Hamm Creek into a thriving salmon habitat
stories.summary: John Beal, a dedicated Vietnam veteran, took it upon himself to revive Seattle's Hamm Creek, which had suffered from pollution. His approach included removing trash and reintroducing native plants to restore the ecosystem. By founding I'M A PAL, Beal rallied local volunteers and secured necessary funding, reigniting community passion. His perseverance has led to Hamm Creek's reintegration with the Duwamish River, fostering rich wildlife and ensuring a lasting ecological legacy.

stories.title: Udhayanidhi Stalin arrest drama: 'No double meaning in my speech; TN CM using diversion tactic,' says DMK leader - top developments
stories.summary: Udhayanidhi Stalin faced arrest over alleged remarks linked to actor Trisha. The Madras High Court directed his release on station bail after questioning. DMK workers staged protests across Tamil Nadu following the arrest. The TVK government and opposition engaged in a war of words. Udhayanidhi denied allegations and stated his remarks were distorted.

stories.title: Only 4 companies? Critics say barring small companies from hiring H-1B for 1-2 years is not enough
'Madrassa pass-outs develop terrorist-like mindset': UP deputy CM Keshav Maurya
stories.summary: Speaking to reporters at Vidhan Bhavan, Maurya alleged that madrassa students do not express patriotic slogans and linked their education to extremism. "Anyone who receives a madrassa education does not chant 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' nor sing 'Vande Mataram', and develops a terrorist-like mindset," he was quoted as saying by news agency PTI. The remarks were strongly criticised by senior Samajwadi Party leader Shivpal Yadav.

stories.title: California's Ranch fire burned 459,123 acres; 8 years later, 71,000 seedlings have been planted
stories.summary: Eight years after California's devastating Ranch Fire burned more than 459,000 acres, the US Forest Service and partner organisations planted 71,000 conifer seedlings in just eight days. The reforestation effort is part of a long-term plan to restore damaged forest, reduce future wildfire risk and support natural recovery across the Mendocino National Forest.

stories.title: How people in Chile's Atacama Desert evolved to survive drinking arsenic-poisoned water
Scientists discover Greenland sharks can see for centuries, debunking blindness myth
stories.summary: Recent studies reveal that Greenland sharks possess well-preserved visual systems that can last for centuries, challenging the previous notion that they were nearly blind. Research shows that their eyes are uniquely suited for low-light environments, demonstrating impressive adaptability. Scientists found healthy rod cells and active genes responsible for light detection, indicating these sharks have a remarkable ability to maintain their eyesight throughout their extended lifespans.

stories.title: Dordoi Bazaar: Shipping container market to commercial heart of Central Asia
'Private media entity organising it': Govt says 'no role' in Sheikh Hasina's proposed August 5 event
stories.summary: The MEA stated no government involvement in a private media event. The proposed forum concerns former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Bangladesh sought clarification from India regarding its support for the event. Hasina resigned in August 2024 and has been living in Delhi. She faces a death sentence for crimes against humanity.

stories.title: 'Insult to nation': Mamata attacks BJP over Netaji remarks, alleges pressure on TMC leaders
'Who is PM Modi to forgive?' Rahul says students 'need apology not forgiveness'
stories.summary: In an Instagram video posted on Friday night PM said that he will forgive young protesters accused of abusing him and his late mother, saying they are misguided children and it is “our job to show them the right way” “Nothing is more painful than seeing a parent grieve their child. Behind every young life lost is a family carrying pain that will never leave them - and serious questions about a broken education system,” Gandhi said in a post on X where he also shared images of his interaction with parents and students.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Giorgia Meloni: "To the women of this nation I want to say that being underestimated is a great advantage, because…”
North Carolina man worked 100-hour weeks for 58 years to save a bankrupt boat company, rejected a $400 million offer and gave it to charity
SC orders nationwide action against 'digital arrest' scams; tells RBI to share SOP on 'mule accounts'
'Answered public discontent with bullets and repression': MEA slams Pakistan over 'farce' PoK polls
stories.summary: In a strong statement, the Ministry of External Affairs demanded action against cross-border terrorism, directly targeting groups like Lashkar-e-Taiba following claims about Indian agencies taking down their commanders. They lambasted the local elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir as illegitimate, citing repression of civilians by Pakistani forces. Moreover, India urged the global community to address Pakistan's actions firmly.

stories.title: 'Will do whatever is necessary for national interest': India after Pakistan deploys 250 Chinese Howitzers
stories.summary: India stated it will protect national interests after Pakistan deployed Chinese artillery guns. Pakistan has reportedly deployed around 250 Chinese-made SH-15 artillery systems. India criticized Pakistan's recent elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir as a farce. The spokesperson noted civilian deaths during a crackdown in the region. Both nations continue to modernize their respective artillery capabilities.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: Madras HC orders Udhayanidhi's release after arrest over 'double meaning' remark; flyers injured as Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight encounters turbulence & more
Travel planning India's most underappreciated vacation task: Survey
Scottish biotech company turned whisky waste into a source of omega-3
Scientists find slugs, beetles and crabs help spread seeds for 186 plant species
'Gungi gudiya' row: NCP workers barge into Maharashtra Congress office over remark on deputy CM Sunetra Pawar — watch
'Decisions at appropriate time': Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren breaks silence on recruitment row amid protests
stories.summary: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren addressed recruitment row concerns seriously. Protesting job aspirants demand an independent probe into examination irregularities. The state CID investigation is gathering pace with several arrests made. Former CM Raghubar Das urged dialogue and a CBI inquiry for justice. The indefinite sit-in continues, with protesters vowing to escalate their agitation.

stories.title: Biodiversity boosts forest growth; loss could cut gains 17% by 2050
'Sadhu-saint not involved': CM Yogi on Ram Mandir donation theft case
stories.summary: Addressing reporters, CM Yogi said said the initial SIT report had not found any involvement of religious figures in the alleged theft of offerings made at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple. "No involvement of any sadhu-saint was found in the SIT's initial report in the case related to the alleged embezzlement of offerings (chadhava) at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple," he said.

stories.title: More than 330,000 gallons of rotting fish sauce in a Canadian town are finally being removed after 20 years of unbearable stench
Quote of the day by Princess Diana: "Don't call me an icon. I'm just a mother trying to…"
How Korea's Haenyeo developed extraordinary cold resistance that lets them dive into near-freezing seas without oxygen tanks, even in their 70s
When wildfires make their own weather: As France sees its first fire cloud, should India be worried?
stories.summary: France witnessed its first pyrocumulonimbus fire cloud event in July 2026. This phenomenon occurs when intense wildfires create their own thunderstorms. India's rising temperatures and dry spells increase forest fire frequency. While India has not reported fire clouds, its forests are becoming more flammable. The Himalayan pine belt presents the highest potential for such an event in India.

stories.title: Andrew Tate's lawyer warns Trump of political fallout if he doesn't help jailed influencer in UK extradition case
How Felix Dennis launched a 10 million-tree vision to restore England's woodlands
stories.summary: Felix Dennis began planting a small wood in 1996, which grew into the Heart of England Forest. This project aimed to restore native broadleaf trees across South Warwickshire. The charity was established in 2003 to continue purchasing and planting land. Dennis envisioned 25,000 acres of woodland open to the public. After his death in 2014, the forest has expanded significantly.

stories.title: Scientists discover four dangerous fish bacteria in Brazil for the first time; one has jumped to a new host species
stories.summary: For the first time, Brazil faces a significant challenge as bacteria previously exclusive to Asia and the USA have been identified within its borders. These bacteria, known to cause columnaris disease, pose an acute risk to the thriving aquaculture sector. Researchers have isolated four species from the Flavobacterium genus, which can infect both Nile tilapia and indigenous fish species.

stories.title: Arrested Jaish suspect surveyed area near CM Suvendu Adhikari's residence: Official
'Many friends yet to return': Patna students restart protest over NEET stir crackdown
stories.summary: The demonstrators demanded immediate release of all students still in jail and the withdrawal of criminal cases registered against those arrested during the statewide agitation. "We want a verified list of those who have been released from jail and those who are still behind bars after being arrested during the protests," one of the protesters said. A student activist from Siwan also alleged excessive use of force during earlier protests.

stories.title: Ancient Roman women left more than 120 inscriptions inside a hidden cave in Spain dedicated to a mysterious goddess
Scientists warn Earth could hit the 1.5°C climate limit sooner than expected
stories.summary: Global warming has significantly accelerated, with the past decade warming faster than any comparable period. Researchers removed natural climate fluctuations to reveal this underlying warming trend. Five major global temperature datasets confirm this acceleration with high statistical confidence. This observed increase suggests the world may approach key climate thresholds sooner. The long-term trend could cross the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C limit before this decade ends.

stories.title: Iran won't escalate tensions but will defend itself, says Pezeshkian amid Trump's warning
stories.summary: Iran states it will defend its security while the US president claims a last chance for a deal. Conflicting reports emerge regarding ongoing negotiations between Iran and the United States. Shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz remains subdued amid these diplomatic claims. Iran's IRGC reportedly launched a drone attack on a US military base in Kuwait. Tehran also prepared retaliatory strikes on Ukraine after a vessel incident.

stories.title: Madras HC orders Udhayanidhi Stalin's release after arrest over 'double meaning' remark
World's oldest amber has been found in China, and it is 65 million years older than expected
stories.summary: In a remarkable discovery, scientists uncovered ancient amber specimens in China that are approximately 385 million years old. This significant find pushes the amber fossil record back by an impressive sixty-five million years. It indicates that early vascular plants may have developed advanced resin-producing capabilities, which could have provided a defensive advantage against wildfires and fungal diseases. The research advances our understanding of plant resilience during the Devonian era.

stories.title: Countries with most black mambas: From South Africa to Kenya, where the deadly snake is found
stories.summary: The black mamba, often cited as the most dangerous snake on the African continent, occupies a wide array of habitats. This snake thrives in arid savannas and rocky terrains throughout sub-Saharan Africa. Countries such as South Africa and Zimbabwe frequently report incidents of black mamba bites. Remarkably, sightings have increased in Kenya and Zambia at higher altitudes, with Tanzania and Botswana also within its expansive territory.

stories.title: Scientists in Iceland are turning carbon dioxide into stone by injecting it into volcanic rock, and it could redefine the fight against climate change
Europe's shrinking rivers have hit shipping, power and tourism
stories.summary: Record low water levels in Europe's major rivers are disrupting electricity production, cargo transport and business operations as heatwaves and drought continue across the continent. Nuclear and hydropower plants have cut output, shipping on the Danube and Rhine has slowed, and companies are reporting lower earnings, highlighting the growing economic impact of prolonged extreme weather

stories.title: Long before GPS, Polynesian sailors crossed the Pacific by reading stars, waves, winds, birds and clouds
Sudden drop in altitude: Flyers injured as Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight encounters turbulence
Mark Zuckerberg's wife invested $125 million in a school for the disadvantaged; now she is closing it to focus on AI
stories.summary: The Primary School, offering tuition-free education to low-income families, has officially closed, impacting around 540 children who depended on its support. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, the school's benefactor, is redirecting its resources towards biotechnology and artificial intelligence. As part of its commitment, it has announced substantial funding aimed at assisting affected students and local organizations.

stories.title: Rose-ringed parakeets: From escaped pets to one of the most recognisable birds
AAP protest E20 petrol policy: Kejriwal, Sisodia stage sit-in after march to PM Modi's residence stopped
stories.summary: Delhi Police stopped Arvind Kejriwal and AAP leaders marching to Prime Minister Modi's residence. The party staged a sit-in protest on Firoz Shah Road after being prevented from proceeding. They carried over 2.30 lakh petitions against the Centre's E20 petrol policy. Kejriwal stated the government should listen to vehicle owners' concerns about the fuel.

stories.title: HC to FDA: Why was license suspended despite 100% compliance? Who will pay for losses?
'Promoting enmity, provoking riot': What are the 9 charges against Udhayanidhi Stalin over Trisha remarks
Centre summons Meta's global team on August 5-6 to raise CSAM, AI concerns
'I will fight tooth and nail': Brewery owner who offered free beer if Trump died, loses licence
stories.summary: Kirk Bangstad, owner of Wisconsin's Minocqua Brewing Company, has vowed to "fight tooth and nail" after the state revoked his brewery's operating permits. The action follows allegations that the company illegally transported beer from Illinois without the required permits or paying taxes. Bangstad, whose brewery previously made headlines for promising free beer if Donald Trump died, called the revocation an "absurd act of heavy-handedness" and plans to appeal.

stories.title: Cocaine worth 1,002 lbs found hidden in rebar truck at California border
stories.summary: Federal officers seized more than $20 million in cocaine hidden beneath the floorboards of a commercial truck carrying 269 bundles of rebar at California’s Calexico border crossing, arresting the driver after finding 366 packages of narcotics.

stories.title: UK pilot spots mysterious 'flying saucer' just 100 feet from passenger plane near Gatwick Airport; officials say the near miss reduced the aircraft's safety
Cancelled experiment: Britain tried to test a balloon that could cool the planet
Russia downs 320 drones: Six killed, warehouses damaged in Moscow, St Petersburg
stories.summary: Russia’s defence ministry said it brought down or destroyed 320 Ukrainian drones across 19 regions overnight, as governors reported six people killed, nine injured and warehouses damaged near Moscow and St Petersburg.

stories.title: 'Did I say anything wrong?' Udhayanidhi Stalin's first reaction after detention over 'vulgar' remark
A rare yellow-flowered California plant unseen since 1957 has been rediscovered
'Resignations are part of politics': DKS on two Congress MLAs quitting over Karnataka cabinet snub

Meet Jo Nagai: 10-year-old Japanese student who discovered butterflies can remember their time as caterpillars after he noticed that the caterpillars he had raised to recognise him after turning into butterflies
Video of dolphin carrying its dead newborn through the Indian Ocean reveals a deep and old 'mourning ritual'
stories.summary: Fraggle, a grieving mother dolphin, carried her deceased calf for six days, a poignant testament to her profound maternal love. Captured by drone footage in the Indian Ocean, this heart-wrenching scene revealed the support of her pod, which gathered around her in solidarity during her mourning. This behavior, seen in over twenty cetacean species, underscores their intricate social connections and possible awareness of mortality.

stories.title: Volunteers spent 40 days inside a French cave believing only 30 days had passed
Justice Manmohan Singh Liberhan, who probed Babri Masjid demolition, dies at 87
CRPF officer kills two colleagues, injures one before killing self in Assam
Most ancient Arctic carbon entering the ocean gets buried
‘Two sides of same coin’: Netaji’s grandnephew Chandra Bose quits TMC, takes swipe at BJP
'Long history of unlawful violence': Global watchdogs condemn Pakistan's crackdown in PoK
stories.summary: International oversight bodies are sounding the alarm over growing violence and restrictions on media freedom during elections. Amnesty International has documented harsh actions against protesters in PoK's Rawalakot, and the Committee to Protect Journalists has identified worsening conditions for reporters. Alarmingly, two independent journalists are reportedly missing after being abducted from their office, with the protest movement accounting for more than eighty fatalities.

stories.title: WhatsApp puts multiple accounts under review, temporarily blocks access for users
Indian agents killed over 30 LeT operatives in Pakistan since 2020, claims Lashkar leader
Govt proposes mandatory Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication systems from Oct 2028 to cut road crashes
21 Bangladesh nationals detained in J&K’s Ramban
stories.summary: Twenty-one Bangladesh nationals were detained in Ramban district last week. Officials are questioning them to learn who facilitated their movement. The group was caught moving in two vehicles during a checking drive. None of them could produce valid identity or travel documents. Investigators are probing if any network assisted these illegal immigrants.

stories.title: Mortar shells found in Poonch border villages
J&K: Days after Kulgam terror attack, man with grenade held in Pulwama
stories.summary: A suspect was apprehended in Pulwama carrying a hand grenade and anti-national posters. This arrest occurred during a security operation following recent migrant worker killings. Authorities booked the local man under stringent anti-terror laws, including the UAPA. Security forces are increasing patrols and checkpoints across the valley. This intensified security aims to maintain peace and prevent further unlawful activities.

stories.title: India crosses 20k organ transplants/yr for 1st time
stories.summary: India performed a record 20,138 organ transplants in 2025, a significant increase over previous years. Delhi-NCR led the nation in transplant procedures, while Tamil Nadu topped deceased organ donors. India now ranks third globally in total organ transplants, after the US and China. Deceased donor transplants continue to fall short of the substantial demand for organs. Government initiatives aim to strengthen organ donation and transplant services across the country.

stories.title: Withdraw cases, allow youngsters to continue studies: SC to states
stories.summary: The Supreme Court permitted governments to withdraw cases against student protesters. This move aims to allow students to pursue their studies without prosecution fears. However, cases against individuals with criminal records will not be dropped. The court will also establish guidelines for the use of graded force by police. Discussions on modalities for dropping cases against genuine students are ongoing.

stories.title: Census phase 2 to begin Aug 17, will capture caste, parents’ birth details
stories.summary: The Census 2027 population enumeration phase begins August 17 in snow-bound northern areas. This phase will capture caste details for the first time since 1931. Parents' date and birthplace will also be recorded as declared by respondents. Passport and Aadhaar numbers may be collected voluntarily during the exercise. The questionnaire for this significant census phase will be notified soon.

stories.title: 60 venomous snakes, cocaine, guns and 22,000 dollars in cash seized during New Mexico drug raid
stories.summary: Federal agents investigating an alleged cocaine trafficking operation in New Mexico made a shocking discovery after uncovering 60 snakes, half a pound of cocaine, three firearms and 22,000 dollars in cash during a raid on a home in the South Valley area near Albuquerque. The seizure inventory included cobras, mambas, pit vipers and pythons, along with an inland taipan, widely regarded as one of the world's most venomous snakes.

stories.title: Opposition toughens stand, washout of session likely
stories.summary: Parliament's monsoon session faces potential washout amid opposition demands. Opposition insists on discussing Ram temple donations and police actions. Union ministers criticize opposition for boycotting legislative proceedings. Bills were passed without debate due to the ongoing parliamentary standoff. The government has not yet assured discussions on the opposition's key demands.

stories.title: UPS has attracted just 4% of NPS
stories.summary: The Unified Pension Scheme for central government employees has seen low adoption rates. Only a small percentage of National Pension Trust

stories.title: Meta CEO Zuckerberg must apologise: Parliamentary Panel
SC: How can transgender ID cards be rendered invalid?
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has sought the government's response regarding the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act. Concerns were raised that the new law might erase existing benefits for transgender individuals. Senior advocates reported that hormone treatment is being denied due to fear of prosecution. They also alleged the discontinuation of the national portal for transgenders. The court questioned the retrospective invalidation of previously issued transgender identity cards.

stories.title: ARAI's study on E20 fuel impact may be made public
stories.summary: Government agencies are considering releasing the ARAI study on E20 fuel's impact. This report, submitted in June 2024, studied E10-compatible vehicles. Fuel consumption increased slightly for two-wheelers and cars in the study. Mass emissions met regulatory requirements for all vehicles tested. The release aims to remove misconceptions among vehicle users about E20 fuel.

stories.title: After success of students protest, Kisan Morcha plans to hit streets
Quote of the day by Paulo Coelho: 'If you're brave enough to say goodbye, life will reward you with a new hello'
Man reunited with lost wedding ring after 10 years as 9-year-old niece finds it in Minnesota lake
stories.summary: A Minnesota man has been reunited with his wedding ring nearly a decade after losing it at the bottom of a lake, thanks to an unexpected discovery by his 9-year-old niece during a family vacation. Stephen Meyer lost his wedding ring in 2016 while swimming with his son in Lake Belle Taine, where his family owns a cabin.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Marco Rubio: 'God has blessed me in many ways but none more important than my wife Jeanette'
'Flavouring neutral alcohol isn't right in spirit'
stories.summary: The FSSAI has prohibited adding rum or whisky flavour to spirits. This practice misrepresents the true nature of alcoholic beverages and misleads consumers. Manufacturers were found using neutral alcohol and adding identical flavouring substances. Several companies, including United Spirits, faced prohibitions and notices. The regulator stressed that characteristic taste should develop naturally through base ingredients.

stories.title: SC expands ambit of Sec 498A to cover cruelty in live-ins too
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has extended legal protection to live-in relationships. These relationships are now covered under Section 498A of the IPC. The court stated that the law must adapt to changing societal norms. Cruelty within such relationships will now be punishable by law. This decision aims to protect women from domestic violence and harassment.

stories.title: Quote by Ludwig Wittgenstein: 'The real question of life after death isn't whether or not it exists...'
stories.summary: Philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein challenged the preoccupation with life after death, suggesting that eternal existence does not address the fundamental questions of life’s meaning. His reflections emerged amidst the chaos of World War One. In contemporary discussions on digital immortality, this crucial insight often gets overshadowed; authentic meaning resides in fully embracing the present and living with intention.

stories.title: Quote of the day by JS Mill: 'I have learned to seek my happiness by limiting my desires...'
stories.summary: Victorian philosopher John Stuart Mill believed that true happiness lies in limiting our desires rather than endlessly pursuing them. After facing a mental crisis due to his upbringing, Mill shifted his philosophy, warning that unending desire leads to a hedonic treadmill. Today, our consumer-driven culture reflects this endless chase; by curbing material wishes, we can unlock a wealth of inner fulfillment and deeper contentment.

stories.title: Man rejects Rs 2 crore offer in India and chooses $160K in the US because...
Colombia intercepted a boat near the Malpelo sanctuary carrying 1,764 pounds of marine animals
stories.summary: Colombian authorities have intercepted a fishing vessel carrying approximately 1,764 pounds of suspected illegally caught marine animals believed to have been taken from the protected Malpelo Fauna and Flora Sanctuary, bringing renewed attention to illegal fishing in one of the country's most ecologically important marine reserves.

stories.title: In 1974, Spain imported two tons of American red crayfish for aquaculture; 50 years later...
stories.summary: Fifty years ago, American red crayfish were introduced to Spain's Guadalquivir River basin, and they have since established a permanent presence. These aggressive invaders have wreaked havoc on local wildlife and disrupted aquatic ecosystems. Yet, local communities have successfully built an economy around their harvesting and processing. This dependence has sparked legal disputes, resulting in a compromise that permits regulated harvesting, balancing ecological health with economic viability.

stories.title: In 2022, France promised 1 billion trees within a decade; four years later, a court...
stories.summary: France's top court invalidated a tree-planting funding decree due to procedural flaws. Ministers failed to consult the public on forestry subsidies impacting biodiversity. This ruling halts financial support for planting one billion trees over ten years. The government must now create a new legal framework with public input. Future funding will focus on restoring damaged forests and promoting diverse tree species.

stories.title: FSSAI suspends water firm's licence, bans sale of dietary supplement
US moves closer to deep-sea mining near American Samoa with 31.5 million acre lease plan
stories.summary: The United States has moved a step closer to deep-sea mining after the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) proposed auctioning two massive seabed lease areas near American Samoa for mineral exploration. The proposal marks a significant milestone in the country's efforts to secure critical mineral supplies for clean energy, electronics and national security.

stories.title: Family gets $350K after otter attack drags toddler underwater
Scottish proverb of the day: "The father buys, the son builds, the grandchild sells and his son..."
Iraqi surgeon grows nose on patient's forehead in rare reconstruction surgery to correct facial damage in high-voltage electrical accident
Of 39 medals won by India at CWG, military personnel bag 18 — nearly 50%
stories.summary: Indian Army athletes secured sixteen medals at the recent Commonwealth Games. These included eight gold, seven silver, and one bronze medal. Two Indian Navy personnel also contributed silver medals in weightlifting. Combined, services personnel achieved forty-six percent of India's total medal haul. Their performance highlights the Army's commitment to nurturing world-class athletes.

stories.title: 'Had no time to flee': Drone strikes Russian Black Sea beach, kills 7 including 3 children, injures 40
'Gen Z protest' may have aided Bankipur win: Prashant Kishor after BJP bastion falls
Military-civil integration key to robust def ecosystem to tackle challenges: Rajnath
Bankipur bypoll: BJP chief Nitin Nabin vows introspection after Kishor ends party's 30-yr hold
Bankipur assembly bypoll: 'Nitish Kumar', 'Lalu Prasad Yadav' lose security deposits
Quote of the day by Serena Williams: "I really think a champion is defined not by their wins, but by…"
stories.summary: Serena Williams believes champions are defined by their recovery after falling. True character emerges during moments of defeat, not just victory. Setbacks are an unavoidable part of any genuine journey toward growth. Resilience allows individuals to adapt and try again after disappointment. This powerful message extends beyond sports to all life's challenges.

stories.title: Robbery attempt at Indian men waiting in parking lot after 11 pm, multi-city chase by police in Texas
Indians trafficked to cybercrime hubs in Golden Triangle tortured with electric shock
Man climbs Brooklyn Bridge, strips naked, plants flags, jumps into East River; survives, identified
stories.summary: A 44-year-old man miraculously survived after jumping from the top of New York City's Brooklyn Bridge on Sunday, authorities said. According to the latest update, the man has been identified as Galymzhan Abaildayev, a Brooklyn resident, who now faces multiple charges following the dramatic incident. Videos of the incident show shocked onlookers screaming as the man jumped from the bridge.

stories.title: India gets 101st 'Ramsar' site as Arunachal Pradesh's Glaw Lake joins elite global list of protected wetlands
Chennai entrepreneur shares how he started business with ₹90,000 after quitting ₹1 crore US job
SKM announces farmers' protests at 100 locations, including Delhi, from November 26
NDA states acted firmly against recruitment scams; opposition failed to curb irregularities: CM Dhami
stories.summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday said that NDA-ruled states have taken firm action against recruitment scams and examination-related irregularities, while alleging that opposition-ruled states failed to curb such malpractices and were marked by widespread irregularities in recruitment processes.

stories.title: World’s third-smallest country Nauru renamed Naoero, code shifts to NRO
TRAI revamps 'TRAI MyCall' mobile app to assess voice call quality
Kevin Smith paid £5 after dropping off his son and another £5 when collecting him
stories.summary: Kevin Smith initially paid ten pounds for two airport drop-offs but was unexpectedly hit with two parking fines totaling two hundred pounds. These fines were charged for completing the payment within the drop-off zone. stories.title: In 1925, the world’s first motel opened in California with rooms for $1.25; after closing in 1991...
stories.summary: The iconic site of the world's first motel in San Luis Obispo is now on the market. With various redevelopment options available, buyers are encouraged to re-envision this historic property. Established in 1925 and ceasing operations in 1991, this site presents a unique opportunity to either preserve or transform a piece of hospitality history amidst the recent trend of revitalizing classic motels into boutique experiences.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Barack Obama: "Change will not come if we wait for some other person or some other time. We are the ones..."
'Threw slipper, carried a knife': What we know about attack on Pappu Yadav
Assam floods: 82 dead, 1.78 lakh affected as relief efforts intensify - key points
College students in US are choosing to live in retirement communities for affordable housing
stories.summary: College students in the US are moving into retirement communities, paying lower rent in exchange for volunteering with older residents. Supporters say the arrangement helps students find affordable housing while reducing loneliness for both generations and building meaningful relationships.

stories.title: Virginia students save family from lake during golf tryouts
stories.summary: Three Culpeper teenagers are heroes after rescuing a family whose kayaks overturned. They heard a splash and a child screaming, then immediately acted. The teens swam to the struggling family and brought them safely back to shore. Police and school officials praised their quick thinking and courage. Their actions highlight the importance of immediate response in water emergencies.

stories.title: You can make yourselves ‘luckier’: Science-backed tips to rewire your brain for luck
stories.summary: Cultivating a belief in your own luck can reshape your brain to recognize new opportunities. By documenting moments of serendipity, you start to see that luck is more frequent than originally believed. Individuals branded as unlucky often experience heightened anxiety, which narrows their perspective. In contrast, self-proclaimed lucky individuals expect good things and interact more openly. Ultimately, creating your own luck demands conscious choices and more frequent attempts.

stories.title: Bordeaux vineyards escaped the immediate wildfires, but repeated heatwaves are shrinking...
stories.summary: European vineyards face an early harvest due to prolonged heat and drought conditions. Wildfires across southwestern France and Greece have forced thousands to evacuate their homes. Emergency services continue to battle numerous blazes, particularly in Greece and on Crete. Spain sees some relief as national emergency declarations are lifted in certain areas. Record continent-wide warmth exacerbates fire risks and impacts air quality for millions.

stories.title: 'To end discrimination against women': Taslima Nasreen calls for UCC implementation in India, Bangladesh and Pakisatn
stories.summary: Exiled author Taslima Nasreen urged India, Bangladesh, and Pakistan to adopt a Uniform Civil Code. She stated this law is essential for eliminating discrimination, particularly against women. Nasreen highlighted that Hindu women in Bangladesh lack equal inheritance rights. She also expressed disappointment over disruptions at her felicitation ceremony. The author emphasized the importance of freedom of expression for all individuals.

stories.title: ‘Ban on Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League a move against democracy’: Taslima Nasreen
Engineers linked two deep wells through 629°F rock beneath Oregon’s Newberry volcano; the experiment could unlock round-the-clock power without burning fuel
stories.summary: Mazama Energy connected two deep wells reaching 629 degrees Fahrenheit. This marks the world's hottest enhanced geothermal system ever built. The company plans three more wells in 2026 targeting hotter rock. This project aims to unlock superhot rock for cleaner energy production. Geothermal energy could become a significant player in the clean energy mix.

stories.title: Can BJP crack Punjab? Inside its strategy to challenge AAP and Congress in 2027
'Kerala stands united': Rahul Gandhi offers support as rains claim 8 lives, leave 8 missing
Teen's routine fishing trip ends with a South Dakota record that had stood since 1970
stories.summary: A routine fishing trip on South Dakota's Wall Lake turned into a record-breaking moment for teenager Jack Backman after he caught a one-pound pumpkinseed, setting a new state record. Thinking he had hooked a crappie, Backman was surprised to discover the rare catch. The fish beat a 12-ounce state record that had stood since 1970.

stories.title: 'Double standards': Pakistan rejects UN report on civilian casualties in Afghanistan strikes
Quote of the day by LeBron James: "I think the reason why I'm the person who I am today is because…" - an inspiring lesson on resilience, adversity and the power of difficult beginnings
stories.summary: LeBron James credits his difficult childhood for shaping his current character and perspective. He views past hardships as the essential foundation for his achievements. These challenging experiences fostered patience, gratitude, and determination within him. His journey demonstrates that starting circumstances do not permanently define one's future. Real success often carries a responsibility to help others facing similar struggles.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Indonesia ferry fire kills 5, rescue teams recover Nirmal Purja's body & more
'If India is so great, why settle in Dubai?' Raj Thackeray targets Vivek Oberoi, R Madhavan
Students from around the world experience the Jain way of life in Rajasthan
'Ready to face death': Pappu Yadav defiant after FIR over Ram Temple donation 'theft' skit
stories.summary: Pappu Yadav remains defiant after police filed a case against him and other opposition leaders. The FIR stems from a Parliament skit which depicted alleged theft of Ram Temple donations. Yadav stated he is ready to face death to protect people's faith and religious sentiments. Varanasi Police registered the case following a complaint by a religious leader. Another complaint was filed against the MP in the national capital.

stories.title: California vineyards used owl boxes to attract barn owls, reducing rodent numbers by up to 52%
stories.summary: A new study from California has found that barn owls help vineyards control rodents naturally by both hunting them and making them more cautious. Researchers observed up to 52% fewer rodents in vineyards with more owls. The findings suggest that encouraging barn owls through nest boxes could reduce the need for pesticides while supporting biodiversity and sustainable farming.

stories.title: 'That hurts us': CWG silver medalist Lovlina flags 'missing' Northeast on Glasgow restaurant's India map
The towel on the chair: How it became India's ultimate status symbol
158 exam irregularity cases await trial; CBI seeks fast-track disposal under new anti-paper leak law
stories.summary: Over 150 recruitment exam irregularity cases await trial, some dating back two decades. The CBI will ask high courts to move these pending matters to new fast-track courts. Dedicated prosecutors and resources will be provided to expedite the conclusion of these trials. The new anti-paper leak law mandates day-to-day hearings and trials within three months. This initiative follows recent student protests and calls for examination system reforms.

stories.title: 'Mekedatu project is permanent solution': Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar on Cauvery water dispute with Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar views the Mekedatu dam project as a permanent solution. He stated the Supreme Court and central government have already responded to the proposal. Shivakumar urged all stakeholders to move forward without further delays or wasting time. This project aims to bring both states to the table for amicable discussions. The Cauvery water dispute centers on sharing river waters during periods of low rainfall.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Selena Gomez: You have to be uncomfortable sometimes in order to move forward
stories.summary: Selena Gomez, the renowned pop artist, champions the idea that navigating discomfort can be crucial for personal evolution. Transitioning from her Disney roots, she successfully emerged as a singer, actress, and entrepreneur. With transparency about her mental health battles, Gomez inspires others to seek professional support. Through her Rare Beauty brand, she also promotes mental wellness initiatives worldwide, illustrating that challenges often pave the way for growth.

stories.title: King Charles, Prince William pay tribute to ex-British soldier Nirmal Purja killed in Pakistan avalanche
5 dead, 41 missing after ferry catches fire off Indonesia's Madura Island
'He will not be taken back': Mayawati expels former MP Ashok Siddharth from BSP again
stories.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party president Mayawati expelled former Rajya Sabha member Ashok Siddarth from the party. Siddarth faced expulsion for indiscipline and violating party directives in several states. The party chief also announced the expulsion of coordinator Randhir Singh Beniwal for similar reasons. Mayawati clarified that senior Uttar Pradesh office-bearers would not hold state roles. Ramji Gautam will continue as Punjab in-charge until upcoming assembly and Lok Sabha polls.

stories.title: 150-year-overdue library book returned in Australia; racks up Rs 16 lakh 'late fee'
stories.summary: A library received a book returned after 150 years overdue. The calculated late fee reached approximately twenty-eight thousand Australian dollars. This rare book was discovered during home renovations and was damaged. It was borrowed by a local resident's great-great-grandfather in the 1870s. The book will now join the library's local history collection.

stories.title: 'Police powers misused': Prashant Kishor alleges voter intimidation, files complaint over Bankipur bypoll
'Still a student, learning every day': Rahul Gandhi's Gen Z-style Friendship Day wish
Indian diaspora in China flags anti-India social media posts, visa curbs at 1st embassy outreach
stories.summary: Indian diaspora members voiced concerns over anti-India content and visa issues. Ambassador Vikram Doraiswami assured actions were being taken to address these matters. Visa requirements for Chinese citizens traveling to India will be eased soon. The embassy plans to establish a legal assistance framework for professionals. Cultural outreach programs will also be expanded to promote Indian diversity.

stories.title: 'Govt forgets when donations are stolen': Congress defends Rahul Gandhi after Ram Mandir skit FIR
How being poor damages your brain, new study finds
stories.summary: Long-term financial strain can significantly speed up the aging of the brain. Research highlights that persistent monetary worries contribute to cognitive decline, particularly noticeable by the age of fifty-three. Brain scans portray more severe shrinkage in individuals facing such hardships, with men from lower socioeconomic backgrounds suffering even harsher effects. Providing support for those in financial distress could play a vital role in preserving cognitive health in the future.

stories.title: Delhi HC transfers special judge assigned to paper leak cases a week after taking charge
'Drugs part of enemy nations' terror plan to hurt India': PM Modi during 'Nasha Mukt Yuva' launch - top quotes
Study warns Northern Hemisphere lakes could lose around 40 days of winter ice by 2100
stories.summary: A new international study has found that lake ice across the Northern Hemisphere could shrink by about 40 days by the end of this century if emissions remain high. Researchers identified critical winter temperature thresholds beyond which ice loss accelerates sharply, raising concerns over water quality, freshwater ecosystems and communities that depend on stable winter ice.

stories.title: 100-million-year-old ichthyosaur's last meal found; bite marks implicate giant Kronosaurus
stories.summary: A remarkable ichthyosaur fossil, hailing from 100 million years ago, has provided a glimpse into its final feast, which included fish, cephalopods, and even a pterosaur. Using sophisticated scanning methods, scientists could identify these stomach contents non-invasively. Notably, the fossil bears evidence of severe bite marks, implicating the Kronosaurus queenslandicus as the likely predator, illuminating aspects of Australia’s ancient marine food web.

stories.title: How an escaped aquarium plant unleashed California's killer algae in 2000
'Let Cauvery unite our people': Karnataka BJP chief calls on Tamil Nadu CM Vijay to bridge 'differences'
'Dismantle terror infrastructure first': India's US envoy hits out at Pakistan over Indus Waters Treaty
Culture can slow ageing, says study
Global breastfeeding rates rise, India yet to arrest decline
Japan earthquake aftermath: Woman dies of heat stroke in parked car; toll rises to 36
stories.summary: An elderly woman died from heat stroke while sheltering in her car after a massive earthquake. Authorities are warning of growing heat-related risks for evacuees amid sweltering temperatures. Thousands remain displaced, with many sleeping in cars or outside their homes for privacy. Temperatures are climbing, raising fears of further heat-related illnesses among survivors. The government is rushing essential supplies to evacuation centers to improve living conditions.

stories.title: Washington wildfires scorch over 2,50,000 acres of land; trigger mass evacuations
stories.summary: Thousands of firefighters battled multiple wildfires across Washington state on Saturday. Governor Bob Ferguson declared a statewide emergency and imposed a burn ban. The fast-moving Old Trails Fire in Spokane threatened thousands of structures and forced evacuations. Power utility Avista implemented safety shutoffs, leaving many customers without electricity. Officials confirmed some structures were destroyed as the extent of damage was assessed.

stories.title: 'Rs 18cr stolen every year': Raj Thackeray alleges Siddhivinayak temple donation scam
3 killed in US Idaho shopping area shooting; gunman among dead
stories.summary: Three people died and two were injured after a gunman opened fire. The shooter was also among the deceased, with authorities investigating the motive. The chaotic scene unfolded near a busy In-N-Out Burger restaurant on Saturday afternoon. Witnesses described seeing an armed individual and people fleeing the area in fear. Law enforcement confirmed the threat to the community was over after the incident.

stories.title: Long hours hurting resident docs’ mental health, NMC tells SC
stories.summary: Resident doctors face significant psychological distress from long working hours. The National Medical Commission acknowledged these demanding schedules impact their health. The commission stated reasonable working hours are essential for doctor and patient wellbeing. However, NMC expressed inability to enforce this, citing health authorities' domain. A doctors' group highlighted rising suicide cases due to these conditions.

stories.title: Railway Board panels suggest premature retirement of 5 officers
stories.summary: Railway Board committees recommended premature retirement for five Group A officers. This action targets corruption, lack of integrity, and inefficiency within the service. Two senior administrative grade officers and three junior administrative grade officers were affected. These decisions were made under the Indian Railway Establishment Code provisions. Previously, thirty-two officers were retired in 2022 for similar reasons.

stories.title: CBI files EPFO cheating case against Anil Ambani
stories.summary: The CBI has filed a cheating case against Reliance Capital and Anil Ambani. This action stems from an alleged Rs 1,816 crore loss to the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation. EPFO invested Rs 2,500 crore in Reliance Capital’s debentures which later defaulted. While the issue was settled earlier, ED findings prompted a new fraud case. Anil Ambani denies any wrongdoing in this matter.

stories.title: E20: AAP plans pro-choice rally to PM residence
stories.summary: Arvind Kejriwal announced a march to the Prime Minister's residence on Tuesday. He demanded consumers have a choice between pure petrol and E20 fuel. Kejriwal also called for E20 fuel to be priced lower than pure petrol. He challenged the government to release scientific studies supporting the E20 fuel policy. The AAP leader advised consumers to consider electric vehicles for future transportation needs.

stories.title: Monsoon hope as WMO sees an El Niño counter
stories.summary: India faces a risk of below-normal monsoon rainfall due to El Niño. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole may offer some relief to the country. This oceanic pattern could improve rainfall conditions in southern India. It might prevent the monsoon from slipping into a deficient phase. International forecasts suggest a positive IOD could develop soon.

stories.title: Judge Ujjal Bhuyan questions SC collegium’s opacity
stories.summary: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan questioned the Supreme Court collegium's lack of transparency in judicial appointments. He noted that recent collegium resolutions provided no reasons for their decisions. This opacity, he argued, could allow unsuitable individuals to enter the judiciary. Citizens possess a right to know deliberations concerning judicial elevations and transfers. The JALDI report highlights varying transparency levels across India's higher courts.

stories.title: July GST collections up 15.4% to Rs 2.1 L cr on higher imports
stories.summary: Goods and Services Tax collections rose 15.4 percent to Rs 2,11,205 crore in July. This increase was largely due to a 29 percent jump in integrated GST on imports. Strong economic activity and higher commodity prices also contributed to the robust tax collections. Central GST mop-up increased 12.3 percent while state GST grew 8.7 percent. Net collections after refunds went up 15.8 percent, reflecting continued economic resilience.

stories.title: Government approves 2 tunnels for Valley-Jammu connectivity
Indian-origin mayor of US city asks ICE to 'go home', says he will always support the immigrant community
India-China border trade resumes after 6 years
stories.summary: India and China have reopened two key Himalayan trade routes after six years. Traditional border trade resumed Saturday through Lipulekh and Shipki La passes. Chinese authorities restricted the initial batch of traders to twenty people. Indian traders can export 36 categories of goods, while Chinese traders bring twenty. A new trade mart was also inaugurated near the international border.

stories.title: NEET-PG aspirants to face Aadhaar, iris authentication
Twitch streamer ExtraEmily gets her own Hulu and Disney+ series as Creator Essentials brings her Twitch content to TV
stories.summary: Twitch streamer ExtraEmily is launching her own television series titled Creator Essentials. This new show features fifteen episodes, each approximately twenty-two minutes long. The series is designed for teenagers and highlights her personality and gaming adventures. This move expands her reach beyond Twitch to major streaming services. It signifies a growing trend of online creators transitioning to television.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Sigmund Freud: 'The more perfect a person is on the outside, the more demons they have on the inside' and why absolute perfection is a facade
Quote of the day by Mohammed bin Salman: 'I fear that the day I die, I am going to die without accomplishing what I have in my mind'
Twitch streamer SmaK reveals Twitch apologized after sudden 30-day ban over joke as creators criticize the platform’s automated ban system
stories.summary: Twitch streamer SmaK received a thirty-day ban after making a joke during a livestream. He was joking about needing to go away while reacting to chat messages. Twitch later removed the ban and apologized for the mistaken suspension. This incident highlights issues with automated moderation systems and context. SmaK has since returned to streaming after the platform corrected its error.

stories.title: Florida evangelist who says passengers have no choice but to listen to her sermons removed from flight; Alaska Airlines puts her on no-fly list
Cloudburst damages structures in Kishtwar; rain halts Amarnath Yatra
stories.summary: Flash floods in Kishtwar's Chatroo area damaged shops and houses early Saturday. Vehicles were washed away, and the national highway sustained damage from debris. The Amarnath Yatra was suspended from Jammu due to incessant rain. Schools remained closed in several districts as a precautionary measure. Affected shopkeepers and business owners will receive government compensation.

stories.title: Fear stalks Kashmir’s brick kilns after terrorists kill 2 migrant workers
stories.summary: Two migrant labourers were killed Friday evening in Kulgam, causing panic among workers. Brick kilns across south Kashmir halted operations as labourers stayed indoors. Many workers expressed concerns about their safety and earning a living. Security forces visited the kilns and assured the labourers of protection. Officials directed authorities to ensure the safety of all migrant workers.

stories.title: NYC Mayor Mamdani snubbed at funeral of soldier killed in Iranian missile strike: Report
Green Card updates for August: EB-1 may become unavailable for Indians
'Prepare to depart': US embassies issue alert across Middle East amid Iran tensions
stories.summary: US embassies in Middle East urged citizens to depart due to potential conflict escalation. The security alerts warned of unpredictable Iranian actions and possible attacks on US interests. President Trump threatened Iran with severe military action following alleged truce violations. Iran warned countries supporting the US against facing war's flames. Regional shipping and travel face disruptions amid ongoing hostilities and heightened tensions.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia arrests over 14,000 in week-long crackdown on residency, labour violations
NEET-PG 2026 gets major overhaul: Centres closer to home, single-shift exam, fewer questions with no change in test duration
stories.summary: NEET-PG exam sees significant changes for candidate convenience and enhanced security. Candidates now select three preferred states for their examination centre locations. The exam duration remains the same, but questions reduce to 180 for more time. Aadhaar and iris biometrics strengthen registration and exam day security measures. NEET-PG 2026 will be conducted in a single shift for uniform assessment.

stories.title: 'Girls' clothes torn, heads broken': CJP founder demands PM Modi apology over police action on July 20th
Army's intelligence units, Rajasthan police bust counterfeit combat uniform racket in Sriganganagar
stories.summary: Indian Army intelligence and Rajasthan police seized nearly 1,000 meters of unauthorized combat cloth. This action followed a lead pointing to a local firm supplying counterfeit army-pattern fabric. The coordinated operation on July 30 uncovered a wider network distributing fake military uniforms. Similar counterfeit cloth was previously seized in Bareilly, traced to Sriganganagar. Unauthorized sale of military camouflage cloth is restricted and banned in many sensitive regions.

stories.title: 'You should've apologized': Congress targets PM Modi over his 'forgive you' remark in Insta video
stories.summary: In a bold move, Congress leader Supriya Shrinate has taken aim at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, demanding he apologize for the alleged brutal treatment of students during recent protests. She accused the government of cruelty and called for accountability, urging the Prime Minister to step into Parliament and address the issue directly, particularly after his comments about supporting the youth.

stories.title: 13-year-old Oregon student designs a chamber that turns moisture in the air into water for drought-hit farms
stories.summary: In a remarkable feat of ingenuity, a young student has created technology that converts air moisture into potable water. This device stands as a sustainable beacon for farmers struggling with inadequate water supply. Featuring a Peltier module for condensation, it smartly monitors water delivery and environmental factors through advanced sensors. Roy Kim aspires for his invention to play a significant role in alleviating the global water challenges faced by agriculture.

stories.title: Mushroom hunters find rare snake nest in Nepal forest, officials restrict access
Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos' ex-wife MacKenzie Scott: “There are lots of resources each of us can pull from our safes to share with others…”
‘My return to Kolkata proves injustice cannot be permanent’: Taslima Nasreen
stories.summary: Exiled author Taslima Nasreen returned to Kolkata after nineteen years of absence. She stated her return proves injustice is not permanent and spoke for women's rights. Nasreen expressed concern over rising religious extremism in Bangladesh and curtailed freedom of speech. She lamented not finding a permanent home in the Bengals, though Europe offered security. The writer emphasized her advocacy for equality and human rights, not offense.

stories.title: Wife not entitled to interim maintenance if adultery allegation is prima facie true: SC
Trump rejects Iran link in Minnesota cyberattacks, blames Governor Tim Walz instead
Savannah Guthrie begs public after mother's disappearance; ransom note said 'buried in nature'
DMK moves SC seeking immediate release of Cauvery water from Karnataka to Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: The DMK has petitioned the Supreme Court for immediate Cauvery water release from Karnataka. Karnataka's government faces a directive to release 3,500 cusecs daily for fifteen days. The plea also seeks to clear an accumulated water release shortfall of 9.46 TMC. Karnataka's Chief Minister urged protesters to withdraw their agitation against water releases. The state government will protect farmers' interests while respecting judicial orders.

stories.title: ‘Egg-therapy could turn on its head’: Bengal BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya cautions party workers
stories.summary: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya cautioned party workers against arrogance and complacency. He warned that the "egg therapy" could turn against them if they become overconfident. Bhattacharya acknowledged that extortion culture has not been fully eradicated since the government took power. He emphasized the need to free the business ecosystem from partisan politics. The party is making earnest efforts to build a government for West Bengal.

stories.title: 'Returned to the US 3 days before visa expiry': Indian H-1B holder shares what happened next
CBI books Anil Ambani, Reliance Capital in Rs 1,816 crore EPFO fraud case
West Bengal to clear all pending CAA applications within six months, says Suvendu Adhikari
stories.summary: West Bengal's Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari pledged to resolve all pending CAA applications soon. He stated the law grants citizenship and is not meant to revoke it. Nearly twenty-four thousand citizenship certificates have already been issued to eligible refugees. The government will delegate powers to district magistrates for faster application processing. This initiative aims to provide citizenship to persecuted minorities from neighboring countries.

stories.title: UK finance minister John Healey to present first Budget on October 28
2,000-pound US bomb hits Iran family home; Centcom says 'we never target civilians'
India’s students do not need PM Modi's forgiveness, they are owed his apology: Rahul Gandhi
Ladakh Police file zero FIR against influencer over alleged anti-Amit Shah Facebook video
'Days of threat culture over': Bengal CM assures security to Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen
'Disappointed with PM Modi': Shehzad Poonawalla’s sarcastic 'dictator' jibe at oppn after quitting BJP
stories.summary: Taking a jibe at PM Modi's critics, Shehzad Poonawalla expressed "disappointment" with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership style. He sarcastically suggested Modi learn dictatorship from past Congress leaders. Poonawalla cited Indira Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru as examples of strong rule. He also mentioned past Congress governments' actions during protests. The former spokesperson concluded Modi had not met Left-liberal expectations.

stories.title: Major row over airport detention of Johns Hopkins health researcher Fatima Ameaka; Colleagues say she is brilliant but DHS says she is an 'illegal'
Spain races to secure Ceuta border with floating barrier after mass crossings and 67 deaths
PM Modi inaugurates Swami Vivekananda Cultural Youth Centre in Mysuru
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Viveka Smaraka youth centre in Mysuru. This centre aims to inspire young Indians with nation-building and service ideals. The Prime Minister highlighted youth strength driving India's economic growth and development. He also emphasized education in mother tongue and promoting local products. The new facility will nurture youth dedicated to national service and societal welfare.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja dies in avalanche; India's medal rush continues in CWG 2026 & more
stories.summary: Mountaineer Nirmal Purja died in a Broad Peak avalanche, ending his legendary career. India secured more medals at the Commonwealth Games 2026, reaching a total of thirty. Rahul Gandhi demanded an apology from Prime Minister Modi for NEET students. A stricter anti-paper leak law has now come into force nationwide. Complaints were filed against Rahul Gandhi and Pappu Yadav regarding a protest.

stories.title: ‘How did Hockey India executive board not know?’ Congress questions govt over saffron jersey row
stories.summary: Congress leader Mallikarjun Kharge questioned the government regarding the hockey jersey color change. He stated the decision was made without Hockey India Executive Board approval. The traditional blue jersey identity is deeply connected to Indian sports traditions. Hockey India defended the design, citing consultations with players and staff. However, the president claimed no prior knowledge of the implemented decision.

stories.title: Innocent Canadian man spent 18 months in prison after police missed underscore in username
Nathula pass border trade resumes after 6 years; traders seek expansion of goods list
'Defeat delimitation': In Tamil Nadu, Rahul Gandhi's appeal to parties with 'Ettappan' warning
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi labeled the proposed delimitation exercise a BJP conspiracy. He stated it aims to disenfranchise people and reduce Tamil Nadu's political power. Supporting delimitation makes one a 21st-century Ettappan, a Tamil term for traitor. He urged all Tamil people and parties to oppose this proposal. National parties were also asked to defeat the delimitation in the House.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Martin Luther King Jr.: "Darkness cannot drive out darkness; only light can do that. Hate cannot drive out hate; only ..."
Antarctica's Concordia Station hit minus 119.4°F, its coldest temperature in 16 years
stories.summary: Antarctica's Concordia Research Station recorded its coldest temperature in sixteen years on July eighteenth. This extreme cold was caused by polar winter and high elevation conditions. The station sits atop the East Antarctic Plateau, far from ocean influences. Meteorologists attribute the deep freeze to a persistent high-pressure system. Such measurements offer valuable insights into Earth's climate system.

stories.title: Clavicular US college tour: Everything to know about the Kick streamer’s US livestream event
stories.summary: Clavicular is set to begin his US College Tour on August 2, 2026, where he plans to livestream visits to colleges and fraternities across America. His announcement has received mixed reactions online, while many fans also remember his viral Arizona State University selfie that became a popular internet meme earlier this year.

stories.title: Air India expands Canada network with new Mumbai-Toronto flights, upgrades Delhi route
'Not met a single parent or student': Rahul Gandhi slams PM Modi over 'forgiving' students video
How 832 solar panels help one farm produce food, energy and extra income
Explained: What changes after India's tougher anti-paper leak law comes into force
stories.summary: A new anti-paper leak law is now in effect across India. Investigations into exam fraud must now conclude within two months. Trials will be expedited through fast-track courts, aiming for quicker resolutions. Individuals face up to ten years imprisonment and significant fines for paper leaks. Organized rackets will receive even harsher penalties, deterring future examination malpractices.

stories.title: Students don’t need PM Modi’s forgiveness; they deserve his apology: Rahul Gandhi
stories.summary: He criticised the Prime Minister for not meeting a single grieving parent or a student whose future was stolen by a leaked question paper. He said the Centre had failed to acknowledge the suffering of students and their families.

stories.title: ‘Act of aggression against Iran’: Araghchi warns UK over US access to British military bases
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister warned Britain that allowing US strikes from its bases is aggression. He stated this action grants Iran the right to self-defense under international law. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham approved continued US military base access for operations. Burnham also reaffirmed UK commitment to maritime security efforts in the Strait of Hormuz. London maintains it is not part of any war with Iran and supports diplomacy.

stories.title: Rose Metcalf helped guide 400 people off the sinking Costa Concordia, signalled rescuers with her earring
stories.summary: In a dramatic turn of events aboard the Costa Concordia, Rose Metcalf, a dancer, played a pivotal role in the life-saving efforts. She rallied crew members to create a human chain, ensuring safe evacuation amidst panic. Innovatively, Metcalf descended the ship's side to reach the water's edge and signaled a rescue helicopter with a makeshift light. Her courage and resourcefulness were instrumental in saving lives during that dire night.

stories.title: 'Honey trap' angle emerges in Bengal Jaish probe; woman arrested from Jharkhand
‘Sentiments hurt’: Seers, lawyers file police complaints against Pappu Yadav, Rahul Gandhi over Ram Temple skit
stories.summary: Seers and lawyers filed police complaints in Varanasi against Pappu Yadav and opposition leaders. They alleged their religious sentiments were hurt by a protest enacted in Parliament. The opposition leaders staged a symbolic protest over alleged Ram Temple donation embezzlement. This protest occurred after allegations of financial irregularities surfaced regarding temple donations. Legal action has been sought against the opposition leaders involved in the demonstration.

stories.title: Ram Temple skit row: Rahul Gandhi, Pappu Yadav, Awadhesh Prasad booked for 'insulting Sanatan Dharma'
stories.summary: Seers and lawyers filed police complaints in Varanasi against Pappu Yadav and opposition leaders. They alleged their religious sentiments were hurt by a protest enacted in Parliament. The opposition leaders staged a symbolic protest over alleged Ram Temple donation embezzlement. This protest occurred after allegations of financial irregularities surfaced regarding temple donations. Legal action has been sought against the opposition leaders involved in the demonstration.

stories.title: Kale Island lost to rising seas now lives on through a marine habitat sculpture
'Go that way': Migrants say Moroccan authorities directed them towards Spain's Ceuta
stories.summary: Moroccan illegal migrants reported encouragement from authorities and social media messages. Thousands crossed into Spain's Ceuta enclave, with many returning due to hardship. At least sixty-seven people died during the unprecedented border crossing event. Spain is reinforcing the Ceuta border after tens of thousands entered. The crisis has sparked political tensions and renewed migration policy debates.

stories.title: His grandfather paid $2,200 for an Allis-Chalmers tractor in 1953; 62 years later, Kevin Klahn bought it back and restored it
stories.summary: Kevin Klahn restored his grandfather's 1953 tractor after buying it back. This vintage Allis-Chalmers WD tractor became a symbol of family heritage. The meticulous restoration project took many hours of dedicated work. It preserved the machine's original character and historical significance. The tractor returned home, representing dedication and enduring family bonds.

stories.title: Major US Black university mandates business suits, bans certain headwear in new dress code
US makes visa bond programme permanent: Effective date, affected countries explained
'In every national security decision, Doval had a role': Amit Shah praises NSA at award ceremony
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah praised NSA Ajit Doval's significant national security contributions. Doval's strategic advice has strengthened India's defense and foreign policy since 2014. Shah highlighted Doval's instrumental role in every major national security decision made by Prime Minister Modi. The NSA's decades-long career in intelligence has been vital for India's transformation. Doval accepted the Lokmanya Tilak National Award with humility, thanking leaders.

stories.title: 'Almost as if I am a terrorist': Tehseen Poonawalla claims house arrest over E20 protest
'Terrorists asked caste, community': Family claims Kulgam victims were 'identified' before being shot
stories.summary: Two Chhattisgarh labourers were killed in a terror attack at a brick kiln in Kulgam. Attackers allegedly questioned the victims about their caste and community before opening fire on them. This incident echoes survivor accounts from a previous terror attack in Pahalgam. The victims were identified as Deepak Ratrey and Bhupendra Bhaina from Chhattisgarh. Authorities are coordinating to return the bodies and provide financial assistance to the families.

stories.title: 'Whenever we seek statehood': Farooq Abdullah questions 'timing' of Kulgam terror attack
stories.summary: Two migrant labourers were killed in a terrorist attack in Kulgam district. National Conference president Farooq Abdullah questioned the timing of this incident. He noted such attacks occur when his party demands statehood restoration. People's Democratic Party chief Mehbooba Mufti called the killings a security lapse. She requested a high-level investigation and compensation for the victims.

stories.title: 'Will march to PM's residence over E20': Kejriwal announces August 3 protest
Since 1869, 120 fish species have crossed the Suez Canal—three more may follow
14-km iceberg cut off food supply, causing 69% drop in Antarctic penguin chicks
Sunken German warship from WWII resurfaces due to low river levels in Serbia
President Murmu assents to anti-paper leak amendment Bill
Minnesota's largest coal plant is now wiring 1.7 million solar panels powering 150,000 homes
stories.summary: The largest coal plant in Minnesota is transitioning to embrace renewable energy by hosting a substantial solar farm. Leveraging the existing transmission systems of the coal facility, the Sherco Solar project is now recognized as the most extensive solar installation in the state. This forward-thinking initiative accelerates grid connection for new energy innovations, with exciting plans for future development and battery storage integration.

stories.title: NSA Ajit Doval receives Lokmanya Tilak National Award for national security contribution
stories.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah presented the award at a ceremony held on the 106th death anniversary of freedom fighter Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
